topics.title: Welcome & Introduction
topics.content:
![header: Welcome](help/images/header_welcome.jpg)

::: lead
Unleash your creativity with **Dashboard Studio**, the ultimate interface design tool for your smart home.
:::

Dashboard Studio operates more like a professional design suite than a rigid list of switches. It delivers a local, powerful canvas that puts you in complete control.

::: alert info paint-brush
**Design Freedom:**

Work in pixels with overlap and layering, or switch to [**Responsive Columns**](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns) so the same dashboard reflows from phone to wall tablet. You choose the mode once in **Dashboard Environment**.
:::

### Key Features

* **Full Dashboard Designer:** A complete built-in editor. Add widgets, bind live data, and layer controls on a canvas.
* **Three Layout Modes:** **Fixed Resolution** for pixel placement, **Scale to Fit Screen** to fill the viewport, and **Responsive Columns** for a fluid grid. See [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes).
* **Basic and Advanced Editor:** **Basic** keeps essentials and presets. **Advanced** opens every styling slideout. Switch this in **Editor Environment**. See [Editor Mode](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode).
* **Widget Presets:** Apply a built-in or Homey-saved look in one click. Save your own packs for reuse. See [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets).
* **Total Style Control:** Define a global theme for consistency, or style each widget individually. Adjust colors, fonts, glows, borders, and transparency.
* **Dynamic & Real-Time:** Animate icons, display live processes, and watch data stream instantly.

### Your Personal Mobile App

Dashboard Studio is not restricted to wall-mounted tablets. Design a phone remote, a media player, a weather station, a dense energy layout, or a browser start page.

When you already know the screen size, start with [**Fixed Resolution**](help://Layout%20Modes#help-fixed-resolution). That is the native, pixel-perfect canvas. Pick a phone or tablet **Resolution Preset**, or type the exact **Width** and **Height**. For a start page that should follow the browser from phone to desktop, use [**Responsive Columns**](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns) and follow the [Responsive Website tutorial](help://Tutorials/responsive-website-complete-guide). Group related widgets into a combined cell and set **Scale Mode** to **Rescale** so the composition stays proportional.

### Step-by-Step Tutorials

Whether you want a quick five-minute setup or a deep dive into custom interface design, choose the walkthrough that matches your project:

* **[Basic Beginners Tutorial](help://Tutorials/basic-beginners-tutorial) [badge: Homey Pro]:** The simplest, fastest way to get up and running using the automatic setup wizard and essential controls.
* **[Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide) [badge: Homey Pro]:** A comprehensive, beginner-friendly walkthrough that builds a custom dashboard from scratch with gauges, switches, flow cards, themes, and kiosk mounting.
* **[Responsive Website: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/responsive-website-complete-guide):** Learn how to design a fluid, responsive dashboard or startpage using columns, bookmarks, and RSS feeds that adapt to any screen size.

### Universal Compatibility

Because Dashboard Studio generates a standard, highly optimized webpage, it performs flawlessly on:

* iPads & Android Tablets
* Desktop Browsers
* Smartphones (iOS & Android)
* DIY Displays (e.g., Raspberry Pi with touchscreen)
* Any device that can show a modern web page

Ready to begin? Start with the [Tutorials](help://Tutorials) overview, explore the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide), or read about [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes).

topics.title: Editor Interface Guide
topics.content:
![header: Editor Interface](help/images/header_editor.jpg)

::: lead
Welcome to the **Editor Interface Guide**. This overview walks you through every button, toolbar, and settings panel in the Dashboard Studio editor so you can design your ideal dashboards with confidence.
:::

### Page Index

* [1. Editor Header](#1-editor-header)
* [2. Editor Tools](#2-editor-tools)
* [3. Viewer URL & Dashboard Files](#3-viewer-url-dashboard-files)
* [4. Theme](#4-theme)
* [5. Create Widget](#5-create-widget)
* [6. Selected Widget Tools](#6-selected-widget-tools)
* [7. Universal Actions](#7-universal-actions)
* [8. Page Navigator & Utilities](#8-page-navigator-utilities)
* [9. Platform Connection](#9-platform-connection)
* [10. Data Stream Explorer](#10-data-stream-explorer)
* [11. Editor Environment](#11-editor-environment)
* [12. Dashboard Environment](#12-dashboard-environment)
* [13. Regional & Localization](#13-regional-localization)
* [14. Theme Colors](#14-theme-colors)
* [15. Audio](#15-audio)
* [16. Typography](#16-typography)
* [17. Master Widget Settings](#17-master-widget-settings)

### 1. Editor Header

At the very top of the sidebar, the header displays your environment status and dashboard identity at a glance:

::: grid
* [button ph-tag] **App Version:** Shows the currently running Dashboard Studio release.
* [button ph-plugs-connected] **Connection Status:** Displays real-time connectivity (**Homey**, **MQTT**, **Simulation**, or **Offline**). Hover over this tag to see live latency and server details.
* [button ph-file-text] **Dashboard Name:** Indicates the open dashboard configuration file.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Active Page:** Shows the currently viewed page index (such as `P1` or `P2`).
* [button ph-floppy-disk] **Save Status:** Highlights whether changes are `Saved`, `Edited`, or in `Draft` state.
:::

### 2. Editor Tools

Quickly access utilities, galleries, and global editor controls:

::: grid
* [button ph-images-square] **[Image Gallery](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager):** Upload, view, organize, and copy image links stored on your Homey hub. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-music-notes] **[Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery):** Upload sound files, test audio playback, and copy clip paths for alerts and widgets. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-share] **Share:** Export selected widgets as portable JSON snippets to share with others, or import snippets straight from your clipboard.
* [button ph-hammer] **[Tools](help://Tools):** Open helper scripts that automate common tasks, such as the [Widget Preset Editor](help://Tools/widget-preset-editor), [Set Link Open Behavior](help://Tools/set-link-open-behavior), [Make All Dynamic Values Fixed](help://Tools/make-all-dynamic-values-fixed), or [Auto-Widget Gallery](help://Tools/auto-widget-gallery).
* [button ph-circle-half] **Theme Toggle:** Cycles the editor between **Auto**, **Light**, and **Dark**. **Auto** is the default. It follows **Color 1** of the dashboard background: a dark color uses the dark editor, and a bright color uses the light editor.
* [button ph-question] **Help:** Open this documentation panel at any time while editing. Use **Search documentation** at the top of the panel to list topics, subpages, and headings that contain the words you type. Click a row to open that section. **Back** returns to the result list.
* [button ph-sliders] **Edit Mode Zoom:** Scale the whole dashboard while you edit. The left end is **200%**, the center is **100%**, and the right end is **20%**. Enlarge a small dashboard, or fit a large one on a smaller screen. The reset button returns the zoom to **100%**. The value is saved with the dashboard. View mode shows the dashboard at its layout size.
:::

### 3. Viewer URL & Dashboard Files

Manage your dashboard configurations and access display links:

::: grid
* [button ph-arrow-square-out] **Viewer URL:** Shows the view-only URL for your dashboard. Click the link to open the view, or click the copy button to prepare bookmarks for wall tablets and [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display). Supports [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters#7-dashboard-viewer-kiosk-mode).
* [button ph-cloud-arrow-up] **Save to Homey:** Save the current dashboard configuration directly to your Homey storage. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-cloud-arrow-down] **Load from Homey:** Open previously saved dashboards or restore snapshots from automatic backups. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-download-simple] **Export Dashboard:** Download your complete dashboard as a `.json` backup file on your computer.
* [button ph-folder-open] **Import Dashboard:** Load an existing dashboard `.json` file from your computer.
* [button ph-trash] **Reset Canvas:** Launch the dashboard setup wizard to clear the canvas and pick editor mode, layout mode, screen size, theme, and optional live widgets. On **Choose Your Layout Mode**, pick a resolution. The default is **iPad Air 10.9" Landscape**. **Fixed Resolution** also offers **Unlimited** and **Custom**. **Scale to Fit Screen** keeps a real width and height. **Responsive Columns** uses **Max Width**. If no device topics are coming in yet, enable a few capabilities before picking pre-made widgets. **OK** closes the wizard and **Ignore** continues.
:::

### 4. Theme

Quickly swap, explore, or backup visual styling palettes across your entire dashboard:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-left] **Previous Theme:** Step backwards to the previous theme in your list.
* [button ph-caret-right] **Next Theme:** Step forward to the next theme in your list.
* [button ph-squares-four] **[Theme Explorer](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#help-theme-explorer):** Opens a preview browser of **My Themes** and **Built-in Themes**. Click a card to preview on the canvas, then **Apply Theme** or **Cancel**.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Select Theme:** Pick any built-in theme, adjustment theme, or custom theme from Homey storage. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-cloud-arrow-up] **Save Theme:** Save current colors, typography, and container styles to Homey as a reusable custom theme. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-download-simple] **Export Theme:** Download current colors and fonts as a `.json` theme file.
* [button ph-folder-open] **Import Theme:** Load a theme `.json` file from your computer.
:::

For an in-depth guide on full themes, adjustment themes, the Theme Explorer gallery, and modern glass styling, see [Styling & Layering](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#help-theme-explorer).

### 5. Create Widget

Add new controls and visual components to your dashboard:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Widget Type:** Choose the type of widget you want to create from the alphabetized dropdown list.
* [button ph-plus] **Add:** Places a widget of the chosen type onto your canvas. In [Fixed Resolution](help://Layout%20Modes#help-fixed-resolution) and [Scale to Fit Screen](help://Layout%20Modes#scale-to-fit-screen), it appears in the center of the canvas. In [Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns), it joins the layout at the next grid position. If an existing group is open, the widget is added directly inside that group.
:::

New widgets automatically adopt your master defaults. You can immediately apply a [Widget Preset](help://Widgets/presets) for a ready-to-use look, or connect incoming data with [Topics](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29). Explore all available types in [Widgets](help://Widgets).

### 6. Selected Widget Tools

Fine-tune position, visual layering, and lifecycle for the active selection:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Selected Widget Dropdown:** Click this dropdown to see an alphabetized list of every widget on your canvas, color-coded by widget type and organized by page. Selecting a widget automatically navigates to its page and selects it in the editor.
* [button ph-lock-key] **Lock:** Lock or unlock the widget in place so it cannot be dragged or resized by accident.
* [button ph-caret-double-up] **Bring to Front:** Raise the widget one step higher in the visual [layering](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/layering-widgets) order.
* [button ph-caret-double-down] **Send to Back:** Lower the widget one step deeper behind other elements.
* [button ph-palette] **Current:** Reset the selected widget's colors and fonts back to current theme defaults.
* [button ph-palette] **All:** Reset styling across every widget on the canvas back to current theme defaults.
* [button ph-arrow-square-out] **Move to Page:** Relocate the selected widget to another page on your dashboard.
* [button ph-stack-plus] **Duplicate:** Make an immediate duplicate copy of the selected widget (`Ctrl/Cmd+D`).
* [button ph-trash] **Delete:** Remove the selected widget from your canvas (`Delete` or `Backspace`).
:::

::: alert info stack
**Selecting Overlapping Widgets:**

Use **Middle Mouse Click** or hold **Alt** + left click to cycle through layered widgets and select items underneath.
:::

### 7. Universal Actions

Perform clipboard actions, manage history, organize groups, and handle pages:

::: grid
* [button ph-copy text-cyan-400] **Copy:** Copy selected widgets to your internal clipboard (`Ctrl/Cmd+C`).
* [button ph-scissors text-cyan-400] **Cut:** Cut selected widgets to your clipboard (`Ctrl/Cmd+X`).
* [button ph-clipboard-text text-cyan-400] **Paste:** Paste copied widgets onto the active canvas (`Ctrl/Cmd+V`).
* [button ph-arrow-counter-clockwise text-cyan-400] **Undo:** Step back up to 20 actions in your edit history (`Ctrl/Cmd+Z`).
* [button ph-arrow-clockwise text-cyan-400] **Redo:** Reapply undone actions up to 20 steps (`Ctrl/Cmd+Y` or `Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z`).
* [button ph-stack-simple text-cyan-400] **Group:** Combine two or more selected widgets into a unified group that moves together.
* [button ph-stack-minus text-red-400] **Ungroup:** Dissolve a group while keeping all member widgets in place.
* [button ph-arrows-out-simple text-cyan-400] **Open Group / Close Group:** Enter group focus mode to adjust member widgets freely, then close it to return to the main canvas.
* [button ph-file-plus text-emerald-400] **Insert Page:** Add a new blank page to your dashboard.
* [button ph-file-minus text-red-400] **Delete Page:** Remove an empty dashboard page.
:::

::: alert info stack
**Groups in Responsive Columns:**

When using [Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns), a closed group acts as a single widget inside the column grid. You can configure its column span, preferred column, and scale mode as one unified cell, while still editing member widgets freely inside focus mode.
:::

Discover more rapid actions in [Editor Shortcuts](help://Editor%20Shortcuts).

### 8. Page Navigator & Utilities

Navigate between screens and keep your settings workspace organized:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-left] **Previous Page:** Navigate to the previous dashboard page.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Page Indicator:** Displays your active page number.
* [button ph-caret-right] **Next Page:** Navigate to the next dashboard page.
* [button ph-list-dashes] **Toggle Groups:** Expand or collapse all accordion sections in the sidebar to keep your view clean.
:::

### 9. Platform Connection

Set up communication between Dashboard Studio and your smart home:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Platform:** Choose your data provider. Select **Homey** [badge: Homey Pro] for native smart home connectivity, **MQTT** for external brokers, or **Simulation** mode for offline layout testing.
* [button ph-sliders] **Driver Settings:** Configure connection details for your selected driver, including IP addresses, credentials, port numbers, and client identifiers.
:::

When connected to Homey, live devices and capabilities sync automatically. See [Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide).

### 10. Data Stream Explorer

Inspect incoming live data and copy topic addresses across your smart home:

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Filter Topics:** Type in this search box to filter devices, capabilities, and variables in real time.
* [button ph-tag] **Copy Topic Name:** Copy the topic path with a single click, ready to paste into widget bindings.
* [button ph-brackets-curly] **Copy Raw Value:** Copy the latest incoming payload value to your clipboard.
* [button ph-trash] **Clear History:** Clear the temporary list of captured monitor messages.
* [button ph-copy] **Copy All Topic Names:** Copy every known topic name to your clipboard, formatted with one topic per line.
* [button ph-squares-four] **Auto-Widget Gallery:** Open a gallery of live widget previews from the topics in this list. Check the ones you want and add them to the canvas together.
:::

Hover over the monitor list to pause incoming updates while inspecting values. Learn how to connect topics in [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor).

### 11. Editor Environment

::: p #help-editor-mode
Customize your editing workspace, alignment grids, and toolbar behavior:
:::

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Editor Mode:** Toggle between **Basic** and **Advanced** editor tiers. **Basic** mode keeps the inspector clean by focusing on essentials and presets. **Advanced** mode exposes full fine-tuning controls across styling, layout, and data options.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Quick Toolbar:** Choose how the floating tool palette behaves (**Auto Hide When Docked**, **Always Visible**, or **Never Visible**). **Auto Hide When Docked** shows the docked rail when **Universal Actions** starts to scroll out of view. Drag it anywhere across the canvas, dock it to the sidebar edge, or resize it by dragging from the sides or corners to adjust its column layout. When the floating palette is wider than it is tall, icon groups sit left to right. Drag the top or bottom edge to choose 1, 2, 3, or more icon rows, the same way side-dragging chooses columns when groups stack. The move handle sits on the left in that layout.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Grid Size (px):** Set grid cell dimensions (default   px) for alignment in [Fixed Resolution](help://Layout%20Modes#help-fixed-resolution), [Scale to Fit Screen](help://Layout%20Modes#scale-to-fit-screen), and inside open groups in [Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns).
* [button ph-check-square] **Snap to Grid:** Automatically align widgets to the nearest grid step while dragging and resizing. In **Responsive Columns** this control reads **Snap to Grid in groups** and applies while you edit widgets inside an open group.
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Grid Overlay:** Render a subtle dotted grid for visual guidance. In **Fixed Resolution** and **Scale to Fit Screen** it covers the canvas. In **Responsive Columns** this control reads **Show Grid Overlay in groups** and shows the overlay on the open group canvas.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Widget Labels In Editor Canvas:** Control when widget type and name badges appear on the canvas (**Hide**, **Always**, or **Hover**).
:::

### 12. Dashboard Environment

Configure global display proportions, canvas backdrops, and layout rules:

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Active Page:** The page open on the dashboard. A fresh load uses this page, or **Startup Landing Page** when **Enable Startup Landing Page & Inactivity Return** is on.
* [button ph-palette] **Theme:** Select the active theme (built-in or custom). When bound to a topic, you can trigger dynamic scenes like switching from a light theme to a dark theme based on the time of day. Incoming payloads can use theme keys or friendly names (e.g. default_dark, Default Dark, cyberpunk, Cyberpunk Neon, or user theme names; case, spaces, and underscores are ignored), and unrecognized payloads are ignored without making changes.
* [button ph-broadcast] **Current Page Output Topic:** Broadcast the active page number to a live topic whenever navigation occurs.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Layout Mode:** Choose how the canvas behaves. Pick **Fixed Resolution** for pixel-precise coordinate placement, **Scale to Fit Screen** to scale that fixed layout to any screen, or **Responsive Columns** for fluid multi-column grids. See [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes).
* [button ph-check-square] **Keep Aspect Ratio:** In **Scale to Fit Screen**, preserve original aspect ratios with clean letterboxing, or disable to stretch content across the viewport.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Column Count:** Maximum number of columns across wide screens in **Responsive Columns** mode.
* [button ph-check-square] **Reduce Columns to Fit:** Automatically reduce column count when the browser window narrows below minimum column width.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min Column Width:** The minimum width floor for each column before reducing columns or scrolling.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Max Column Width:** Cap maximum column growth (`0` fills available space).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Gap (px):** Spacing between cells in the responsive grid.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min Widget Height:** Minimum height for each widget when cell height is set to auto.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Resolution Presets:** Select standard screen sizes for tablets, phones, and monitors.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Width & Height:** Specify custom canvas pixel dimensions (`0` allows unlimited dimensions).
* [button ph-caret-down] **Column Alignment:** Align leftover column space (**Left**, **Center**, **Right**, or **Stretch**).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Page Padding:** Inset your responsive grid from the display edges (Left, Right, Top, and Bottom).
* [button ph-check-square] **Hide Scrollbars on dashboard:** Conceal browser scrollbars for clean wall tablets and [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display) setups.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Background Style:** Style the canvas backdrop with **Flat Color**, **Linear Gradient**, **Mirror Gradient**, or **Radial Gradient**.
* [button ph-image] **Background Image URL:** Add a backdrop image with custom **Image Fit** (`cover`, `contain`, or `tile`) and an optional **Color Overlay**.
* [button ph-check-square] **Enable Startup Landing Page & Inactivity Return:** Open **Startup Landing Page** when the dashboard loads, and return to it after **Inactivity Timeout (seconds, 0 = Disabled)** from the last tap, click, key press, or scroll. Setting the timeout to `0` disables automatic return and only uses the page on startup. Add `page=` and a page number to the URL to open that page on load. Defaults are page `1` and `60` seconds.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Hold to Activate Duration (seconds):** Set the press duration required before triggering protected switches and buttons.
* [button ph-arrow-counter-clockwise] **Reset all widget default settings:** Restores all widget master defaults to factory settings without changing your Platform or Dashboard Environment configuration.
:::

### 13. Regional & Localization

Set global language, date formats, time display preferences, and calendar rules:

::: grid
* [button ph-translate] **Language / Locale:** Default language for countdown units (years, days, hours, minutes, seconds), weekday names, and month names across the dashboard. Choose **Auto (Browser Default)** to detect the language from the tablet or browser, select one of the 13 built-in languages, or apply a saved custom translation preset.
* [button ph-pencil-simple] **Edit / Customize Translations...:** Opens the translation editor dialog to customize individual words, abbreviations, and units, or save and export reusable language presets.
* [button ph-clock] **Time Format:** Sets the global 12-hour or 24-hour clock preference (**Auto**, **24-Hour**, or **12-Hour (AM/PM)**) inherited by Clock, List, and Graph widgets.
* [button ph-calendar] **Date Format:** Sets the global calendar date order (**Auto**, **DD-MM-YYYY**, **MM-DD-YYYY**, or **YYYY-MM-DD**) inherited across the dashboard.
* [button ph-calendar-blank] **First Day of Week:** Sets the starting weekday column (**Auto**, **Monday**, or **Sunday**) for Markdown calendars in Text widgets.
:::

### 14. Theme Colors

Establish a cohesive visual identity across your entire dashboard:

::: alert info palette
**Using Theme Tokens Anywhere:**

Theme tokens can be used to style elements anywhere in Dashboard Studio, including widget backgrounds, text, borders, icons, and indicator glows. Simply assign a theme token (such as `@accent`, `@primary`, or `@danger`) instead of a fixed color. Whenever you change a theme token in **Theme Colors**, every widget and element using that token updates instantly across your entire dashboard.
:::

::: grid
* [button ph-palette] **Semantic Color Slots:** Customize standard color slots including **Background**, **Background Accent**, **Primary**, **Accent**, **Text**, **Text Muted**, **Card Background**, **Card Border**, **Card Border Accent**, **Success**, **Warning**, and **Danger**.
* [button ph-faders] **Theme Corrections:** Shift every theme color together. **Color Tone** rotates the palette from `-180°` to `+180°`, with `0°` in the center. **Color Intensity** scales color saturation from `0%` to `200%`, with `100%` in the center. **Contrast** spreads dark colors darker and light colors lighter, from `0%` to `200%`, with `100%` in the center. **Brightness** scales from `0%` to `200%`, with `100%` in the center. A color that clips at the high end comes back when Contrast, Brightness, or Color Intensity moves toward `100%`. The reset button returns all four sliders to center.
* [button ph-arrow-counter-clockwise] **Reset all widget default colors to theme colors:** Reconnects all widget master default colors to match factory theme tokens without altering your individual per-widget overrides.
:::

You can also bind any theme color slot to live data (such as [Unified Light State](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state)) using the binding button next to each color picker. **Theme Corrections** is a helper, not a saved setting. Saving keeps the colors you see, and loading another theme returns all three sliders to center. Explore [Dynamic Colors](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/dynamic-colors) and [Styling & Layering](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#theme-colors-semantic-tokens) for details.

### 15. Audio

Bring your dashboards to life with sound feedback and automated alerts:

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Topic Audio:** Configure audio clips to play automatically when specific topics receive new values. Great for door chimes, security alerts, or spoken status updates.
:::

::: alert info clock
**Startup Audio Protection:**

Audio playback stays muted for five seconds after the dashboard loads. This ensures Homey cache replay or retained MQTT messages do not trigger an unexpected burst of sound effects on startup.
:::

Manage uploaded sound files and test playback in the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery). Individual widgets such as Switch, Slider, and Clock can also trigger their own sounds directly within their settings.

### 16. Typography

Set global typographic standards for clean readability:

::: grid
* [button ph-google-logo] **Custom Google Fonts:** Load any typeface from Google Fonts by entering its font family name.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Global Font Family:** Set the primary typeface applied to widgets across your entire dashboard.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Case:** Standardize label text casing (**UPPERCASE**, **Capitalize**, **lowercase**, or **None**).
* [button ph-check-square] **Bold:** Apply bold weight to all widget labels by default.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Line Height:** Set the line height multiplier for multi-line labels.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Horizontal Alignment:** Choose default horizontal text alignment (Left, Center, Right).
* [button ph-caret-down] **Vertical Alignment:** Choose default vertical text placement (Top, Middle, Bottom).
* [button ph-palette] **Default Text Colors:** Establish default palette colors for **Value Color** and **Label Color**.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Font Size Hierarchy:** Configure uniform sizing scales for **Base Size**, **Value Size**, **Label Size**, and **Unit Size**.
:::

### 17. Master Widget Settings

Below Typography, the editor provides global baseline settings for widget containers and each individual widget type:

::: alert info sliders
**Master Defaults vs Individual Overrides:**

Master widget settings define the starting appearance and behavior for newly added widgets. An individual widget only deviates from these defaults when you explicitly change a setting in that widget's own inspector panel.
:::

::: grid
* [button ph-paint-brush] **Container Style:** Customize universal border radius, card backgrounds, opacity, gradient angle, borders, and glow effects for all widget cards.
* [button ph-chat-teardrop-text] **[Dialog Box](help://Widgets/dialog-box):** Shared confirmation overlay. Widget **Confirmation Dialog** settings inherit these until you override them on a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#3-confirmation-dialog).
* [button ph-sliders-horizontal] **Per-Widget Master Defaults:** Configure global defaults for each individual widget type, such as [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch), [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge), [Slider](help://Widgets/slider), [Clock](help://Widgets/clock), and [Light Grid](help://Widgets/lightgrid).
:::

::: p #help-dialog-box
**Dialog Box** sits directly below **Container Style**. It is the dashboard default for confirmation overlays. Full options live in [Dialog Box](help://Widgets/dialog-box).
:::

Newly created widgets automatically inherit these master settings so your layout stays consistent without repetitive styling. When an individual widget needs a unique appearance, customize its settings directly in its own inspector. To discard local overrides and restore a widget back to master defaults, click **Current** in [Selected Widget Tools](#6-selected-widget-tools).

topics.title: Layout Modes
topics.content:
![header: Editor Interface](help/images/header_layout_modes.jpg)

::: lead
Pick how the canvas behaves in **Dashboard Environment** → **Layout Mode**. You can design in pixels, scale that layout to the screen, or let widgets flow in columns.
:::

Switching modes keeps your widgets. Fixed positions stay available when you return to **Fixed Resolution** or **Scale to Fit Screen**. Responsive placement lives in **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**.

### Fixed Resolution

::: p #help-fixed-resolution
Widgets sit at absolute X/Y coordinates with a Width and Height in pixels. This is the classic free-form canvas.
:::

* Choose a **Resolution Preset** (phone, tablet, monitor) or type **Width** and **Height**. `0` on an axis means that axis fills the available space.
* **Grid Size**, **Snap to Grid**, and **Show Grid Overlay** in **Editor Environment** help you align widgets on the canvas.
* Drag to move. Drag the white handles to resize.

Use this mode when you want pixel-perfect wall art, overlapping controls, or a layout locked to one device size.

### Scale to Fit Screen

You still design in pixels, exactly like **Fixed Resolution**. At runtime the whole canvas scales to fill the viewport.

* **Keep Aspect Ratio** (on by default) scales uniformly and letterboxes unused space. The dashboard background still fills the screen.
* Turn **Keep Aspect Ratio** off to stretch the layout to the full viewport.
* The same **Grid Size**, **Snap to Grid**, and **Show Grid Overlay** controls in **Editor Environment** apply here.

Use this when one designed size should fill phones, tablets, and TVs without rebuilding the page. For kiosk bookmarks see [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters#7-dashboard-viewer-kiosk-mode).

### Responsive Columns

::: p #help-responsive-columns
Widgets become cells in a column grid. The page reflows as the window width changes. This is the layout to use when one dashboard should work on phones and wide screens.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Responsive Website Tutorial**
To follow a step-by-step walkthrough creating a full browser start page with bookmarks, a clock banner, smart home controls, and multi-engine search, follow [Responsive Website: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/responsive-website-complete-guide).
:::

A practical pattern is to **double or triple** the column count you have in mind, then set each widget **Column Span** to `2` or `3`. The widgets still line up on your target layout, and you can place a widget at half or one third of that column width. Example: three widgets side by side, with a full-width calendar sitting above them.

Set the column grid under **Dashboard Environment**:

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Column Count:** Maximum number of columns across wide screens.
* [button ph-check-square] **Reduce Columns to Fit:** Automatically uses fewer columns when the window is too narrow for Min Column Width. The Column Count value stays as you set it. The page scrolls only when a single column still cannot fit.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min Column Width:** The minimum width floor for each column before reducing columns or scrolling.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Max Column Width:** Caps maximum column growth (`0` fills the available frame). Use Column Alignment Center when leftover space remains.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Column Alignment:** Positions leftover space (**Left**, **Center**, **Right**, **Stretch**) when Width is greater than `0`, or when Max Column Width caps the columns.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Gap (px):** Spacing between cells in the responsive grid.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min Widget Height:** The height floor for **Auto** and **Fill** cells.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Page Padding:** Insets the widget grid from the display edges (Left, Right, Top, and Bottom). The background still fills the screen.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Width:** Maximum page width (`0` fills the viewport). Height is unused in this mode.
:::

When **Reduce Columns to Fit** is off, the dashboard scrolls as soon as **Column Count** times **Min Column Width** is wider than the window. **Hide Scrollbars on dashboard** clips that overflow for kiosks.

### Per-widget Responsive Layout & Dimensions

Select a widget (or a closed group) to set its grid cell:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Scale Mode:** Choose **Resize** (default, container grows with the cell and content reflows) or **Rescale** (keeps Widget Width and Widget Height as the design size, then scales the interior to fit the cell while borders, corner radius, glow, and padding stay at their configured pixel values).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Order:** Lower numbers appear first in the grid. New widgets receive the next order automatically.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Column Span:** How many columns the cell occupies across the grid.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Preferred Column:** `0` auto-places. A specific number acts as a placement preference, auto-placing if that column is not available and returning when it fits again.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Cell Height Mode:** Choose **Auto** (default) to size the cell to its content, never below **Min Widget Height**. **Fixed** uses the **Cell Height** you type in pixels. **Fill** uses the free space down to the next widget that shares any of its columns. Extra content stays inside the cell. Turn on **Scroll Overflow Content** for Text so long articles scroll. **Min Height** (Fill only) is the floor for that cell. It defaults to **Min Widget Height** and can be overridden. When the widget is last in its columns, the cell stays at **Min Height**.
:::

**Padding** on this slideout is Advanced-only. Basic Settings still shows the rest of **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**.

New widgets receive the next **Order** automatically.

### Combined widgets (groups)

Select two or more widgets and click **Group**. In **Responsive Columns** a closed group is one grid cell with its own **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**.

* **Resize** stretches the members to fill the cell.
* **Rescale** scales the whole composition from the group center, keeping the design aspect ratio. This is how you build a custom control that stays proportional on every screen.

Open the group to edit members on a free-form authoring canvas (same feel as **Fixed Resolution**). **Grid Size**, **Snap to Grid in groups**, and **Show Grid Overlay in groups** in **Editor Environment** align members on that group canvas. Closing the group rebuilds the outline from members that have **Show Container** enabled. Members with **Show Container** off sit as overlays and stay out of that outline.

In **Fixed Resolution** and **Scale to Fit Screen**, groups still move together as a set. Members keep independent positions on the canvas.

Details and toolbar steps live in the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide).

### Related topics

* [Responsive Website: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/responsive-website-complete-guide) for a complete step-by-step walkthrough.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode) for **Editor Environment** (Editor Mode, Quick Toolbar, snap grid, and canvas labels), adding widgets, and groups.
* [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets) for applying a look after you place a widget.
* [Troubleshooting](help://Troubleshooting) if a phone layout still looks tight.

topics.title: Data Types & Formats
topics.content:
![header: Data Formats](help/images/header_data.jpg) ::: lead This section explains how to format your data payloads (from Homey Flows [badge: Homey Pro], MQTT, or Node-RED) so they display correctly in the dashboard, and how to structure advanced JSON commands. ::: ### Quick Reference (Basic Types) | Format Type | Description & Usage | Widgets Using This | Example / Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Boolean (Checkbox)** | Simple true/false logic. Used for turning elements on/off, hiding widgets, or triggering animations. Bound fields support [Binding Options](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas) (word mapping or numeric formula). | *All widgets (Visibility)*, Arrow (Enable Animation), Switch | `true`, `false`, `1`, `0` | | **Number** | Numeric values for sizing, offsets, or sensor data. Bound number fields support [Numeric Payload Formula](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas#numeric-payload-formula). | Gauge (Value), Slider (Value), Graph, Arrow (Line Width) | `24.5`, `100`, `-5` | | **String (Plain Text)** | Standard short strings for naming and labels. | *All widgets (Labels)*, Edit Box, List / Log | `"Living Room"` | | **String (URL)** | Web addresses pointing to resources like camera feeds, or external sites. | Image (Source Type: URL), Switch (Open URL Action) | `http://.../cam.jpg`.
*Tip: Use the [Image Gallery Manager](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager) in the editor to select local uploads.* | | **Raw SVG Code** | Direct XML code for scalable vector graphics. Allows for crisp, infinitely scalable animated elements without loading external files. | Image (Source Type: SVG) | `` | | **Phosphor Icon Class** | A specific text string referencing the built-in Phosphor icon library. | Icon, Menu, Switch (Icon On/Off) | `ph-house`, `ph-lightbulb-fill`.
[See Icons & Images](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/icons-images) | | **Topic Path** | A string representing a local or external data topic used to bind data bidirectionally. | *All widgets (Data Binding)* | `homey/device/light`, `local/button`.
[See Connecting Widgets & Data](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor) | | **Selection Group ID** | A specific text string used to group multiple toggle switches into mutually exclusive "radio buttons". | Switch / Button | `"group_1"`, `"heating_mode"` | | **Color** | Dynamic or static styling properties supporting standard CSS formats and [theme tokens](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/colors). | *All widgets (Background, Fills, Borders)* | `#F54927`, `@accent`.
[See Colors](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/colors) | ### Quick Reference (Advanced Types) | Advanced Type | Description | Documentation | | --- | --- | --- | | **String (Markdown)** | Rich text supporting formatting, tables, lists, and inline icons. Used exclusively by the Text widget. | [View Markdown Reference](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting) | | **[Unified Light State](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state)** | A single JSON object to efficiently control a smart light's state, brightness, and color all at once. | [View Light State format](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state) | | **Graph Data** | Arrays of numbers, time-value objects, or categorized datasets used to render charts and historical logs. | [View Graph formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/graph-data-formats) | | **List / Log Data** | Pipe-delimited strings or JSON arrays containing text, icons, and timestamps for checklists and event logs. | [View List / Log formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/list-log-data-formats) | | **Calendar Events (iCal)** | Filtered calendar event objects produced by Homey Flow [badge: Homey Pro] cards to populate schedules and agendas. | [View Calendar formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/load-filter-ical) | | **[Binding Options](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas) & Formulas** | Defaults, boolean word mapping, live countdown timers, and payload formulas (number, text, color, icon name). | [View Binding Options guide](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas) | | **[Colors](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/colors)** | Theme tokens such as `@accent` that follow **Theme Colors**, plus hex, RGB, and other CSS colors. | [View Colors](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/colors) |

Color Formats

Almost any styling property (like **Background Color**, **Bar Color**, or **Icon Color**) can be bound to a topic. The dashboard supports valid CSS color strings and [theme tokens](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/colors) such as `@accent`. | Format | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | **Hex** | Standard web color (Recommended) | `#ef4444` or `#0f0` | | **RGB** | Red, Green, Blue (0-255) | `rgb(255, 99, 71)` | | **RGBA** | RGB + Alpha (Transparency) | `rgba(255, 99, 71, 0.5)` | | **HSL** | Hue, Saturation, Lightness | `hsl(9, 100%, 64%)` | | **Named** | Standard HTML color names | `red`, `teal`, `transparent` |

widgetSubpages.title: Binding Options & Payload Formulas
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead **Binding Options** let you fine-tune how incoming topic values are interpreted before they reach a widget. Set a fallback when nothing has arrived yet, map custom words to on/off states, or transform values with a compact formula (numbers, text, colors, or icon names). Formulas can use **Value** (the bound topic payload), **Insert Topic** references to other live topics, quoted strings joined with `+`, and boolean logic functions such as **and**, **or**, **not**, **xor**, and **nor**. **contains()** finds exact text inside a payload. **containsanycase()** does the same and ignores letter case. **countdown()** creates live, ticking timers for progress bars, switches, labels, and alerts. ::: [See formula examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=18) [muted: (demo, page 18)] ### Opening Binding Options After you bind a supported field with the **Link Icon** :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400:, an **Options Icon** :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: may appear beside it. Click the faders to open **Binding Options**. The icon turns yellow when boolean mapping, a formula, or color correction is active. A formula that contains only the default **Value** chip is treated as inactive and does not turn the icon yellow. Supported field types: | Field type | What you can configure | | --- | --- | | **Checkbox** (boolean) | Default state, **Transform Mode** (string mapping or numeric formula) | | **Number** | Default value, **Payload Formula** (numeric result) | | **Text** | Default value, **Payload Formula** (may return quoted strings) | | **Icon name** | Default value, **Payload Formula** (quoted Phosphor class names) | | **Color** | Default value, **Payload Formula** (hex or @theme-token result), **Color Adjustments** (color tone, color intensity, brightness) | | **Select** and others | Default fallback value only (no mapping or formula) | Master settings in **⚙️ Dashboard Settings** support the same options for global bindings. ### Default Value At the top of the popup, **Default Value** defines what the widget uses when the topic has not sent anything yet. ::: grid * [button ph-check-square] **Checkbox fields:** A checkbox for the fallback on/off state. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Number fields:** A number input for the starting value. * [button ph-palette] **Color fields:** The color picker (including theme tokens where allowed). * [button ph-star] **Icon name fields:** The Phosphor icon picker (type a class such as `ph-house` or browse the library). * [button ph-caret-down] **Select fields:** The dropdown choice. ::: This default is independent of mapping, formulas, and color adjustments. It applies only while the topic is empty. ### Color fields: Color Adjustments Bound **color** fields show **Color Adjustments** below **Default Value** in the same **Binding Options** popup. ::: grid * [button ph-check-square] **Apply Corrections:** Enable to transform live color payloads after they arrive (including Unified Light JSON auto-extracted colors). Moving any slider automatically enables this setting. * [button ph-sliders] **Color Tone, Color Intensity & Brightness:** Adjust each channel with **Adj** (relative offset or multiplier) or **Fix** (absolute value) modes. Color Tone Adj offsets degrees (-180 to 180), Color Tone Fix sets 0 to 360. Color Intensity and Brightness Adj multiply incoming values (0 to 200%), while Fix pins them to 0 to 100%. ::: The **Options Icon** turns yellow when **Apply Corrections** is active. Use color adjustments to brighten a room-synced background for contrast, rotate color tone for complementary gradients, or cap brightness while keeping the live color tone from your lights. ### Boolean fields: Transform Mode Checkbox bindings (switch state, visibility, charging flags, menu row toggles, and similar) offer two transform modes under **Transform Mode**. #### Boolean Payload Mapping Map incoming **text** to on or off using **Custom True Value** and **Custom False Value**. * Matching is **case-insensitive**. * A **filled** field maps only that exact word (after trimming) to its state. * A **blank** field acts as a wildcard for all other payloads (the opposite state). * If **both** fields are set and the payload matches neither, normal binding rules apply (no forced mapping). **Invert values** swaps the two fields. From empty fields it fills `False` / `True`. From the preset `false` / `true` pair it clears both fields. Otherwise it swaps whatever you typed. ::: alert info lightbulb **Example:** Custom True = `Washing`, Custom False blank. Payload `Washing` turns on. Any other text turns off. ::: #### Numeric Payload Formula Choose **Numeric Payload Formula** to turn the incoming payload into on or off. The formula runs on a numeric payload. The result becomes **0** (off) or **1** (on). Any non-zero finite number is on. **contains()** and **containsanycase()** also run when the payload is ordinary text. **contains(value, "ON")** is on when those exact letters appear anywhere in the text. **containsanycase(value, "ON")** treats `ON`, `On`, and `on` as the same. `Hello the value is ON` is on for both. `Hello the value is on` is on for **containsanycase()**. When the formula does not apply, the incoming payload stays as it arrived. Built-in presets include **Threshold 50**, **Round to 0 or 1**, **Text Contains ON**, **Text Contains Any Case**, and multi-topic patterns that use **and**, **or**, and **not**. When you switch modes, the editor clears the settings from the other mode so stale keys cannot conflict. ### Number fields: Payload Formula Bound **number** fields (gauge value, slider value, offsets, and similar) can use **Payload Formula** without a mode toggle. The transformed result stays a number (not forced to 0/1). Built-in presets include **Invert Sign**, **Absolute**, **Clamp 0-100**, **Whole Number**, and **Threshold 50** (`if(value > 50, 100, 0)`). Use formulas to invert signs, scale readings, clamp ranges, round decimals, combine multiple topics, or apply thresholds before the widget displays or uses the value. ### Text fields: Payload Formula Bound **text** fields can use **Payload Formula** to return text instead of a number. Wrap literal text in quotes (single or double): `if(value >= 50, "yes", "no")`. * The formula result is used as the field's text value. * Compare incoming text payloads with `==` and `!=` against quoted literals. Matching is **case-insensitive** (`Yes == yes`). * **contains(value, "ON")** returns `1` when that exact text appears inside the payload. **containsanycase(value, "ON")** ignores letter case. `Hello the value is ON` matches both. `Hello the value is on` matches **containsanycase()** only. * Join quoted prefixes and suffixes around **Value** with `+`: `"/images/home-night-" + value + ".png"`. * Ordering operators (`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`) work on numbers. Use them on a numeric payload, then return a quoted string from `if()`. * A numeric result is converted to text automatically. Example: `if(value == "on", "Running", "Idle")` returns `Running` when the payload is `on` (any case), otherwise `Idle`. Example: `if(containsanycase(value, "ON"), "Running", "Idle")` returns `Running` when the payload is `Hello the value is on`. ### Icon name fields: Payload Formula Bound **Icon name** fields (Phosphor class names such as `ph-house`) can use **Payload Formula** the same way as **text** fields. Return a quoted Phosphor class so the glyph changes with the incoming value. * Wrap icon class names in quotes: `if(value >= 50, "ph-thermometer-hot", "ph-thermometer-cold")`. * Join a quoted prefix with **Value** to build a class name: `"ph-" + value`. * Compare incoming text payloads with `==` and `!=` against quoted literals. Matching is **case-insensitive**. * **contains(value, "ON")** and **containsanycase(value, "ON")** pick an icon when that text appears inside the payload. **contains()** matches the exact letter case. * Click **Insert Icon** to pick a Phosphor icon. It is inserted as a quoted class (`"ph-house"`) at the cursor. * Built-in presets include **Threshold Two Icons** and **Match Word**. Example: `if(value == "heating", "ph-flame", "ph-snowflake")` shows the flame icon when the payload is `heating` (any case). ### Color fields: Payload Formula Bound **color** fields can use **Payload Formula** to return a color. Return either a hex literal or a @theme-token literal. * Hex literal: `#` + 3, 4, 6, or 8 hex digits (`#abc`, `#abcd`, `#aabbcc`, `#aabbccff`). Example: `if(value >= 50, #121345, #000000)`. * Theme token literal: `@` + token name (`@warning`, `@danger`, `@accent`). Example: `if(value >= 50, @warning, @danger)`. * The formula runs **first**, then any **Color Adjustments** below it apply to the result. For a `@token` result, the token is resolved to its theme color before color correction. * Use `==` and `!=` to compare colors or tokens. Ordering (`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`) and arithmetic (`- * /`) apply to numbers. * **contains(value, "ON")** and **containsanycase(value, "ON")** pick a color when that text appears inside the payload. **contains()** matches the exact letter case. ### Writing formulas The formula field opens with a **Value** chip. That chip represents the payload from the topic bound to this field (the same as typing `value` or `x`). * Type **`value`** (or **`x`**, which is normalized to `value`) for the incoming number on the bound topic. * Click **Insert Value** to add another **Value** token at the cursor. * Click **Insert Topic** to pick a live topic from the dashboard. It is inserted as a `{{topic/path}}` tag chip. * On **Icon name** fields, click **Insert Icon** to pick a Phosphor class. It is inserted as a quoted string at the cursor. * Use ordinary arithmetic, quoted-string joining with `+`, comparisons, boolean logic functions, parentheses, and the functions listed in **Formula syntax reference** below. * Formulas are limited to **512 characters**. * Invalid formulas show a warning when you close the popup and are not saved. Click the left or right half of a tag chip to place the cursor before or after it. Use **Insert Topic** only after placing the cursor where the reference should go. #### Value coercion These payloads are treated as numbers inside formulas: | Payload | Treated as | | --- | --- | | Boolean `true` | `1` | | Boolean `false` | `0` | | String `true` or `True` | `1` | | String `false` or `False` | `0` | | Numeric strings such as `75` | `75` | This applies to **Value** and to every `{{topic}}` reference. ### String, color, and theme-token literals Formulas are not limited to numbers. You can use three extra literal kinds inside any formula: | Literal | Syntax | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | **String** | `"text"` or `'text'` | `if(value >= 50, "yes", "no")` | | **Color** | `#` + 3/4/6/8 hex digits | `if(value >= 50, #121345, #000000)` | | **Theme token** | `@` + token name | `if(value >= 50, @warning, @danger)` | Rules: * `if()` can return any literal kind. The result type must match the field: text and icon name fields accept strings, color fields accept colors or tokens, number fields accept numbers. * **Equality** (`==`, `!=`) works on every type. String equality is **case-insensitive** (`Yes == yes`). Colors compare by hex value. Tokens compare by name. * **Ordering** (`>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`) and **arithmetic** (`- * /`) work on numbers. **`+`** adds two numbers, or joins text when either side is a quoted string or a text payload (for example `"/images/" + value + ".png"`). * A bare `@token` (unquoted) is a color reference and is resolved to its theme color before **Color Adjustments** run. A quoted `"@token"` is plain text and stays literal. * `value` and `{{topic}}` references are typed automatically: a numeric payload becomes a number, a `#hex` or `@token` payload becomes a color or token, and any other text becomes a string. ### Referencing other topics Use **Insert Topic** when a formula needs data from a topic other than the one bound to this field. | Step | What happens | | --- | --- | | **Insert Topic** | Opens the same searchable topic list used when binding. Pick a topic to insert `{{device/capability}}` as a tag chip. | | At runtime | Each `{{topic}}` reads the latest payload from live data. | | Transforms | Referenced topics use their own **Binding Options** first (boolean word mapping or their own formula) before the value enters your expression. | | Reactivity | When a referenced topic updates, every widget whose formula mentions it re-runs, even if the bound topic did not change. | ::: alert info lightbulb **Tip:** If a referenced topic sends text such as `open`, configure **Boolean Payload Mapping** on that topic's bound field so the reference resolves to `1` or `0` before your formula runs. :::

Formula syntax reference

#### Variables | Token | Meaning | | --- | --- | | `value` | The incoming numerical payload on the bound topic (preferred) | | `x` | Alias for `value` (automatically converted) | | `{{topic/path}}` | Live value from another topic via **Insert Topic**. Uses that topic's binding transforms first. | #### Arithmetic operators | Operator | Meaning | Example | Result (value = 10) | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `+` | Addition | `value + 5` | `15` | | `+` | Join text | `"/img/" + value + ".png"` | `/img/10.png` | | `-` | Subtraction | `value - 3` | `7` | | `*` | Multiplication | `value * 2` | `20` | | `/` | Division | `value / 4` | `2.5` | | `( )` | Grouping | `(value + 5) * 2` | `30` | | Unary `-` | Negate | `-value` | `-10` | #### Joining text Use `+` to build a string from quoted literals and **Value** (or an **Insert Topic** reference). Quotes mark the fixed prefix and suffix. **Value** is the live payload from the bound topic. ::: code-block Prefix, Value, suffix "/images/home-night-" + value + ".png" ::: When the payload is `lightning`, the result is `/images/home-night-lightning.png`. The same pattern works on **text** fields (image URLs, labels) and **Icon name** fields (`"ph-" + value`). On **number** fields, `+` still adds two numbers (`value + 5`). The **Prefix and Suffix** preset inserts `"/images/" + value + ".png"`. #### Comparison operators Comparisons evaluate to **1** (true) or **0** (false). Use them inside **`if()`** or pass them to boolean logic functions. | Operator | Meaning | Example (value = 75) | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `>` | Greater than | `value > 50` | `1` | | `>=` | Greater than or equal | `value >= 50` | `1` | | `<` | Less than | `value < 50` | `0` | | `<=` | Less than or equal | `value <= 50` | `0` | | `==` | Equal | `value == 75` | `1` | | `!=` | Not equal | `value != 0` | `1` | #### Boolean logic functions Logic functions also return **1** (true) or **0** (false). Inside a formula, **0** is false. Any other finite number is true. | Function | Meaning | Min args | Example | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **`and()`** | **1** only when every argument is non-zero | 2 | `and(1, 0)` | `0` | | **`or()`** | **1** when at least one argument is non-zero | 2 | `or(1, 0)` | `1` | | **`not()`** | **1** when the argument is zero, otherwise **0** | 1 | `not(0)` | `1` | | **`xor()`** | **1** when an odd number of arguments are non-zero | 2 | `xor(1, 1)` | `0` | | **`nor()`** | **1** when every argument is zero (logical NOT-OR) | 2 | `nor(1, 0)` | `0` | With topic references, pass comparisons, topic chips, or **`value`** as arguments. Example: `and({{motion}}, {{lamp}})` with motion = `1` and lamp = `0` returns `0`. #### Math and utility functions | Function | Arguments | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **`if()`** | `(condition, then, else)` | Returns **then** when **condition** is non-zero, otherwise **else** | `if(value >= 50, 100, 0)` | | **`round()`** | `(n)` or `(n, decimals)` | Rounds to the nearest integer, or to the given decimal places | `round(value)` | | **`min()`** | `(a, b, …)` | Returns the smallest argument | `min(value, 100)` | | **`max()`** | `(a, b, …)` | Returns the largest argument | `max(value, 0)` | | **`abs()`** | `(n)` | Absolute value (removes the sign) | `abs(value)` | | **`number()`** | `(n)` | Converts the argument to a number | `number(value)` | | **`contains()`** | `(text, part)` | **1** when `part` appears in `text` with the same letter case. A blank `part` returns **0** | `contains(value, "ON")` | | **`containsanycase()`** | `(text, part)` | **1** when `part` appears in `text`, ignoring letter case. `ON`, `On`, and `on` all match. A blank `part` returns **0** | `containsanycase(value, "ON")` | | **`countdown()`** | `(target[, format][, doneText])` | Starts a live ticking countdown. Formats include clock strings, localized words, units (including years), percentages, booleans, and custom ending text when elapsed | `countdown("5m", "timer", "Done!")` | #### **`if()` in detail** Syntax: **`if(condition, valueIfTrue, valueIfFalse)`** * **condition** can be a comparison (`value >= 50`), a logic call (`and(...)`), a topic reference, or any expression. Zero means false. Any other finite number means true. * **valueIfTrue** and **valueIfFalse** can be numbers, quoted strings, colors, theme tokens, or nested expressions, including another **`if()`**. #### Nested `if()` for three bands Place a second **`if()`** in the else branch to return three different results from one payload. A common pattern is a 0-100 reading split into low, mid, and high. Read the formula from the outside in. The outer test runs first. When it is false, the inner **`if()`** decides between the remaining two results. ::: code-block Three color bands if(value >= 66, #ff0000, if(value >= 33, #00ff00, #0000ff)) ::: | Incoming value | What happens | Result | | --- | --- | --- | | `80` | `80 >= 66` is true, so the outer branch wins | Red `#ff0000` | | `50` | Outer test is false. Inner test `50 >= 33` is true | Green `#00ff00` | | `10` | Both tests are false, so the inner else wins | Blue `#0000ff` | This splits a 0-100 scale into three bands: | Band | Range | Color | | --- | --- | --- | | High | `66` and above | `#ff0000` (red) | | Mid | `33` through `65` | `#00ff00` (green) | | Low | below `33` | `#0000ff` (blue) | Put the **highest** threshold on the outside. That way 80 matches red first, 50 falls through to green, and 10 falls through to blue. The same nesting works with quoted icon names, quoted text, theme tokens, or numbers. Nest another **`if()`** in the inner else to add a fourth band. The 256-character formula limit still applies. ### Countdown Timer Functions: countdown() Live countdown timers bring dashboards to life. Whether you want a visual kitchen timer on your wall tablet, an automatic progress bar for your laundry machine, or a switch that stays on for ten minutes before turning off, the **countdown()** function handles it all in a single expression. Countdowns tick every second on active dashboard pages. To protect battery life on tablets and phones, the timer uses a demand-driven engine. It ticks only when at least one active widget on your current page needs it. When you switch pages, turn off your display, or background your browser, the timer pauses automatically. You can write countdown formulas inside the **Payload Formula** of any widget field (including switches, buttons, gauges, sliders, containers, and icons), or inline inside Text widgets using `{{countdown(...)}}`. #### How countdowns work A countdown formula accepts up to three arguments: ::: code-block Countdown signature countdown(target, [format], [doneText]) ::: * **target (required):** How long to count down, or when to finish. This can be a duration string such as `"5m"` or `"8y 30d"`, raw seconds such as `300`, an incoming device payload like `value`, another topic reference, or a future calendar date. * **format (optional):** The presentation style. When omitted, it outputs a clean digital clock format (`mm:ss`, `hh:mm:ss`, or with years and days for long timers). If you pass a custom message that is not a format keyword (such as `"Ready!"`), it is automatically treated as `doneText`. * **doneText (optional):** Custom text displayed when the timer reaches zero (e.g. `"Done!"`, `"Finished!"`, `"Pizza Ready!"`). When omitted, it uses the ending text defined in your Dashboard Regional & Localization translations, or falls back to standard zero time (`00:00` or `0s`). Countdowns clamp at zero once time expires. They never count into negative numbers. This makes checking whether a timer is finished straightforward and reliable. #### Supported input targets The target argument accepts many practical formats. You do not need to convert minutes to seconds in your head or format timestamps manually. | Target type | Example syntax | What it does | | --- | --- | --- | | **Short duration** | `countdown("5m")` | Counts down from 5 minutes (300 seconds). | | **Short seconds** | `countdown("45s")` | Counts down from 45 seconds. | | **Mixed duration** | `countdown("1h 30m")` | Counts down from 1 hour and 30 minutes. | | **Multi-unit string** | `countdown("2d 4h 15m")` | Counts down across days, hours, and minutes. Whitespace between units is optional. | | **Multi-year duration** | `countdown("8y 30d 4h")` | Counts down across years (365 days), days, and hours. | | **Regional / Dutch units** | `countdown("2u 30m")` | Accepts localized duration units such as `u` (uur), `min`, and `sec`. | | **Raw seconds number** | `countdown(300)` | Direct numeric seconds (300 seconds = 5 minutes). | | **Incoming device payload** | `countdown(value)` | Uses the payload from the bound topic (such as remaining seconds or a duration string from Homey). | | **Referenced topic** | `countdown({{kitchen/timer}})` | Tracks a countdown from any other live topic on your dashboard. | | **Clock string** | `countdown("05:00")` | Reads clock formats directly as 5 minutes. | | **Future calendar date** | `countdown("2026-12-25 00:00")` | Counts down to a specific target date and time. | | **Date only** | `countdown("2026-12-25")` | Counts down to midnight at the start of that date. | When a countdown is placed inside a conditional test like `if(value == "on", countdown("10m"), "00:00")`, the timer anchors to the exact moment the condition turns on. When the condition turns off, the anchor cleans up automatically. #### Output format styles Pass a format name as the second argument to choose how the remaining time is calculated or displayed: | Format key | Example formula | Output while running | Output at zero (clamped) | Best suited for | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Default** *(omitted)* | `countdown("5m")` | `05:00` (or `01:30:00` when hours remain) | `00:00` (or custom ending text) | Digital clocks, labels, and cards | | **Default (with years & days)** | `countdown("8y 30d 4h")` | `8y 30d 04:00:00` | `00:00` (or custom ending text) | Long-range project, milestone, or vacation counters | | **`"timer"`** | `countdown("5m", "timer")` | `00:05:00` (always `HH:MM:SS`) | `00:00:00` (or custom ending text) | Fixed-width digital timers and stopwatches | | **`"compact"`** | `countdown("8y 30d", "compact")` | `8y 30d` (top 2 active units) | `0s` (or custom ending text) | Compact cards and tight spaces | | **`"compact-full"`** | `countdown("8y 30d 4h", "compact-full")` | `8y 30d 4h` (includes every active unit) | `0s` (or custom ending text) | Detailed multi-unit event summaries | | **`"words"`** | `countdown("8y 30d", "words")` | `8 years, 30 days` (top 2 units) | `0 seconds` (or custom ending text) | Natural speech, sentences, and notes | | **`"words-full"`** | `countdown("8y 30d 4h", "words-full")` | `8 years, 30 days, 4 hours` (all units) | `0 seconds` (or custom ending text) | Full descriptive sentences and long-term milestones | | **`"years"`** | `countdown("8y 30d", "years")` | `8` (whole years remaining) | `0` | Long-term milestone triggers and badges | | **`"days"`** | `countdown("2026-12-25", "days")` | `48` (whole days remaining) | `0` | Event badges and holiday counters | | **`"hours"`** | `countdown("5h30m", "hours")` | `5` (whole hours remaining) | `0` | Shift trackers and heating schedules | | **`"minutes"`** | `countdown("45m10s", "minutes")` | `45` (whole minutes remaining) | `0` | Cooking alerts and laundry cycles | | **`"seconds"`** | `countdown("90s", "seconds")` | `90` (total seconds remaining) | `0` | High-precision numeric gauges and math | | **`"percent"`** | `countdown("5m", "percent")` | `0` climbing smoothly to `100` | `100` | Standard progress bars, sliders, and gauges | | **`"percent-remaining"`** | `countdown("5m", "percent-remaining")` | `100` dropping smoothly to `0` | `0` | Depletion gauges and battery-style rings | | **`"isDone"`** | `countdown("5m", "isDone")` | `0` (false) | `1` (true) | Completion badges, alerts, and dialogs | | **`"isRunning"`** | `countdown("5m", "isRunning")` | `1` (true) | `0` (false) | Switch states, active glows, and spinners | All text, unit letters, and word outputs automatically use your dashboard language set in **?? Dashboard Settings** under **Canvas & Environment**. #### Custom ending text when time expires You can display a custom message as soon as a countdown reaches zero instead of `00:00` or `0s`: * **Per-timer ending text:** Pass your custom message as the third argument (or as the second argument if using the default clock format): * `countdown("5m", "timer", "Time's up!")` shows `00:05:00` while running, and `Time's up!` when finished. * `countdown("5m", "Pizza Ready!")` uses the default format and switches to `Pizza Ready!` when finished. * **Dashboard-wide ending text:** You can also set a default ending text across all countdowns in **?? Dashboard Settings -> Regional & Localization -> Edit Translations** (for example `"Done"` or `"Gereed"`). Any countdown that does not specify an inline custom ending text will automatically display this message when elapsed. #### Automatic conversion to numbers (Auto-coercion) In Dashboard Studio, clock strings and duration words convert to numbers automatically when used in numeric contexts. You never need to write manual conversion math. * **Clock strings to seconds:** `"05:00"` evaluates as `300` seconds. `"01:30:00"` evaluates as `5400` seconds. * **Duration strings to seconds:** `"45s"` evaluates as `45`. `"1h 15m"` evaluates as `4500`. * **Zero clamping:** `"00:00"` evaluates as `0`. * **Direct comparisons:** You can write `countdown("5m") > 60` or `countdown("1m") == 0` without conversion helpers. * **Direct numeric widget input:** Passing `countdown(300)` directly to a Gauge configured with Min `0` and Max `300` automatically drives the needle from `300` down to `0`. #### Activating controls on a timer (Boolean options) When connecting a countdown to a checkbox property (such as widget visibility, button state, container glow, or switch state), use `"isRunning"` or `"isDone"`. They return clean `1` (on) and `0` (off) values. ##### Keep a switch or light ON while a timer runs Use `"isRunning"` to keep equipment active for a specific duration. ::: code-block Switch active for 15 minutes countdown("15m", "isRunning") ::: When applied to the **State** property of a Switch / Button widget, the switch stays active while time remains. Once the timer reaches zero, the switch automatically turns off. ##### Show a "Finished!" badge or container when done Use `"isDone"` to reveal notifications, warning icons, or dialog boxes the moment a timer finishes. ::: code-block Show completion badge countdown({{washing_machine/timer}}, "isDone") ::: Bind this expression to the **Visibility** property of a Container or Label widget. The widget remains hidden while the washing machine runs, and pops into view as soon as time hits zero. ##### Trigger an alert dialog when time expires Bind the **Open** or **Visibility** property of a Dialog Box widget to: ::: code-block Open dialog on completion countdown("30m", "isDone") ::: The dialog remains closed until the thirty-minute countdown finishes, then opens automatically on your canvas. #### Progress bars, gauges, and sliders Countdown formulas make it easy to build visual progress indicators without complex math. ##### Progress bar that fills up from 0% to 100% Add a Slider widget, set its type to **Progress**, and leave its Min and Max at `0` and `100`. Then set its **Value** formula to: ::: code-block Filling progress bar countdown("45m", "percent") ::: The bar begins completely empty at 0%, steadily fills as time elapses, and reaches 100% when the 45 minutes are up. ##### Gauge ring that winds down from 100% to 0% Add a Gauge widget with Min `0` and Max `100`. Bind its **Value** to: ::: code-block Depleting countdown gauge countdown("10m", "percent-remaining") ::: The gauge starts fully lit at 100% and winds down to 0% as the timer runs out. ##### Exact seconds gauge If you prefer showing actual seconds rather than percentages, configure your Gauge with Min `0` and Max `300` (for 5 minutes). Then bind **Value** to: ::: code-block Direct seconds gauge countdown(300) ::: Thanks to automatic numeric conversion, the gauge tracks seconds directly from 300 down to 0. #### Dynamic text, colors, and icons Because `countdown()` works inside `if()` statements, you can change styles and messages based on remaining time. ##### Change color during the final minute Turn a widget yellow while running, but switch to a bright red warning color when less than 60 seconds remain: ::: code-block Warning color in final minute if(countdown("5m", "seconds") <= 60, @danger, @warning) ::: ##### Change color when finished Keep a label green while running, then switch to a neutral gray when done: ::: code-block Finished color toggle if(countdown("15m", "isDone"), #64748b, #22c55e) ::: ##### Dynamic timer icon Display an active hourglass while a timer is running, and switch to a checkmark when complete: ::: code-block Timer icon toggle if(countdown("10m", "isRunning"), "ph-hourglass-high", "ph-check-circle") ::: ##### Custom text message upon completion Show the remaining digital clock while running, but replace it with a friendly message when the timer finishes: ::: code-block Custom completion text if(countdown("5m", "isDone"), "Tea is ready!", countdown("5m", "timer")) ::: ##### Natural language in Text widgets In a Text widget, you can insert countdown tokens directly into your markdown content: ::: code-block Inline markdown text The sprinkler shuts off in {{countdown("20m", "words")}}. ::: This displays as *The sprinkler shuts off in 20 minutes.* and updates smoothly every second. ### Examples [See live formula examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=18) [muted: (demo, page 18)] #### Countdown payload formulas | Goal | Field type | Formula | Incoming / topics | Result | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Standard digital countdown | Text or Label | `countdown("5m")` | None | `05:00` ticking down to `00:00` | | Three-part digital timer | Text or Label | `countdown("10m", "timer")` | None | `00:10:00` ticking down to `00:00:00` | | Compact readable timer | Text or Label | `countdown("1h30m", "compact")` | None | `1h 30m` ticking down to `0s` | | Localized full words | Text or Label | `countdown("45m", "words")` | None | `45 minutes` (or `45 minuten`) | | Days to target holiday | Text or Label | `countdown("2026-12-25", "days")` | None | Remaining whole days | | Progress bar filling 0-100% | Number (Slider/Gauge) | `countdown("30m", "percent")` | None | `0` climbing to `100` | | Depletion gauge 100-0% | Number (Slider/Gauge) | `countdown("15m", "percent-remaining")` | None | `100` dropping to `0` | | Gauge tracking raw seconds | Number (Gauge 0-300) | `countdown(300)` | None | `300` dropping to `0` | | Switch active while running | Checkbox (formula) | `countdown("10m", "isRunning")` | None | On while ticking, Off when done | | Show badge when finished | Checkbox (formula) | `countdown(value, "isDone")` | topic = `"15m"` | Off while ticking, On when done | | Warning color in last minute | Color | `if(countdown("5m", "seconds") <= 60, @danger, @accent)` | None | Accent color, turns red at 60s | | Color change on completion | Color | `if(countdown("5m", "isDone"), #22c55e, #eab308)` | None | Yellow while running, green when done | | Icon changes on completion | Icon name | `if(countdown("5m", "isRunning"), "ph-hourglass-high", "ph-check-circle")` | None | Hourglass while running, checkmark when done | | Custom text message when done | Text | `if(countdown("5m", `({{livingroom/temp}} + {{bedroom/temp}}) / 2` | both `20` | `20` | | Double a referenced reading | Number | `{{sensor/power}} * 2` | topic = `15` | `30` | | Show whole watts | Number | `round(value)`
