widgetSubpages.title: Unified Light State (JSON)
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
To control smart lights efficiently, Dashboard Studio uses a standardized JSON format. This allows you to set On/Off, Brightness, Color, and Temperature in a single command. It is compatible with **Home Assistant** standards.
:::

To control smart lights efficiently, Dashboard Studio uses a standardized JSON format. This allows you to set On/Off, Brightness, Color, and Temperature in a single command. It is compatible with **Home Assistant** standards.

**Auto-Color Binding:** If you bind a Color Property (e.g. Icon Color) directly to a topic containing this JSON object, the system will automatically extract the color information and apply it. Open [**Binding Options**](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas#color-fields-color-adjustments) on the bound color field and use **Color Adjustments** to correct or offset the live color.

::: code-block Full State Object
{
 "state": "ON", // "ON" or "OFF"
 "brightness": 255, // 0-255
 "color_mode": "hs", // "hs" or "color_temp"
 "color": {
 "h": 360, // 0-360 (Hue)
 "s": 100 // 0-100 (Saturation)
 },
 "color_temp": 153 // 153 (Cold) - 500 (Warm)
}
:::

#### Partial Updates (Patching)

You do not need to send the entire object every time! The system supports **Partial Updates**. Send only the fields you want to change, and the rest will remain as they are.

::: code-block Example: Just Dimming
Description: This changes brightness to 50% without affecting color or state.
{ "brightness": 128 }
:::

::: code-block Example: Change Color
Description: This changes color to Red. The system automatically switches the bulb to Color Mode.
{ "color": { "h": 0, "s": 100 } }
:::

![content: Unified Light Data](help/images/data_light_json.jpg)

#### Smart Light Grid Arrays [badge: Homey Pro]

The **Smart Light Grid** widget can control multiple lights at once without needing an advanced flow. Instead of binding each tile manually, you can optionally bind the Grid to a Homey variable [badge: Homey Pro] containing a JSON Array of these state objects. Turn off **Color/White Indicators** in the widget settings if you want a cleaner tile without the small color or white-light preset markers.

::: code-block Light Grid State Array
[
 { "state": "ON", "brightness": 255 },
 { "state": "OFF" },
 { "state": "ON", "color": { "h": 120, "s": 100 } }
]
:::

*For complex widgets, see [Graph Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/graph-data-formats) or [List / Log Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/list-log-data-formats).*

widgetSubpages.title: Load & Filter iCal: Filtered Events (JSON)
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
The **Load & filter iCal** flow card downloads a calendar feed and outputs a **Filtered Events (JSON)** flow tag. This tag contains all matching appointments within your selected date window, ready to be converted into Markdown or parsed in custom Homey Scripts.
:::

When building flows, you normally pass this tag directly into the **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** card. If you prefer to write custom automation logic in **Homey Script**, you can parse this tag with `JSON.parse(...)` to access the date window and the list of event objects.

The **Combine calendar events** card uses the exact same data structure, outputting a merged and sorted **Combined Events (JSON)** tag.

In each event object, `startDate` and `endDate` are provided as standard ISO timestamps. Convenient helper flags are also included to identify all-day, multi-day, or recurring events.
::: code-block Example (shortened)
{
 "filterStart": "2026-05-01T00:00:00.000Z",
 "filterEnd": "2026-05-07T23:59:59.999Z",
 "events": [
 {
 "title": "Team meeting",
 "startDate": "2026-05-02T14:00:00.000Z",
 "endDate": "2026-05-02T15:00:00.000Z",
 "uid": "event-uid@example.com",
 "allDay": false,
 "calendarId": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
 "isTimed": true,
 "isAllDay": false,
 "isMultiDay": false,
 "isRecurring": false,
 "calendarEventKind": "timed",
 "calendarEventBlock": 2
 }
 ]
}
:::

#### Root object

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `filterStart` | Start of the filter window (ISO string, UTC). |
| `filterEnd` | End of the filter window (ISO string, UTC). |
| `events` | Array of events that overlap the window after expansion. |

#### Each event (common keys)

| Key | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `title` | Event title from the feed (SUMMARY). |
| `startDate`, `endDate` | Start and end instants (ISO strings in JSON). |
| `uid` | Stable iCal UID for the series or instance. |
| `allDay` | `true` for all-day (date-only) events. |
| `calendarId` | Short id derived from the feed URL (for “color by calendar source” in app settings). |
| `rrule` | Recurrence object when the master had a rule. This is often `null` on single expanded instances. |
| `recurrenceId`, `recurrenceStart` | Override / exception wiring from iCal (often empty on simple events). |
| `status`, `sequence` | iCal STATUS and SEQUENCE values. |
| `exDates`, `rDates` | Exclusion and extra-date lists from the component (may be empty arrays). |
| `isTimed`, `isAllDay`, `isMultiDay`, `isRecurring` | Dashboard Studio flags describing how the row behaves in tables. |
| `calendarEventKind` | Summary label for styling: `timed`, `all_day`, `multi_day`, or `recurring`. |
| `calendarEventBlock` | Block index `1` to `4` for color-block tables (maps to event type unless overridden by calendar source in app settings). |
| `multiDayAllDay` | Marks long all-day spans that cross calendar days. |

*Optional keys may appear depending on the feed (recurrence metadata, etc.). Treat unknown keys as forward-compatible.*

widgetSubpages.title: Graph Data Formats
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Graphs](help/images/header_graphs.jpg)

::: lead
[The Graph widget](help://Widgets/graph) supports **Live Streaming** (append one value at a time) and **Snapshot Mode** (replace the whole series in one payload).
:::

### Quick field guide

Object-array points use short keys. Use the right key for the job:

| Key | Meaning | Used when **X Axis Format** is… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **`v`** | Plotted value (required on object points) | Always (this is the Y value) |
| **`l`** | Text label for the X tick | **Text Labels** |
| **`t`** | Timestamp (ISO date/time string) | Date and time formats. Also **Datapoints** and **Text Labels** when **Linear Time Scale** is on |

Rules that matter most:

* **`l` is for words** (month names, categories, room names). **`t` is for real timestamps**, not display text.
* With **Text Labels**, only `l` is shown. Missing or empty (`""`) `l` leaves that tick blank.
* With a **date / time** format, only `t` is shown. Missing, empty, or non-date `t` leaves that tick blank.
* **Datapoints** shows the point index. With **Linear Time Scale** on, each point is placed by its timestamp.
* Prefer standard JSON with **double quotes** (`"l": "jul"`). Single quotes often work, but double quotes are the reliable form.

Enable **Show X Axis** whenever you want those ticks visible.


### 1. Live Stream (Single Point)

Sending a single number appends it to the graph history buffer and records the time that number arrived. With **Show X Axis** on, a date or time **X Axis Format** (**Date**, **Date Hours**, **Hours**, **Hours:Minutes**, or **Hours:Minutes:Seconds**) shows that time under the point. **Linear Time Scale** places each point by its timestamp, including when **X Axis Format** is **Datapoints**. A quiet gap stays empty on the chart.

*Settings:* **Buffer Size (Stream)** sets how many points are kept. **Scroll Direction** controls which side new points enter from.

::: code-block
24.5
:::


### 2. Simple Array (Snapshot)

A plain list of numbers. Replaces the entire graph. X ticks use the point index unless you switch to object arrays with `l` or `t`.

::: code-block
[10, 15, 12, 18, 20, 22, 19]
:::


### 3. Object Array (`v`, optional `l`, optional `t`)

Each item is an object. **`v`** is required. **`l`** and **`t`** are optional and can appear on the same point, or only on some points.

::: code-block
[
  { "t": "2024-01-01T08:00:00Z", "l": "heater", "v": null },
  { "t": "", "v": 100 },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T10:05:00Z", "l": "Other", "v": 105 },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T10:10:00Z", "v": 105 },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T12:00:00Z", "l": "", "v": null }
]
:::

**X Axis Format** picks which optional field is drawn:

* **Text Labels** → `l` only (time ignored)
* **Date / time formats** → `t` only (labels ignored)
* **Datapoints** → index only

**Sort order:** If every point has a valid timestamp in `t`, the widget sorts chronologically (same idea as Homey Insights). If any `t` is missing, empty, or not a real date, the payload order is kept.

**Empty Y values:** Use JSON `null` for `v` when there is no measurement (not zero). The X slot stays, but line / fill / bar / point drawing skips that slot so the stroke breaks at the gap.

* `"v": null` before the first reading in a range
* `"v": null` after “now” on a **Today** Insights chart
* Stable Insights readings often repeat the same numeric `v` across timestamps (forward-filled by the flow card)


#### Text labels only (sparse months, categories, …)

Put category text in **`l`**, not in `t`. Omit `l` (or use `""`) on points that should have no tick text.

Set **X Axis Format** to **Text Labels**.

::: code-block
[
  { "l": "jul", "v": 90.56 },
  { "v": 91.88 },
  { "v": 91.55 },
  { "l": "aug", "v": 88.97 },
  { "v": 89.38 },
  { "l": "sep", "v": 90.49 }
]
:::

::: alert warning
**Common mistake:** Putting month names or categories in `t` (for example `"t": "jul"`). **`t` is only for timestamps.** Those strings will not appear under **Text Labels**. Use `"l": "jul"` instead.
:::


#### Time-value (Homey Insights)

The **Homey Insights [badge: Homey Pro]** flow card sends `{ "t", "v" }` objects (no labels). That is the same object-array format with only timestamps and values. [badge: Homey Pro]

Set **X Axis Format** to a date / time option (not **Text Labels**).

::: code-block
[
  { "t": "2024-01-01T08:00:00Z", "v": null },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T10:00:00Z", "v": 100 },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T10:05:00Z", "v": 105 },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T10:10:00Z", "v": 105 },
  { "t": "2024-01-01T12:00:00Z", "v": null }
]
:::

You can publish the same shape from MQTT, Node-RED, or Homey Script.


### 4. Categorized Data (object map)

Send a JSON **object** whose keys are labels and whose values are heights. This replaces the whole series.

Works with any chart type; especially clear for **bar** charts comparing categories.

Set **Show X Axis** on and **X Axis Format** to **Text Labels**. Order follows the object key order.

Use `\n` inside a key for a multi-line label (handy for a second line such as a percentage).

::: code-block
{
  "Solar\n(22%)": 3.2,
  "Grid\n(38%)": 5.4,
  "Battery\n(10%)": 1.5,
  "Heating": 4.1,
  "Lighting": 0.8,
  "Other": 1.2
}
:::

*Settings:* Keep **X Axis Fixed Width** at `0` to size the label area automatically, or set a fixed height to clip overflow.

The same result as an object array of `{ "l", "v" }` points (section 3 without timestamps).


---


### Advanced Graph Formatting

#### Axes & Labels
::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **X Axis Format:** Choose **Datapoints** (index), **Text Labels** (`l`), or date / time formats (`t`). Empty `l` or `t` values leave that tick blank.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Axis Fixed Width:** Auto-reserves space from label size when set to `0`. A fixed value forces the boundary and can clip overflow.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Y-Axis Scale Mode:** Select **Fit Data Range (Exact Min/Max)**, **Clean Steps (1, 2, 5...)**, or **Whole Numbers Only (Counts)**.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Positioning (Offset X/Y):** Fine-tunes the plot area position and axis label offsets.
:::

#### Data Rendering & Smoothing
::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Dynamic Floor / Ceiling:** Automatically adjusts the axis bounds to your data. Turn off to configure strict, **Fixed Floor** or **Fixed Ceiling** bounds.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Baseline Value:** Sets where the fill starts (useful for import and export power charts).
* [button ph-check-square] **Smooth Line:** Enables a monotone cubic curve that stays within peaks and valleys.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Smoothing Amount:** Visual smoothing from 0 to 100. Higher values flatten trends without changing the stored payload.
:::

*Empty slots (`v: null`):* Gap in the series; line and fill break instead of dropping to zero.

#### Charts & Grids
* **Negative values (bar charts):** Show below baseline, mirror upward, or hide. Dedicated negative colors available.
* **Grid lines:** Horizontal grids support distinct top, bottom, and baseline strokes plus inner lines. Vertical grids follow your X-axis interval.

widgetSubpages.title: List / Log Data Formats
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
The **List / Log** widget displays structured lists of items with optional icons, timestamps, and interactive checkboxes. It supports multiple input formats and can also act as an interactive checklist that publishes its state.
:::

### Input Formats

#### 1. Simple Text (Log Mode)

Sending a plain string adds it to the **top** of the list. Older items are removed when the "Max Lines" limit is reached. Strings may include **line breaks** so a single log entry can span multiple rows.

::: code-block Simple String
"Motion detected in Garden"
:::

#### 2. Pipe-Delimited String

Use the `|` character to include an icon and/or a checked state in a single string. All four formats below are supported:

| Format | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `"Front Door Open"` | Unchecked, no icon |
| `"ph-warning\|Front Door Open"` | Unchecked, with warning icon |
| `"true\|Front Door Open"` | Checked, no icon |
| `"true\|ph-warning\|Front Door Open"` | Checked, with warning icon |

::: code-block Example
Description: A pre-checked item with a WiFi icon.
"true|ph-wifi-high|Network: Online"
:::

#### 3. JSON Array (List Mode)

Sending a JSON array **replaces the entire list**. Each item is an object. All fields are optional except `text`.

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | String | The display text (required). May contain line breaks for multi-line rows. |
| `checked` | Boolean | Initial checkbox state (default: false) |
| `icon` | String | Phosphor icon name (e.g. `ph-wifi-high`) |
| `timestamp` | Number | Unix timestamp in milliseconds |

::: code-block Full Example
[
 { "checked": true, "icon": "ph-wifi-high", "text": "Network: Online" },
 { "checked": false, "text": "Backup: Pending" },
 {
 "icon": "ph-warning",
 "text": "Old Event",
 "timestamp": 1709550000000
 }
]
:::

::: code-block Minimal Example
Description: Items with no icon or timestamp, which is the simplest use case.
[
 { "text": "Feed the cat" },
 { "text": "Turn off lights" },
 { "text": "Lock the door" }
]
:::

#### 4. Raw Data Mode

Enable **Raw Data** in widget settings to display any value as plain text, including complex JSON objects, without any parsing.

---

### Interactive Checklist

Enable **Show Checkboxes** in the **Appearance** section to turn the list into an interactive checklist. Users can tap items to check/uncheck them.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Checkboxes:** Turn the list into an interactive checklist where users can tap items to check or uncheck them.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Checkbox Alignment:** Place checkboxes on the Left or Right side of each row.
* [button ph-check-square] **Read Only:** Shows checkboxes but prevents user interaction.
* [button ph-check-square] **Strikethrough (Checked):** Adds a strikethrough and dims checked items.
* [button ph-star] **Icon Style:** Customize **Default Row Icon**, **Icon (On)**, and **Icon (Off)** (Phosphor style, size, colors, and optional custom image URL per slot).
:::

---

### Output & Trigger Topics

The list can publish its state back to Homey. Set an **Output Topic** and configure when to publish using **Output Mode**.

| Output Mode | When it fires |
| --- | --- |
| **On Trigger Topic Only** | Only fires when a message arrives on the *Trigger Topic*. Use this for a "Submit" button pattern. |
| **On Any Change** | Fires instantly on every checkbox click, incoming data update, or external trigger command. |

#### Output Formats

| Format | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **JSON Array (Objects)** | Rich objects with checked, text, icon, and timestamp. Recommended. | [See below](#list-output-json) |
| **Boolean Array** | A simple array of true/false values per item. Useful for simple automation. | `[true, false, true]` |

::: code-block JSON Array (Objects): Output #list-output-json
Description: Optional fields (icon, timestamp) are only included when present. Received as a string, which can be parsed with JSON.parse() in your automation platform.
[
 { "checked": true, "icon": "ph-wifi-high", "text": "Network: Online" },
 { "checked": false, "text": "Backup: Pending" },
 { "checked": false, "icon": "ph-warning", "text": "Old Event", "timestamp": 1709550000000 }
]
:::

#### Trigger Topics

In addition to the main Trigger Topic, three special control topics are available:

| Topic Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Trigger Topic** | Receiving any value on this topic fires the output publish immediately. |
| **Trigger Topic: Select All** | Marks all items as checked. Publishes immediately if Output Mode is "On Any Change". |
| **Trigger Topic: Deselect All** | Marks all items as unchecked. Publishes immediately if Output Mode is "On Any Change". |
| **Trigger Topic: Delete Selected** | Permanently removes all currently checked items from the list. Publishes the new list if Output Mode is "On Any Change". |

::: alert info info
**Tip: Use Local Topics for Dashboard Buttons** 

To wire a Button or Switch widget to any trigger topic (Select All, Deselect All, Delete Selected, or Trigger), use a `local/` topic, for example, `local/checklist/select_all`. Local topics stay entirely within the dashboard and do not require a platform connection or flow.
:::

::: alert info memory
**Persistent State via Variable [badge: Homey Pro]** 

For reliable state persistence across reloads and app updates, bind **Data (String/JSON)** in the **Data & Behavior** section to a Homey text variable (e.g. `homey/event/my_checklist`), and set the **Output Topic** (under **Output & Trigger**) to the same address. Then create a flow: 

**WHEN** "Dashboard Studio `my_checklist` triggered" **THEN** set Homey variable [badge: Homey Pro] *my_checklist* to the *Value (String)* tag. 

Every change the user makes is saved to the variable and automatically restored when the page reloads. No reliance on the cache, which is cleared on every app update.
:::

::: alert info arrow-square-out
**Retrieving List State from a Flow [badge: Homey Pro]** 

A flow can request the current list state at any time by sending any value to the configured **Trigger Topic**. The widget will immediately publish the full current state to the Output Topic, which your flow can then read via the trigger card's *Value (String)* tag.
:::

::: alert info shield-check
**Loopback Protection:** 

If your *Output Topic* and *Data (String/JSON)* binding point to the same topic, the widget automatically detects its own echo using a content fingerprint (based on item timestamps) and avoids re-publish, preventing an infinite loop.
:::

### Timestamps

Enable **Show Timestamp** under **Appearance**. Each item uses its own embedded timestamp (from JSON input), or the time it arrived for pipe-string input. Format options live in the **Timestamp Format** slideout:

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Time Format:** Choose between Hours:Minutes or Hours:Minutes:Seconds.
* [button ph-check-square] **24 Hour Clock:** Off for 12h (AM/PM), on for 24h format.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Date Format:** Select DD-MM, DD-MM-YYYY, MM-DD, MM-DD-YYYY, or None.
:::

![content: List Widget Example](help/images/list_widget.jpg)

*For static multi-line text blocks, use the [Text widget](help://Widgets/text) instead.*

widgetSubpages.title: Markdown Formatting Reference
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead Use the following syntax in the **Text Content** field to format your text. ::: Use the following syntax in the **Text Content** field: | Element | Syntax | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | **Header 1** | `# Text` | `# Welcome Home` | | **Header 2** | `## Text` | `## Living Room` | | **Header 3** | `### Text` | `### Camera Feed` | | **Bold** | `**text**` | `**Status: Armed**` | | **Italic** | `*text*` or `_text_` | `_Standby_` | | **Strikethrough** | `text` | `Out of order` | | **Blink** | `[blink]text[/blink]` or `[blink 1.5]text[/blink]` | `[blink]Door open[/blink]` | | **Unordered List** | `- Item` or `* Item` | `- Lights\n- Blinds` | | **Ordered List** | `1. Item` | `1. Open Gate\n2. Turn on lights` | | **Table** | `\| Col 1 \| Col 2 \|` `\| --- \| --- \|` `\| Val 1 \| Val 2 \|` | See demo dashboard | | **Table Cell Background (hex)** | `[cell #RRGGBB]` at cell start | `\| Room \| [cell #34FF1C]21 °C \|` | | **Table Cell Background (theme)** | `[cell @token]` at cell start | `\| Room \| [cell @accentSoft]21 °C \|` | | **Text Color (hex)** | `[color #RRGGBB]text[/color]` | `[color #34FF1C]**Live**[/color]` | | **Text Color (theme)** | `[color @token]text[/color]` | `[color @accentSoft]Warning[/color]` | | **Header in Table Cell** | `#` / `##` / `###` on its own `
` segment inside a cell | `\| Room \| ## Living
Details \|` | | **Block Callouts** | `[block1:text]` … `[block4:text]` | `[block1:Info]` or `[block3:Warning]` | | **Horizontal Rule** | `---` | `---` (On a separate line) | | **Image** | `![alt](url)` | `![Cam](local/cam.jpg)` | | **Image (width)** | `![alt\|240](url)` | `![Cam\|240](local/cam.jpg)` | | **Image (height)** | `![alt\|x180](url)` | `![Cam\|x180](local/cam.jpg)` | | **Image (width x height)** | `![alt\|240x180](url)` | `![Cam\|240x180](local/cam.jpg)` | | **Image Tint (hex)** | `![alt\|#RRGGBB](url)` | `![logo\|#ff8800](logo.svg)` | | **Image Tint (theme)** | `![alt\|@token](url)` | `![logo\|240\|@accent](logo.svg)` | | **Icon Tint (hex)** | `:ph-icon\|#RRGGBB:` or `:ph-duotone ph-icon\|#RRGGBB:` | `:ph-heart\|#ff8800:` | | **Icon Tint (theme)** | `:ph-icon\|@token:` or `:ph-duotone ph-icon\|@pri\|@sec:` | `:ph-duotone ph-android-logo\|@accent\|@danger:` | | **Link** | `[label](url)` | `[Router Admin](http://10.0.0.1)` | | **Help link** | `[label](help://Topic)` | `[Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge)` | | **Link (new tab)** | `[label](url ^)` | `[Manual](https://example.com ^)` | | **Inline Icon** | `:ph-icon-name:`, `:ph-icon-name|size:`, `:ph(ph-duotone ph-android-logo|size):`, or `:ph-duotone ph-android-logo|size:` | Legacy slug uses **Markdown Icon Style**. Append optional `|size` or `|color` (same pipe tint rules as images). Bracket or `:ph-` + weight + glyph sets explicit styles. Duotone accepts two colors for primary and accent layers. | | **Live Topic** | `{{topic/path}}` | `{{homey/temp}}` | | **Payload Formula** | `{{if({{homey/temp}} > 20, "hot", "cold")}}` | Same language as Binding Options | | **Line Break** | Press Enter once | (Forces a new line within the same block) | | **Line break (single line)** | `\n` (backslash + letter n) | `\| A \| B \|\n\| --- \| --- \|\n\| 1 \| 2 \|` | **Single-line markdown:** Type `\n` where you would press Enter. The text widget turns each `\n` into a line break so tables, lists, and headings work in one line. This is useful for topic-bound **Text Content**, `{{topic}}` values, or button **On/Off Value** payloads. #### Payload formulas [See live formula examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=18) [muted: (demo, page 18)] Wrap a [Payload Formula](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas#writing-formulas) in the same `{{ }}` braces as a live topic. Put `{{topic/path}}` references inside the expression (inline formulas use topic references, not the **Value** chip). Join quoted prefixes and suffixes with `+`. The result is inserted as markdown, so icons, tables, and `[color]` spans render as usual. ::: code-block {{if({{homey/temp}} > 20, "hot", "cold")}} {{round({{homey/temp}}, 1)}} {{if({{state}} == "on", ":ph-flame:", ":ph-snowflake:")}} {{if(containsanycase({{device/state}}, "ON"), "On", "Off")}} {{"/images/home-night-" + {{local/climate}} + ".png"}} ::: Use `==` when the topic sends text such as `on` or `heating`. **contains()** matches the exact letter case. **containsanycase()** treats `ON`, `On`, and `on` as the same. `Hello the value is ON` matches both. Formula language, functions, and the 512-character limit match Binding Options. #### Icon and image sizing Add an optional pipe size after the label (pixels). Omit it to keep the default size (icons inherit text size; images use responsive width). * **Width only:** `|240` sets width to 240 px; the other axis scales proportionally. * **Height only:** `|x180` sets height to 180 px; width scales proportionally. * **Both:** `|240x180` sets width and height in px. Examples: * Image: `![Cam|240](local/cam.jpg)` * Image tint: `![logo|@accent](icon.svg)` or `![logo|240|#ff8800](icon.png)` * Icon: `:ph-cloud-sun|32:` or `:ph-duotone ph-android-logo|24:` or `:ph(ph-duotone ph-android-logo|32):` * Icon tint: `:ph-heart|@accent:` or `:ph-duotone ph-heart|@accent|@danger:` or `:ph-arrow-circle-down|32|#ff8800:` * Icon slug: use `:ph-cloud-sun|90:` (not `:ph-ph-cloud-sun|90:`). A leading `ph-` on the slug is accepted if duplicated. Works in table cells, block callouts, and `{{topic}}` payloads. #### Links opening in a new tab To open a Markdown link in a new browser tab, add a caret after the URL inside the parentheses. You may use a space before the caret (recommended for readability): `[Docs](https://example.com/page ^)`. Links written as `[Docs](https://example.com/page)` without the caret stay in the same tab as the dashboard. **rel="noopener noreferrer"** is applied automatically for new-tab links. #### Documentation links Use `help://` to open the in-app Documentation panel to a topic, subpage, or section. Encode spaces as `%20` or `+`. Encode `:` as `%3A` and `&` as `%26`. Add `#` plus a heading slug or an id such as `help-step-1`. Examples: * `[Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge)` * `[RSS News Reader](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/rss-news-reader)` * `[Homey step 1](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide#step-1-enable-devices)` * `[Homey step 1](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide#help-step-1)` A trailing `^` on a help link is ignored. Help links always open the Documentation panel. #### Image and icon tint Recolor a PNG or SVG silhouette (transparent background works best) by adding a color token in the alt pipe after the label. **Inline Phosphor icons** use the same pipe tokens on all three forms (`:ph-slug:`, `:ph-weight ph-glyph:`, `:ph(...):`). Size and tint tokens can appear in any order. Tint uses the same hex/rgb/hsl and `@theme` tokens as text color and table cell backgrounds. Inline icon tints override **Markdown Icon Color** in the editor. **Images:** * `![logo|@accent](icon.svg)` tint only * `![logo|240|#ff8800](icon.png)` width and tint * `![logo|@accent|120x80](icon.svg)` tint and explicit size **Icons:** * `:ph-arrow-circle-down|@accent:` single-color tint (duotone sets both layers uniform) * `:ph-duotone ph-android-logo|@accent|@danger:` primary and accent duotone layers * `:ph-cloud-sun|32|#ff8800:` size and tint (non-duotone ignores a second color) Tint replaces image colors with a flat fill. Full-color photos become a solid silhouette. In the **Full editor**, use **Image URL** to set optional Width, Height, and Tint when inserting. #### Text color Wrap any inline text in `[color spec]text[/color]` using a hex/rgb/hsl color or a theme token such as `@accentSoft` or `@markerTint1`. Works in paragraphs, headers, tables, block callouts, and `{{topic}}` payloads. * `[color #34FF1C]**Live**[/color]` in a paragraph or table cell * `# [color @markerTint1]Title[/color]` for a colored heading line * `[cell @surfaceAlt][color @text]21 °C[/color]` combined with table cell background In the **Full editor**, use **Text color** (the **A** with a color bar, after **Italic**) when text is selected. Theme tokens follow **Theme Colors** when the dashboard theme changes. Use **Clear** in that picker to remove the wrapper. Color overrides the typography role color for wrapped text; size and weight still come from the role. #### Table cell background At the **start** of a table cell, add a color prefix (optional space after `]`). Use a hex/rgb/hsl color or a theme token such as `@accentSoft` or `@markerTint1`. The rest of the cell is normal markdown. * `| Living room | [cell #34FF1C]21 °C |` * `| Garage | [cell @accentSoft]:ph-warning: Offline |` * `| Spare | [cell @markerTint2] |` (background only) In the **Full editor**, use **Table cell background** (the paint bucket with a color bar, next to **Insert table**) when the cursor is inside a table cell. Theme tokens follow **Theme Colors** when the dashboard theme changes. Use **Clear cell background** in that picker to remove the prefix. #### Table alignment (GFM) In the table **separator line** (the `| --- |` row right below the header), you can control alignment per column: * `---` = Default * `:---` = Left aligned * `:---:` = Center aligned * `---:` = Right aligned In the **Full editor**, use the column alignment buttons next to **Insert table** when the cursor is inside a table. **Override:** You can override GFM alignment in two ways: * **Text & Typography → Table Header / Table Text alignment:** choose **Table-Defined** to honor `:---`/`:---:`/`---:`, or choose **Left**/**Center**/**Right** to force a fixed alignment. * **Text Settings → Horizontal Alignment:** choose a specific alignment to override everything, or set it to **Use Typography Settings** to use per-role settings from **Text & Typography**. #### Block callouts Use `[block1:text]` … `[block4:text]` (case-insensitive) to render tinted callout blocks. The four block colors can be adjusted in the editor under **Markdown** (**Block 1 Color** … **Block 4 Color**). For table styles, column widths, element colors, typography, and the Full editor, see the [Text widget guide](help://Widgets/text).

widgetSubpages.title: Icons & Images
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Media](help/images/header_media.jpg)
### Icon Picker

::: lead
Dashboard Studio ships the full **Phosphor Icons** catalog (thousands of icons). Open the browser, type keywords to filter, and scroll to browse. Search updates as you type.
:::

1. Click the icon input field in any widget settings.
2. The **Icon Browser** will appear.
3. Type to search (e.g., "sun", "wifi", "battery").
4. Click an icon to apply it.

When adjusting a bound **Icon Color**, the color popover stays open while you fine-tune the value (some browsers previously closed it too early).

![content: Icon Browser](help/images/media_icon_browser.jpg)

### Custom Images

Most widgets (like Gauge, Switch, and the Image widget) support custom image URLs.

* **Web URLs:** Use any public HTTPS link (e.g., `https://example.com/my-icon.png`).
* **Homey gallery picker:** On Homey, image URL fields show a gallery button beside the box. Click it to pick or upload a file into Image widget **URL** / **Fallback URL**, dashboard **Background Image URL**, or a custom icon **Image URL**. See [Image Gallery Manager](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager#insert-from-a-field). [badge: Homey Pro]
* **Local Images:** If you are familiar with hosting files on Homey (e.g., via the Image Grabber app or FTP), you can use local paths.
* **SVG:** The Image widget can load **SVG** URLs directly (including simple SMIL animation where the browser allows it).
* **Timed refresh:** The Image widget can reload its URL on a timer. See [Live Camera Feeds](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/live-camera-feeds) for snapshot-style camera use.
* **Fallback URL:** In the Image widget’s **Data & Source** section, set an image to show when the primary **URL** fails (broken link, MQTT value, or a failed **Enable Live Refresh** tick). Default is `images/brokenlink.png`. Clear **Fallback URL** to show nothing instead of an error overlay.

#### Masking (Colorizing Images)

If you upload a black PNG icon with a transparent background, enable **Tint with icon color** in the icon style settings (under **Icon** or a menu row’s icon controls) so the dashboard can re-color the image dynamically (e.g., turning a custom lamp glyph yellow when on).

![content: Custom Image Settings](help/images/media_custom_image.jpg)

### Related topics

* [Image Gallery Manager](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager) for files hosted on Homey.
* [Image widget](help://Widgets/image) for URL, SVG, and live refresh.

widgetSubpages.title: Colors
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
**Theme Colors** are the named colors of your dashboard. Refer to one with a **theme token** such as `@accent`. The token follows **Theme Colors** in **Dashboard Settings**, so a theme change updates every place that uses that token.
:::

Type a theme token in any color field, send it as a topic value, or return it from a [Payload Formula](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas#color-fields-payload-formula). Markdown text color, table cell backgrounds, and image or icon tints accept the same tokens. The color picker lists these names when you pick a theme color.

A theme token starts with `@` and the token name, for example `@warning`. Hex, RGB, HSL, and named CSS colors stay fixed. A theme token stays linked to the theme.

topics.title: Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)
topics.content:
![header: Data & Topics](help/images/header_data.jpg)

::: lead
Dashboard Studio routes live data through **topics**: dedicated communication channels for your devices, capabilities, variables, flows, and moods. Devices publish instant status updates so your bound widgets always stay in sync, while interactive controls publish commands straight back to turn lights on, adjust variables, trigger flows, or set room moods.
:::

### Homey: Enabling Capabilities [badge: Homey Pro]
![content: Homey App [badge: Homey Pro] Configuration](help/images/homey_config_app.jpg)

To keep your dashboard responsive, organized, and tailored to your home, Dashboard Studio lets you choose exactly which capabilities you want to use. In the Homey app, open **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration** and expand each device to select only the capabilities you need.

**Enabled** capabilities immediately create topic communication so your dashboard widgets can display live data and send commands. Leaving unused capabilities unchecked keeps your setup clean, conserves valuable hub memory and network bandwidth, and provides an extra layer of protection by exposing only the features you intend to display.

All regular smart home devices, including lights, smart plugs, climate controls, sensors, curtains, and media players, connect and work out of the box without requiring any special key or setup.

### Read, Write, and Read/Write

Capabilities vary depending on what they do. Some are **read-only** (sensor measurements), some are **write-only** (action triggers), and many support **both** (such as light switches and thermostats). The editor displays this right next to topic names with clear badges:

::: access-legend
* [access: R] **Read only**: The dashboard displays values from this topic. Binding it to a control that publishes data will have no effect.
* [access: W] **Write only**: This is useful for command-style topics. There might be nothing to display until your logic sends data.
* [access: RW] **Read / write**: State flows in and your widget can push changes back on the same topic.
* [access: L] **Local**: The topic starts with `local/` and never leaves the browser.
* [access: F] **Flow**: Tied to Homey Flow [badge: Homey Pro] event topics (for example `homey/event/…`).
:::

Pay close attention to these badges when picking a topic so you do not bind an interactive slider or switch to a read-only channel.

### Variables, Flows, and Moods (Personal API Key) [badge: Homey Pro]

While your physical devices and sensors work straight away, Homey protects system-level logic by requiring administrator permissions for direct write and trigger actions. Adding an optional **Personal API Key** unlocks full two-way control for three specific features:

* **Writing to User Variables:** Editing numeric, text, or boolean Homey Logic variables directly from input widgets like edit boxes, switches, or sliders ([access: RW]). Without a key, variables are read-only ([access: R]).
* **Starting Flows:** Running Standard or Advanced Flows directly from a dashboard button or switch using the `start` capability ([access: W]).
* **Activating Zone Moods:** Triggering mood lighting scenes directly from dashboard widgets.

If you only monitor sensors, control regular physical devices, or read variable values, you do not need an API key at all.

![content: Homey Personal API Key Permissions](help/images/homey_api_key_dialog.jpg)

#### Creating a Personal API Key

To generate your key in Homey:

1. Open the **Homey Web App** at `my.homey.app` in your web browser.
2. Click the gear icon in the bottom left corner to open **Settings**.
3. Select **API Keys** in the sidebar.
4. Click **New API Key** and enter a friendly name (for example `Dashboard Studio`).
5. Select the permissions for the features you want to use:
   * **Variables** (`homey.logic`): Grants read and write access to User Variables.
   * **Flows** (`homey.flow.start` and `homey.flow.readonly`): Grants permission to start flows and read their state.
   * **Moods** (`homey.mood.set` and `homey.mood.readonly`): Grants permission to set and read zone moods.
6. Click **Save** and copy the generated key to your clipboard.

#### Adding the Key to Dashboard Studio

1. In the Homey app, navigate to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings** tab.
2. Paste your copied key into the **Personal API Key** input field.
3. Click outside the input box or press tab. Dashboard Studio verifies your key immediately with Homey.
4. Active permission indicators update right below the field:
   * **Variables**: Green badge confirms write access to Logic variables is active.
   * **Flows**: Green badge confirms flow starting access is active.
   * **Moods**: Green badge confirms zone mood control is active.

#### Enabling Items in Configuration

Once your key is verified, open the **Configuration** tab in **Settings → Dashboard Studio**. Scroll down past your devices to the **System & Automation** section:

* **User Variables:** Toggle on any variable you wish to publish. With a verified key, variables gain full two-way editing ([access: RW]). Without a key, they remain read-only ([access: R]).
* **Flows:** Standard and Advanced Flows appear grouped by their folders. Enable the flows you want to trigger from the dashboard. With start permissions, flows expose the `start` capability ([access: W]). If your key has view-only permissions, flows display as read-only ([access: R]).
* **Zone Moods:** Moods are neatly grouped under their active zones (for example Living Room or Kitchen). Enable any mood to expose it as a direct action topic for your dashboard buttons.

Click **Save Settings** at the bottom of the page to apply your selections.

::: alert info timer
**Protection Cooldowns for Flows and Moods**

To protect Homey from accidental overload and prevent rapid repeat triggers, Dashboard Studio applies built-in cooldowns:
* **Flows:** A **10-second cooldown** applies per flow before it can be started again.
* **Moods:** A **3-second cooldown** applies per mood before it can be activated again.

This safeguards your system against unintentional user mistakes, such as accidentally binding a flow trigger to a constantly moving slider or a rapidly updating sensor topic.
:::

### Custom Topic Names

You are never limited to the suggestions in the dropdown. Type any **unique** name into the topic field and confirm it to create a custom binding. Stick to simple characters including letters, digits, `/`, `_`, and `-`. **Avoid spaces** completely so names copy cleanly into Flow cards, MQTT, and logs.

### Binding in the Editor

Click the **Link Icon** :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400: beside a setting to bind it. The field turns cyan and actively follows the topic. Open the **Arrow** :ph-bold ph-caret-down text-cyan-500: in the field for a quick list, or open the **Data Stream Explorer** under **⚙️ Dashboard Settings** to monitor live traffic and copy topic names. Once bound, an **Options Icon** :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: may appear. Click it to open **[Binding Options](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas)**: set a default when the topic is empty, map custom words to on/off states, or transform numerical values with a formula. See the full guide in [Binding Options & Payload Formulas](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas). Master settings support the same bindings as individual widgets.

### Global vs. Local Topics

**Global** topics reach your platform driver ([badge: Homey Pro], MQTT, Node-RED, etc.). Use them for physical devices and system variables. **Local** topics always begin with `local/` (for example `local/menu_status`) and securely stay inside the browser for lightning-fast UI wiring between widgets. Always prefer `local/` when external hub traffic is unnecessary.

### Keeping Multiple Tabs in Sync
**Enable Topic Auto-Echo** (on by default in the Homey App [badge: Homey Pro] settings) rebroadcasts widget output across all open sessions. This ensures every browser tab viewing the same dashboard stays perfectly synchronized. Turn it off only if you intentionally desire isolated, independent dashboard instances.

### Flows and Automation

Topics connect seamlessly to Homey Flows [badge: Homey Pro] and external automations. Flows can trigger when a dashboard topic fires, or they can push values into topics that the dashboard displays. Detailed walkthroughs are available in the [Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide) and [Homey Flow [badge: Homey Pro] Cards](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards).

topics.title: Widgets
topics.content:
::: lead
Widgets are the pieces you place on your dashboard: menus, gauges, buttons, text blocks, and more. Each one has its own settings in the editor sidebar, grouped into slideouts (for example **Data & Behavior**, **Appearance**, **Icon**, and **Text & Typography**).
:::

### How to add a widget

1. In **Create Widget**, pick a type from the dropdown.
2. Click **Add**. In **Fixed Resolution** or **Scale to Fit Screen** the widget appears in the center. In **Responsive Columns** it takes the next grid **Order**.
3. Bind topics in the inspector :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400:. See [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor).
4. Apply a [preset](help://Widgets/presets) for a finished look, or open **Advanced** slideouts to fine-tune.

If a group is open, **Add** places the widget inside that group.

### Basic Settings and Advanced

**Editor Mode** in **Editor Environment** controls how much of the inspector you see. The same slideout holds **Quick Toolbar**, snap grid, and **Widget Labels In Editor Canvas**. See [Editor Mode](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode).

* **Basic** shows **Widget** (name, visibility, page, presets) plus **Basic Settings** (size or responsive cell, **Widget Label**, **Show Container**, and the essentials for that type). Style comes from [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets).
* **Advanced** shows every slideout. Use **Show Advanced Settings** / **Force Basic Settings** on one widget when you need the other tier.

Geometry follows [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes): X/Y/Width/Height in Fixed and Scale, **Responsive Layout & Dimensions** in Responsive Columns.

### Master settings (defaults for everyone)

Many options have defaults that apply to all widgets of a type until you change them locally. You edit those under **master / global settings** (the same place you set theme-wide typography and colors). When you add a new widget, it starts from those defaults. You can still override anything on the widget itself.

To open those default settings: **click empty space on the canvas** (no widget selected), *or* with a widget selected, open the widget dropdown at the top of the sidebar and choose **:ph-bold ph-gear: Dashboard settings**.

Several widgets also have an **Audio** slideout. File hosting and topic triggers are documented in [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery).

### See widgets in action

The built-in **demo** dashboard includes a page full of sample widgets so you can compare types and layouts.

[Open the widget demo gallery](?dashboard=demo&page=4) [muted: (`?dashboard=demo&page=4`)]

### Widget Guides

::: grid
* [button ph-table]
**[Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets)**
Reusable look and behavior packs for one widget type.

* [button ph-arrow-right]
**[Arrow / Line](help://Widgets/arrow)**
Static separators or animated data-flow paths.

* [button ph-battery-charging]
**[Battery](help://Widgets/battery)**
Charge, tank, or fill-level indicator.

* [button ph-clock]
**[Clock](help://Widgets/clock)**
Analog, flip, or text time and date.

* [button ph-squares-four]
**[Container](help://Widgets/container)**
Background frame or labeled card for layered layouts.

* [button ph-chat-teardrop-text]
**[Dialog Box](help://Widgets/dialog-box)**
Shared confirmation overlay for switches and buttons.

* [button ph-textbox]
**[Edit Box](help://Widgets/editbox)**
Type and send text or numbers to a topic.

* [button ph-gauge]
**[Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge)**
Round or bar readout for a numeric value.

* [button ph-chart-line]
**[Graph](help://Widgets/graph)**
Line, bar, or live plots of changing data.

* [button ph-star]
**[Icon](help://Widgets/icon)**
On/off glyph, image, or blink indicator.

* [button ph-image]
**[Image](help://Widgets/image)**
Photos, SVG, or snapshot camera refresh.

* [button ph-text-t]
**[Label](help://Widgets/label)**
Lightweight text caption with auto-fit dimensions.

* [button ph-lightbulb]
**[Light Grid](help://Widgets/lightgrid)**
Multi-light tiles with a color and brightness panel.

* [button ph-list-dashes]
**[List / Log](help://Widgets/list)**
Scrolling log, feed, or checkbox list.

* [button ph-list]
**[Menu](help://Widgets/menu)**
Navigation list, dropdown, or slide-out panel.

* [button ph-sliders-horizontal]
**[Slider](help://Widgets/slider)**
Drag a numeric value such as brightness or volume.

* [button ph-toggle-left]
**[Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch)**
Toggle, push button, page jump, or URL.

* [button ph-text-t]
**[Text](help://Widgets/text)**
Markdown text, tables, and live placeholders.
:::

### Related topics

* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide) for selecting widgets and using the sidebar.
* [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes) for Fixed, Scale, and Responsive Columns.
* [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets) for applying and saving looks.
* [Styling & Layering](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering) for colors, z-order, and **Show Container**.
* [Icons & Images](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/icons-images) for icons and pictures on widgets.
* [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery) for clips on Homey and per-widget audio.
* [Tools](help://Tools) for extra editor scripts, including the [Widget Preset Editor](help://Tools/widget-preset-editor).

widgetSubpages.title: Widget Presets
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Editor Interface](help/images/header_editor.jpg)

::: lead
A **widget preset** is a reusable pack of look and behavior for one widget type. Apply it to style a new widget in one step, or save your own pack to Homey.
:::

In **Basic** [Editor Mode](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode), presets are the primary way to style widgets. **Basic** keeps essentials visible. Style comes from the pack you apply. **Layout Mode** (Fixed, Scale, or Responsive) is a separate canvas choice. See [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes).

Presets skip position, lock, page, visibility, name, and data bindings. Those stay on the widget.

### Apply a preset

Select a widget. In the **Widget** inspector section, use **Presets**.

A preset only writes **included** (checked) settings. Those values replace the matching fields on the widget. Unchecked settings keep the widget's previous value.

* Homey **My Presets** appear first (A to Z), then built-in presets.
* Previous and next buttons step through the list.
* When a preset file has two or more variants, a **sub-preset** dropdown appears on the row below. Previous and next on that row step through variants. Choosing a main preset applies its first variant.

### Save, Export, Import, Reset

These actions sit under the dropdown (**Advanced** editor mode).

::: grid
* [button ph-cloud-arrow-up] **Save:** Stores the preset on Homey under **My Presets** for this widget type. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-download-simple] **Export:** Downloads a `.json` preset file.
* [button ph-folder-open] **Import:** Loads a preset file. Multi-variant files ask which sub-preset to apply.
* [button ph-arrow-counter-clockwise] **Reset to Default:** Clears preset style and behavior on this widget. Size is kept.
:::

### Save dialog

**Preset Name** and **Preset Sub Name (optional)** are type-or-pick fields. Pick an existing **My Preset** to fill the sub list, or type a new name.

Choose what to store:

* **All changed settings** stores every value that differs from the factory default. In the editor, those altered fields show a **blue outline**, so you can see what will be stored.
* Only the **checked** (included) items in a preset overwrite the widget. Unchecked settings stay as they are on that widget.
* **Custom selection** opens a settings tree. Check the leaves you want. **Match Selected Preset** checks the same leaves as the preset currently selected in the list.

On Homey, matching an existing name switches the primary button to **Overwrite**.

### Widget Preset Editor

Open **Tools** (hammer) → **[Widget Preset Editor](help://Tools/widget-preset-editor)** to edit factory packs and **My Presets** in a multi-column grid, choose which settings each variant includes, and save or export the result.

### Related topics

* [Widget Preset Editor](help://Tools/widget-preset-editor) in [Tools](help://Tools) for the spreadsheet workspace.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode) for **Create Widget** and **Editor Mode**.
* [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes) for Fixed, Scale, and Responsive Columns.
* [Styling & Layering](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#1-the-styling-cascade-master-vs-local) for master colors versus a preset on one widget.

widgetSubpages.title: Arrow / Line
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Arrow / Line](help/images/widget_arrow.jpg)

::: lead
The **Arrow / Line** widget is a highly versatile graphic element used to draw animated data flows, static separators, or complex custom vector paths directly on your dashboard. Whether you need a simple straight line to divide content or a multi-point animated flow to visualize energy moving from your solar panels to your battery, this widget handles it natively without requiring external images.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=9) [muted: (demo, page 9)]

### 1. Creating Static Lines & Separators
One of the most common uses for the Arrow widget is to simply draw a static dividing line between other widgets (often requested as a "separator" widget on the forums).

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Head Size:** Set to `0` to remove the arrowhead and create a standard line.
* [button ph-check-square] **Enable Animation:** Toggle animated flow along the line. Disable this under Animations & Effects for static dividers.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Thickness & End Cap Radius:** Adjust line stroke thickness and corner rounding for rounded or square tips.
* [button ph-palette] **Main Color:** The primary color stroke of the separator line.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Pro Tip:** Once you've styled a static line to your liking, use the duplicate button to quickly stamp out multiple identical separators across your dashboard.
:::

### 2. Custom Path Geometry
The Arrow widget supports multi-point paths, allowing you to draw right-angled or complex flowing shapes.

::: grid
* [button ph-crosshair] **Start & End Points:** Drag the cyan crosshair handles in the editor to visually position the start and end coordinates.
* [button ph-plus] **Corner Points:** Inserts intermediate joints into the line to create bends. Drag the created handles to position them.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Corner Radius:** Natively rounds sharp joints, creating a smooth sweeping path between points instead of a harsh zigzag.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Head Round:** Rounds off the sharp corners of the arrowhead itself.
:::

::: alert warning gauge
**Performance Consideration:** Adding custom corner points switches the rendering pipeline. A straight line uses a highly optimized, fast-mode CSS gradient animation. A curved line with custom points relies on SVG masks and native Gaussian blurs to animate the flow around bends. This is visually striking but has a higher GPU impact, especially on older tablets.
:::

### 3. Animated Flows
The Arrow widget excels at visualizing data movement, such as energy, water, or network traffic.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Enable Animation:** When enabled, the secondary Flow Color slides continuously along the path.
* [button ph-check-square] **Reverse Flow Direction:** Reverses the animation direction. The arrowhead automatically jumps to the opposite end.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Flow Width & Gradient Width:** Controls the size and softness of the moving flow segment.
* [button ph-palette] **Flow Color:** Sets the moving gradient color. Can be dynamically bound to a device topic.
:::

::: alert info magic-wand
**Editor Tip:** In View mode, the Arrow widget completely ignores pointer events (clicks pass through it), meaning you can safely layer large background arrows across your entire canvas without blocking the buttons underneath. In Edit mode, the widget catches clicks so you can select and adjust it.
:::

### 4. Glow Effects
You can apply a native drop-shadow to the entire path to create a neon or glowing aesthetic.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Glow:** Enables the outer glow drop-shadow effect along the entire line path.
* [button ph-palette] **Glow Color:** The color of the glowing halo. Can be bound to dynamic states.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Glow Width & Opacity:** Sets the blur spread width and transparency of the glow.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Battery
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Battery](help/images/widget_battery.jpg)

::: lead
The Battery widget is a versatile graphical indicator for charge levels. It can display continuous fluid levels or segmented blocks, automatically change colors when critically low, and display a charging state icon. While designed for device batteries, it can also be used creatively as a generic capacity or fill-level visualization.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=15) [muted: (demo, page 15)]

### 1. Data & Behavior

Link your device capabilities to these core data properties to animate the widget in real-time.

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **% Value:** The primary fill level of the battery (`0` to `100`). Values outside this range are visually clamped so the battery fill never exceeds its casing.
* [button ph-check-square] **Charging State:** A boolean (`true` or `false`) toggle. When active, a prominent charging icon :ph-bold ph-lightning: is overlaid on the center of the battery body.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Low Threshold:** The percentage at or below which the battery fill color switches from the normal Good state to the Low warning state (defaults to `20`).
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Not just for batteries**
The widget can act as a generic tank or capacity indicator. You can feed it any 0–100 percentage value, such as a water tank level, storage drive capacity, or goal progress.
:::

### 2. Appearance

The physical shape and coloring of the battery can be heavily customized to match your dashboard's theme or mirror specific physical devices.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Vertical Mode:** Toggles the battery orientation from the default horizontal layout to a vertical layout with the terminal at the top.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Segments (0=Solid):** By default, the battery fill is a continuous solid block. Entering a number greater than 0 (such as `4` or `5`) divides the interior into individual discrete cells.
* [button ph-palette] **Good Color:** The interior fill color when the value is strictly above the Low Threshold.
* [button ph-palette] **Low Color:** The interior fill color when the value drops to or below the Low Threshold.
* [button ph-palette] **Border Color:** The color of the battery's outer casing and the positive terminal.
* [button ph-palette] **Empty Color:** The color used for depleted segments when Segments is greater than `0`.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Outline Width:** The thickness of the battery's outer border.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Inner Padding:** The gap between the outer casing and the inner fill.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Terminal Size:** The width (or height, if vertical) of the positive contact node protruding from the battery.
:::

::: alert info magic-wand
**Displaying the exact numeric percentage**
The Battery widget visually represents the charge level, but it skips automatically print the numeric percentage on the screen. Because Dashboard Studio functions like a design tool with pixel-perfect layering, you can easily show the exact value: just create a separate **Text** widget, bind it to the same battery data topic, set its background to *Disabled*, and drag it directly over the battery's casing.
:::

### 3. Text & Typography

Add an optional text label to identify the device or sensor.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Text:** The string to display above the battery. If left blank, the label container collapses and takes up no space.
* [button ph-text-t] **Widget Label:** Comprehensive typography panel to style the text font family, size, color, alignment, casing, and Offset X/Y.
:::
By leaving instance-level overrides blank or unchanged, you can restyle every battery on your dashboard simultaneously simply by adjusting the global master settings.
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Full:** Plays audio when the battery reaches 100% capacity.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Empty:** Plays audio when the battery reaches 0% capacity.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Charging:** Plays audio when the charging state becomes active.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Stop Charging:** Plays audio when the charging state turns off.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Clock
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Clock](help/images/widget_clock.jpg)

::: lead
The Clock widget displays the current time and date in three highly customizable formats: an analog clock face, an animated flip clock, or a structured text readout. It runs autonomously in the browser, providing precise, localized timekeeping without relying on MQTT updates.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=14) [muted: (demo, page 14)]

### 1. Display Modes

The widget operates in one of three primary **Types**, selected from the **Type & Time** section:
::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Type:** Choose between **Analog Clock** (classic watch face with hands), **Flip Clock** (animated retro split-flap display), or **Date Time Text** (flexible typographic date and time readout).
:::

### 2. Time Source & Timezones

By default, the Clock uses the viewing device's local system time. You can decouple it from the local device to show the time in another region:
::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Use system time:** When disabled, the Timezone dropdown becomes available to select a specific IANA timezone.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Timezone:** Select a specific IANA timezone (such as `Europe/Amsterdam` or `America/New_York`).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Manual time offset:** Applies a manual offset in minutes to the displayed time.
* [button ph-check-square] **12-hour clock (AM/PM):** Available for Flip and Date Time Text modes. Displays hours in 12-hour format with an AM/PM indicator.
:::

::: alert info magic-wand
**Smooth Sweeping in Custom Timezones**
Dashboard Studio leverages modern browser APIs (`fractionalSecondDigits`) to ensure the analog second hand sweeps perfectly smoothly, even when decoupled from the local system time and forced into a custom timezone.
:::

### 3. Analog Face & Hands

When set to **Analog Clock**, two new configuration sections appear:
::: grid
* [button ph-palette] **Analog Face:** Toggle Show Ticks and Show Numbers, and adjust Number Distance %, Cap Size, and dial colors.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Hands & Sweep:** Configure the Width and Length % of the Hour, Minute, and Second hands independently.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Sweep Mode:** Choose **tick** for distinct 1-second jumps, or **smooth** for a continuous sweeping second hand.
:::

### 4. Flip Clock Configuration

When set to **Flip Clock**, the **Flip Clock** section provides deep aesthetic control over the animated cards:
::: grid
* [button ph-palette] **Upper / Lower Card Colors:** Set distinct colors for the top and bottom halves of the flip flaps.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Card Roundness & Separator:** Control the flap corner radius and the pixel gap between cards.
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Labels:** Toggles the small unit captions (such as Hours, Minutes) beneath each card.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Language / Locale:** Translates the default unit labels into your chosen language using the browser Intl engine.
* [button ph-textbox] **Custom Labels:** Enter explicit custom strings in Custom Hour, Minute, and Second Label fields.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Responsive Sizing**
The Flip Clock automatically scales its cards to fit the widget's bounding box on the dashboard grid. To make the numbers larger, increase the widget dimensions, and adjust the **Flip numbers** font size in the **Text & Typography** section.
:::

### 5. Date Time Text Layout

The **Date & Time** section offers granular control over exactly what time and date information is shown:
::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Time Controls:** Toggle Show Hour, Show Minute, and Show Second, customize Time Separator Character (default `:`), and toggle Blink Separator.
* [button ph-textbox] **Date Separator Character:** Optional character placed between date parts (for example `/` for `22/8/2026`). Leave empty to keep a space between parts.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Date Segments:** Configure up to 5 sequential date parts (**Date Part 1** through **5**) including Day of Month, 2-Digit Day (for example `08`), Number of Month, 2-Digit Month, Name of Month, Name of Day, Week Number, and Year Long. Set unused parts to None.
* [button ph-check-square] **Line Break After Date:** Forces the time readout onto a new line below the date string.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Language / Locale:** Automatically translates month and weekday names according to the selected locale.
:::

### 6. Typography & Nesting

Like other modern Dashboard Studio widgets, the Clock uses **nested typography** (`overrides.typography`). All font sizes, families, alignments, and colors are managed in the **Text & Typography** section. The available typography slides dynamically update based on the chosen Display Mode:
- **Analog numbers**: Styles the numbers around the analog dial.
- **Flip numbers**: Styles the large digits on the flip cards.
- **Flip labels**: Styles the small "Hours/Minutes" text below the flip cards.
- **AM / PM**: Styles the AM/PM indicator on the flip clock.
- **Time & Date**: Styles the unified text readout in Date Time Text mode.

### 7. Global Clock Defaults

Almost every clock setting, from the timezone and display mode to the flip card colors and typography, is linked to a **Master Setting**. This means you can drop a factory default Clock onto your dashboard, and it will immediately adopt the global clock styles defined in your dashboard's master configuration, keeping all clocks visually consistent.
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Every Second:** Fires an audio clip once per second.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Every Minute:** Fires an audio clip at the start of each minute.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Every Hour:** Fires an audio clip at the top of the hour.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Every Day:** Fires an audio clip once per day at midnight.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Container
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Container](help/images/widget_container.jpg)

::: lead
The Container widget is a versatile layout element that serves as a blank canvas or a visual grouping mechanism for other widgets. It is a fundamental building block for designing complex, layered dashboard interfaces.
:::

### 2. Grouping & Layering
The true power of the Container widget shines when you combine it with multiple other widgets to create custom composites.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Design Tip:**
You don't have to try to fit every visual element into a single widget's settings. For example, to build a highly customized climate panel, place an empty Container on the canvas. Then, drag Graph, Text, and Slider widgets on top of it. Uncheck **Show Container** on the top widgets, and use the underlying Container to frame the entire composition seamlessly. In **Responsive Columns**, **Group** those widgets and set **Scale Mode** to **Rescale** so the panel scales as one cell. See [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes#combined-widgets-groups).
:::

### 3. Text & Typography
The Container features a built-in title section, making it perfect for creating labeled cards (e.g., "Living Room", "Thermostat", or "Energy").

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Text:** The main title displayed at the top of the container. If left blank, the container acts purely as a visual block.
* [button ph-text-t] **Typography:** Fully customizable font family, size, color, case formatting, and alignment.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Positioning (Offset X / Offset Y):** Adjust Offset X and Offset Y to fine-tune exactly where the label sits within the box, independent of container padding.
:::

### 4. Appearance & Styling
Because the Container inherits from the application's base widget architecture, you have full control over its aesthetics via the standard **Appearance** properties.

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Padding:** Adjusting padding is crucial to creating clean whitespace between the container edges and the widgets placed inside it.
* [button ph-palette] **Backgrounds:** Set a solid background color, apply a dynamic color based on data, or use a background image.
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Container:** Uncheck to make the container completely transparent while keeping its structural grouping or title.
* [button ph-check-square] **Visibility:** Bind the visibility of a Container to a data topic or Homey variable [badge: Homey Pro] to dynamically show or hide the visual grouping based on real-time states.
* [button ph-palette] **Translucency & Blur:** Fade the background gradient with **Start Opacity** and **End Opacity**, and frost whatever shows through it with **Background Blur**.
* [button ph-palette] **Inner Glow:** Paint a soft halo inside the container edge. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Inner Glow Color** and **Inner Glow Opacity**.
:::

For a frosted-glass panel, combine a translucent background with **Background Blur** and a soft light **Inner Glow**.

::: alert info magic-wand
**Layering Trick:**
When building complex interfaces, uncheck **Show Container** on top-layered widgets so the underlying Container acts as a unified backdrop for your custom control panel.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Dialog Box
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Dialog Box](help/images/widget_dialog.jpg)

::: lead
The **Dialog Box** is the shared confirmation overlay for your dashboard. Set the message, buttons, and look once. A [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#3-confirmation-dialog) can show it before an action runs. When the overlay is open, the confirm button is already selected. Left and Right move between the buttons. Enter runs the selected button.
:::

Open it from **Dashboard Settings**: click empty canvas, or pick **Dashboard Settings** in the widget dropdown. **Dialog Box** sits under **Master Widget Settings**, just below **Container Style**.

### 1. Message and buttons

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Message:** The question on the overlay. Line breaks stay visible.
* [button ph-textbox] **Confirm Label & Dismiss Label:** The two button captions (defaults `Yes` and `No`).
* [button ph-palette] **Button Color:** Background color for the confirmation and dismissal action buttons.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Button Roundness:** Corner radius for both action buttons.
* [button ph-check-square] **Auto Button Size:** On by default. Turn it off to set manual Button Width and Button Height.
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Button Icons:** Adds a Confirm Icon and Dismiss Icon on the buttons (defaults are `ph-check` and `ph-x`).
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Dialog Icon:** Adds a Dialog Icon beside the message (on by default). Size defaults to `50`. Other icon settings follow Icon widget defaults.
:::

### 2. Panel look and placement

::: grid
* [button ph-palette] **Background Color & Borders:** Customize Background Color, Border Color, Border Width, Border Opacity, and Corner Radius. Empty radius, border width, and opacity follow Container Style.
* [button ph-check-square] **Auto Dialog Size:** On by default. Turn it off to set manual Dialog Width and Dialog Height.
* [button ph-check-square] **Center Dialog:** Keeps the overlay in the middle of the canvas. Turn it off to set manual Dialog X Position and Dialog Y Position.
* [button ph-check-square] **Modal Mode:** In view mode, dims and locks the canvas until the user chooses Confirm or Dismiss.
:::

In [Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns) the overlay stays centered.

### 3. Typography

::: grid
* [button ph-text-t] **Dialog Text:** Styles the overlay message typography. Unset values follow Label Defaults Label Typography.
* [button ph-text-t] **Button Label:** Styles the Confirm and Dismiss button captions. Unset values follow Switch Inside the Button typography.
:::

### 4. Use it on a Switch / Button

1. Select a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#3-confirmation-dialog).
2. In **Data & Behavior**, turn on **Require Confirmation**.
3. Open **Confirmation Dialog Appearance** to override the look for that widget only. Unset fields keep these Dialog Box defaults.
4. Use **Preview in Edit Mode** to place and resize the overlay on the canvas. Confirm and Dismiss do not run the action in the editor.

**Toggle Switch** asks when turning On. Check **Confirm When Turning Off** if Off should wait too. **Push Button** always asks on the press (or completed hold).

For a fully custom overlay made of your own widgets, see [Confirmation Dialogs](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/confirmation-dialogs).

### Related topics

* [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#3-confirmation-dialog) for **Require Confirmation**.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-dialog-box) for where **Dialog Box** sits in Dashboard Settings.
* [Confirmation Dialogs](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/confirmation-dialogs) for a custom teleport overlay.
* [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns) for Responsive Columns centering.

widgetSubpages.title: Edit Box
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Edit Box](help/images/widget_editbox.jpg)

::: lead
The Edit Box widget allows you to create interactive text input fields on your dashboard. Use it to send custom string payloads, numbers, or multi-line messages directly to an MQTT topic.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=10) [muted: (demo, page 10)]

### 1. Data & Behavior
The **Data & Behavior** section controls how the Edit Box captures and transmits user input.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Input Mode:** Choose between **Single Line** (standard text input) or **Multi-Line** (textarea where users can press Shift+Enter for new lines).
* [button ph-caret-down] **Send Behavior:** Determines when the payload is published: **Live (On Type)** (with 300ms debounce), **Keyboard (Enter)**, **Keyboard (Enter) & Exit**, **Trigger Topic**, or **Open URL**.
* [button ph-broadcast] **Output Topic:** The MQTT topic where typed text is published.
* [button ph-broadcast] **Trigger Topic:** The MQTT topic that triggers the send action when Send Behavior is set to Trigger Topic.
* [button ph-check-square] **Clear on Send:** Automatically clears the input field immediately after the payload is transmitted.
* [button ph-textbox] **Custom Placeholder:** Faded text shown when the input is empty. Defaults to a smart placeholder based on Send Behavior and Input Mode.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Form Tabbing & Batch Sending**
Windows users often prefer using the `Tab` key to navigate between input fields. If you are building a data-entry form with multiple Edit Boxes, you can set them all to **Keyboard (Enter) & Exit**. When a user tabs out of an Edit Box, its content is sent immediately. 
*Note: Tabbing order currently follows the exact order the widgets were created in.*

Alternatively, if you want to submit all fields at once, set all Edit Boxes to **Trigger Topic**, point them to a single trigger, and use a Button widget to fire that trigger!
:::

### 2. Appearance
The **Appearance** section allows you to style the input container, borders, and focus states.

::: grid
* [button ph-palette] **Background Color & Opacity:** Sets the background fill of the input field. Lower the opacity to create semi-transparent glass inputs.
* [button ph-palette] **Border Color, Width & Radius:** Controls the solid border and corner radius around the input field.
* [button ph-check-square] **Enable Focus Glow:** When enabled, clicking into the Edit Box applies a highlighted border and outer glow effect.
* [button ph-palette] **Focus Glow Color:** The color of the focus ring and border when the input is active.
:::

### 3. Text & Typography
The **Text & Typography** section manages the visual styling of both the descriptive label and the actual text you type.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Widget Label:** Optional text displayed directly above the input field. Leave blank to hide the label entirely.
* [button ph-text-t] **Widget Label Typography:** Full control over the label font, size, color, case, and alignment.
* [button ph-text-t] **Input Text Typography:** Controls the styling of the text typed inside the box.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Text Padding:** Adjusts the internal spacing between text and the input border.
* [button ph-palette] **Placeholder Color:** Sets the specific color of the empty placeholder text.
:::

::: alert info magic-wand
**Read-Only in Edit Mode**
To prevent accidental keystrokes while you are designing your dashboard, the Edit Box is completely disabled (read-only) while in Edit Mode. You must exit Edit Mode to test typing and sending payloads.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Gauge
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Gauge](help/images/widget_gauge.jpg)

::: lead
The **Gauge** widget is a versatile data visualization tool that displays a numeric value along a defined scale. It supports round and horizontal bar styles, multi-color gradients, custom baselines, and highly customizable typography for captions, values, units, and axes.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=6) [muted: (demo, page 6)]

### 1. Data & Behavior
Use this section to define the numeric bounds and formatting of your gauge:
::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Value:** Bind this to a numeric capability (such as Temperature, Power, or Dim level).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min / Max:** Define the physical minimum and maximum values for the gauge track.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Decimal Places & Zeros:** Control how many decimals to show, and whether to keep trailing zeros.
* [button ph-check-square] **Abbreviate Large Values:** Automatically shorten large numbers (such as `1.5k` or `2M`) to keep the dashboard clean.
* [button ph-check-square] **Custom Display Range:** Decouples the physical gauge track from the displayed text value (for example mapping raw 0-255 sensor data to a 0-100% display readout).
:::

When bound, use the faders icon :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: on **Value** to open [Binding Options & Payload Formulas](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas).

### 2. Appearance
The Appearance section controls the shape, layout, and colors of the gauge.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Style:** Choose between **Round**, **Horizontal**, or **None** (hides the track completely, displaying only text and icon).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Bar Width & Track Width:** Set the thickness of the active bar and the background track.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Size Adjustment & Gap:** Scale the gauge within its container and control spacing between bar and text.
* [button ph-palette] **Start, Middle & End Colors:** Set multi-color gradient points along the gauge bar.
* [button ph-check-square] **Solid color at value:** When enabled, the bar fills entirely with the single color corresponding to the current value's position on the gradient instead of drawing the gradient.
* [button ph-palette] **Track Color, Opacity & Outline:** Customize the empty track background color with **Track Color** and **Track Opacity**, plus the outline stroke with **Outline Width**, **Outline Color** and **Outline Opacity**.
* [button ph-palette] **Track Blur & Inner Glow:** Frost the backdrop behind a translucent track with **Background Blur** on the round arc and the horizontal bar. **Track Inner Glow** adds a soft glow that follows the track. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Track Inner Glow Color** and **Track Inner Glow Opacity**.
* [button ph-palette] **Bar Opacity, Outline & Inner Glow:** Fade the active bar with **Bar Opacity**. Stroke it with **Bar Outline Width**, **Bar Outline Color**, and **Bar Outline Opacity**. **Bar Inner Glow** paints a soft halo inside the bar edge. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Bar Inner Glow Color** and **Bar Inner Glow Opacity**. **Bar Outline Color** and **Bar Outline Opacity** stay hidden until **Bar Outline Width** is above `0`. The track outline does the same.
* [button ph-check-square] **Bar Glow:** Add a neon glowing effect around the active bar.
