* [button ph-number-square-five] **Baseline Value:** Change where the gauge starts filling from (default fills from Min). Setting a custom baseline allows the bar to grow upwards for positive values and downwards for negative values.
* [button ph-check-square] **Axis Labels & Ticks:** Automatically generate ticks and numbers along the track with Target Tick Count, Label Offset, and Scale Mode (Fit Data Range (Exact Min/Max), Clean Steps (1, 2, 5...), Whole Numbers Only (Counts)).
:::

Lower **Track Opacity** below `100` to let the blur show the frosted backdrop. Appearance settings left unset use the Gauge master defaults. Combine a translucent track with **Background Blur** and a soft light inner glow for a frosted-glass gauge.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Tip on Spacing:** If you notice too much white space between the value and a round gauge, decrease the **Gap** setting. If you haven't overridden it on individual widgets, you can adjust the *Default Round Gap* in the master Global Settings to fix it across your entire dashboard at once.
:::

### 3. Icon
The Gauge widget features a single customizable icon slot.
::: grid
* [button ph-star] **Icon Slot:** Select a built-in Phosphor icon or provide a custom image URL.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Icon Base Size & Offsets:** Adjust the icon size and X/Y offsets to position the icon beside your value.
:::

::: alert info magic-wand
**Creating an Animated Warning Gauge:** The Gauge widget skips have built-in threshold warning animations (like blinking red when a value is too high) to prevent overcomplicating its settings. 

However, you can easily build this yourself! Simply place an **Icon** widget directly on top of your Gauge widget, giving it the same icon and size but selecting a 'filled' weight and enabling the 'Blink' animation. Hide the background of the Icon widget in its Container settings, and bind its visibility to your high/low threshold logic in Homey. You can even disable the icon on the base Gauge widget so that only the animated overlay handles the icon.
:::

### 4. Text & Typography
The Gauge widget provides robust, independent typography controls for four distinct text elements:
::: grid
* [button ph-text-t] **Caption, Value, Unit & Axis Labels:** Dedicated typography slideouts to adjust font family, size, color, bold, italic, opacity, and offsets independently for each role.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Text Position:** Control where the text block sits relative to the gauge bar (**Bottom**, **Top**, **Left**, or **Right**).
* [button ph-caret-down] **Value Horizontal Alignment:** Control the alignment of the entire value block within the widget (**Left**, **Center**, or **Right**).
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Smart Alignment Defaults:** The value alignment automatically defaults to `Center` when the Text Position is set to Top or Bottom. It defaults to `Left` when the Text Position is Left or Right. You can always override this manually if you want right-aligned text next to a left-aligned gauge.
:::

Each typography role (Caption, Value, Unit, Axis) has its own dedicated slideout where you can independently adjust the font family, size, color, bold, italic, opacity, and X/Y offsets. If a role's color or font is left unset, it gracefully falls back to the master Default Settings.
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Value Change:** Plays an audio clip whenever the bound gauge value updates.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Graph
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Graph](help/images/widget_graph.jpg)
::: lead
The **Graph** widget lets you plot and compare data series on a shared timeline. Whether you want to monitor room temperatures, track daily solar production against household power consumption, or see when your heating turns on and off, this widget turns raw numbers into clear, readable charts that match your dashboard styling.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=7) [muted: (demo, page 7)]

### Quick Settings Reference

::: grid
* [button ph-lightning] **Data & Behavior:** Manage graph series, data sources, topic connections, value multipliers, streaming buffer modes, time windows, and baseline limits.
* [button ph-palette] **Appearance:** Choose your visual style (Line, Smooth, Stepped, Bar, Text), set smoothing, bar spacing, **Graph Offset X** and **Graph Offset Y**, bar direction, and whether several bar series sit side by side or stack.
* [button ph-ruler] **Axes & Labels:** Set up scale modes, decimal formatting, large-value abbreviation, headroom, date/time formats, interval skipping, and axis titles.
* [button ph-grid-nine] **Grid Lines:** Style the background grid lines for value levels, time intervals, and the baseline.
* [button ph-hash] **Tick Marks:** Customize small tick mark strokes along axis borders, including size, thickness, and color.
* [button ph-dots-three-outline] **Points & Point Values:** Show dots on a line, and show numbers on the points or only while hovering.
* [button ph-list-bullets] **Legend:** Configure docking position, floating canvas coordinates, swatches, auto-sizing, and row or column layouts.
* [button ph-text-t] **Text & Typography:** Customize fonts, sizes, colors, and opacities for axis numbers, axis titles, legend items, point labels, and headers. **X Axis (Datapoints)** and **X Axis (Label)** are marked **Base Typography** because the matching Y axis copies them. Tick rotation is **Rotation** inside those axis groups. **Invert Y on Negative Values** places point numbers below negative points and above positive ones.
* [button ph-sparkle] **Animations & Effects:** Configure Draw In and Morph animations, adjust update durations, enable shimmer waves, and test live animation previews.
:::

---

### Quick Start: Creating Your First Graph
![content: Quick Start: Creating Your First Graph](help/images/graph_quick_start_creating_your_first_graph.jpg)

Setting up a graph takes just a few simple steps:

1. **Add the Widget:** Add a **Graph** widget to your canvas from the widget bar.
2. **Apply a Preset Look:** In the **Widget** section of the inspector, open **Presets** to choose a visual style like **Smooth Line Graph**, **Line Graph**, or **Bar Graph**. You can also choose curated sub-presets and style variants to quickly adjust line curves, fills, or bar themes. Presets set up colors, curves, and typography in one step without touching your data connections.
3. **Connect Your Data:** In **Data & Behavior**, open your graph card and select your data source. You can connect Homey capabilities, MQTT topics, Node-RED flows, or custom JSON streams. Click **Pick Live Values** to browse active device sensors and live feeds with mini preview charts. Click **Add Graph** whenever you want to plot multiple measurements on the same chart, such as comparing indoor and outdoor temperatures side by side.
4. **Fine-Tune Advanced Behaviors:** In **Data & Behavior**, open **Scale Range & Baseline** to fit the chart to your data, set a baseline, and choose how negative values are drawn. Open **Axes & Labels** to name the axes and format the numbers. In **Animations & Effects**, enable smooth draw-in or conveyor morphing. Use **Legend** to dock or float the companion list so viewers can toggle series on and off.

---

### Connecting Data & Understanding Formats
![content: Connecting Data & Understanding Formats](help/images/graph_connecting_data_understanding_formats.jpg)
Graphs support two different ways of handling data:

* **Live Streaming:** Ideal for live sensor readings. As new numbers arrive from Homey or MQTT, the widget records each reading at the current clock time and slides it along the timeline.
* **Snapshots & History:** Ideal for full historical datasets like Homey Insights or pre-formatted lists of numbers. The entire dataset is sent in a single update, and the widget draws the full curve at once.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Looking for payload details?**
For complete details on JSON shapes, CSV lists, and timestamp formatting for Homey Flows or Node-RED, take a look at the dedicated [Graph Data Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/graph-data-formats) guide.
:::

#### Scaling Units with Value Multiplier
Incoming sensor readings or network feeds often report numbers in milli, kilo, or mega units. When combined with other series on a shared timeline, unscaled numbers can push the entire chart way out of scale. With this feature you can correct this. Each graph card includes a **Value Multiplier** setting to scale numbers automatically:
* Enter `0.001` to convert Watts into Kilowatts (turning `2500` into `2.5`).
* Enter `0.01` to turn raw decimals into percentages.
* Enter `0` to keep values unchanged.

---

### Choosing the Right Visual Style
![content: Choosing the Right Visual Style](help/images/graph_choosing_the_right_visual_style.jpg)
The **Visual Type** setting in **Appearance** changes how your points are drawn:

* **Line & Smooth Line:** The natural choice for continuous sensor feeds like temperature, humidity, and battery levels. Use **Smoothing Amount** to create soft, silky curves without sharp angles.
* **Stepped Line:** Draws crisp right-angle steps between points. This is perfect for digital signals, relay states, window contacts, and thermostat target temperatures.
* **Bar Graphs:** Displays values as distinct columns. Set **Bar Direction** to **Vertical** for standard columns, or **Horizontal** for sideways bars. **Bar Series Layout** places multiple series **Side by Side** in each category, or **Stacked** on the same band. **Stacked Gap Step** narrows each bar drawn on top so the ones underneath stay visible. You can also provide custom labels for each individual bar directly inside the incoming data payload. For details on structuring your series array, see the [Bar Graph Data Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/graph-data-formats#3-object-array-v-optional-l-optional-t) guide.
* **Text Chart:** A compact mode that displays the latest numeric reading prominently in the center of the widget container.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Tip: Styling with Presets**
You can change the preset look of your graph at any time. Applying a preset updates visual styling, colors, and line shapes, but it preserves your configured data series, topic bindings, and custom graph names.
:::

---

### Managing Timelines & Streaming Buffers
![content: Managing Timelines & Streaming Buffers](help/images/graph_managing_timelines_streaming_buffers.jpg)
Under **Streaming Values** in **Data & Behavior**, you can control how many readings are kept in memory and how the timeline moves:

* **Buffer Mode:** Choose **Point Count** to keep the most recent number of samples (set by **Maximum Data Values**). Choose **Time Period** to retain data across a rolling time window like 1 hour, 24 hours, or 7 days.
* **Fixed Time Period:** When enabled, the visible graph always covers the full timeframe you selected. If your sensor only started reporting an hour ago on a 24-hour chart, the earlier hours remain cleanly empty. When disabled, the timeline expands dynamically to fit your available points.
* **Timeline Progress:** In a fixed time period, choose **Continuous Real Time** to let the timeline glide smoothly forward with your wall clock, keeping the right edge locked to right now. Choose **On New Value** if you only want the timeline to advance when a fresh reading arrives.
* **Reverse Direction:** Check this option to reverse the flow of time so the latest points enter from the left and scroll toward the right.
* **Line Gaps:** Choose **Break on Missing Time** to show a visible gap when a sensor goes offline or stops sending readings. Choose **Connect Points** to draw a continuous line between available points across quiet periods.

---

### Animations & Transitions

The **Animations & Effects** slideout lets you add smooth movement to your charts:

* **Draw In:** Sweeps lines smoothly across the screen from left to right and rises bars from the baseline when opening a page.
* **Morph & Extend:** Smoothly glides live incoming readings along the timeline conveyor and morphs curve points in place during updates.
* **Shimmer on Unchanged Data:** Plays a gentle highlight wave across the line when an identical reading arrives, giving you visual feedback that the sensor is still actively reporting.
* **Testing Your Look:** Use the **Preview Full Graph** and **Preview Stream Value** buttons in the inspector to test how your animation settings look without waiting for live sensor events.

---

### Scales, Limits & Friendly Axis Numbers

**Scale Range & Baseline** in **Data & Behavior** sets how high and low the chart reaches. **Axes & Labels** controls how those numbers are written.

#### Smart Vertical Limits
* **Dynamic Floor & Ceiling:** By default, the graph scales its limits to fit your actual data range. The floor tracks the lowest number across all graphs rather than forcing zero. This keeps tight ranges easy to read, such as room temperatures fluctuating between 19 and 22 degrees. Turn either toggle off to type your own **Fixed Floor** or **Fixed Ceiling**.
* **Use Baseline:** Places a highlighted reference line at a specific value, such as a comfort setpoint of `21` on a room temperature graph or a nominal `230` on a mains AC voltage monitor.
* **Negative Handling:** Choose **Show as Positive** to mirror negative values above the baseline, **Show as Negative** to draw them below the line, or **Ignore (Hide)** to omit negative points. Each graph card has a **Positive Line Color** and a **Negative Line Color**, plus **Positive Line Opacity** and **Negative Line Opacity**. Bar graphs use **Positive Bar Color**, **Negative Bar Color**, **Positive Bar Opacity**, and **Negative Bar Opacity**. The area under a line can use a separate **Positive Fill Color** and **Negative Fill Color**. Leave a fill color unset and it follows that side's line color. This makes it easy to visualize bidirectional power flows, such as displaying red positive bars for grid consumption (importing power) and green negative bars for solar feed-in (exporting surplus power).

#### Clean Numbers & Tilted Labels
* **Y Axis Scale Mode:** Choose **Clean Steps (1, 2, 5...)** to place grid lines on neat, round numbers. Choose **Fit Data Range (Exact Min/Max)** to stretch across your exact boundaries, or **Whole Numbers Only (Counts)** for integer increments.
* **Abbreviate Large Values (k, M):** Value-axis ticks of 1,000 and up show as thousands and millions, such as 12.5k or 3.2M. This is on by default. Turn it off when you want the full number.
* **Rotating Tick Labels:** Long dates can crowd a small graph. **Rotation** under **X Axis (Datapoints)** tilts the category ticks. **Rotation** under **Y Axis (Value)** tilts the value ticks. The margin grows so the words stay on the canvas. Horizontal bars rename those groups.

#### Axis Titles
In **Axes & Labels**, **X Axis Label** and **Y Axis Label** sit above **Show X Axis** and **Show Y Axis**. Type a name to draw it outside the tick labels, centered on that axis. Leave the field empty and the title stays hidden, with no extra margin.

**X Axis (Label)** in **Text & Typography** is marked **Base Typography**. **Y Axis (Label)** uses that style until you change a setting there. **Rotation** on **Y Axis (Label)** starts at `-90` degrees and does not copy the X axis title. When **Bar Direction** is **Horizontal** and you have not set a rotation, **Y Axis (Label)** stays at `-90` and **X Axis (Label)** stays at `0`.

When **Bar Direction** is **Horizontal**, these names swap so they match the axis you see.

---

### The Interactive Companion Legend
![content: The Interactive Companion Legend](help/images/graph_the_interactive_companion_legend.jpg)

The legend is a separate companion element that can dock along the edges of the graph or float freely on your canvas:

* **Docking vs Floating:** Set **Position** to **Right**, **Left**, **Top**, or **Bottom** to attach the legend to the graph edge. Set **Floating** to drag the legend anywhere on your canvas.
* **Drag to Detach:** You can drag a docked legend panel directly on the canvas. As soon as you move it, it automatically becomes a floating panel at the drop location.
* **Resizing:** Use the round edge and corner handles to resize a legend panel just like any other widget.
* **Click to Hide:** In viewer mode, clicking any graph name in the legend temporarily hides that line from the chart and instantly recalculates the scale across the remaining lines.
* **Matching Container Style:** The legend panel automatically shares the background blur, colors, border, and glow of the main graph widget.

---

### Usage with Homey Insights [badge: Homey Pro]

To display long-term historical logs from Homey, connect a **Homey Logic: Insight Card** to your graph widget. For step-by-step instructions on setting up flow cards to push historical data, visit the [Insights Flow Cards](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/insights) guide.

widgetSubpages.title: Icon
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Icon](help/images/widget_icon.jpg)

::: lead
The Icon widget is a highly versatile building block for displaying binary states, visual indicators, or interactive triggers. It supports dynamic colors, separate Active/Inactive glyphs, custom image URLs, and blinking animations.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=13) [muted: (demo, page 13)]

### 1. Data & Behavior

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Default State (On/Off):** Sets the initial state of the widget (`false` = Inactive, `true` = Active). Typically bound to a boolean device capability via MQTT or Homey.
:::

On bound boolean fields, open the faders icon :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: for [Binding Options & Payload Formulas](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas).

### 2. Icon States (Inactive & Active)

The widget separates its visual configuration into two distinct slideouts: **Icon** (Inactive) and **Active Icon**.

::: grid
* [button ph-star] **Inactive Icon & Active Icon:** The Inactive icon acts as the leader, while the Active icon inherits shape, weight, and offsets unless explicitly overridden.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Icon Source:** Choose between the built-in Phosphor icon library or a custom image URL (SVG or PNG).
* [button ph-check-square] **Tint with Icon Color:** When using a custom transparent image, enable this to apply your selected Icon Color to the image via a CSS mask.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Dynamic Color Binding**
You can change the color of an icon dynamically based on Homey flows [badge: Homey Pro]. Send a standard CSS color string (like `#FF0000` or `red`) to a custom topic (e.g., `WarningColor`), and bind that topic directly to the Icon's color property using the link icon.
:::

### 3. Appearance & Effects

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Icon Size:** Scales the icon in pixels. Inherits from global master settings if left untouched.
* [button ph-check-square] **Blink on Active:** When enabled, the icon pulses continuously when its state becomes Active.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Blink Speed (s):** Adjusts the animation cycle duration of the blink effect.
* [button ph-check-square] **Glow on Active:** When enabled (the default), the active state uses a drop-shadow glow matching the active color. Turn off to keep blink and colors without the glow.
:::

**Icon Size** and **Blink on Active** also sit in **Basic Settings**, beside **Default State (On/Off)**.

### 4. Text & Typography

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Caption:** Optional text displayed underneath the icon. Leave blank to use the widget purely as a standalone graphical icon.
* [button ph-text-t] **Typography Controls:** Fully customize the font family, size, color, case, and alignment of the caption through the nested typography section.
:::

::: alert info magic-wand
**Complex UI Layering**
Icons are excellent for creating rich composite visuals. You can layer icons over graphs, sliders, or empty containers. Uncheck **Show Container** to place the icon seamlessly over other widgets with pixel-perfect precision.
:::
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Activated:** Plays an audio clip when the icon state transitions to active.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Deactivated:** Plays an audio clip when the icon state transitions to inactive.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Image
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Image](help/images/widget_image.jpg)

::: lead
The Image widget is a highly versatile tool for displaying static images, live camera feeds, and animated vector graphics (SVGs). It features built-in support for live refreshing, smooth crossfade animations, fallback images, and full spatial control.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=13) [muted: (demo, page 13)]

### 1. Data & Source
This section defines where the image comes from and how frequently it updates.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Source Type:** Choose between **URL** (for standard images like PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP) and **Animated Vector Graphic (SVG)** (for raw SVG markup).
* [button ph-image] **URL:** The primary web address of the image. Can be bound to an MQTT topic to dynamically change the image. On Homey, use the gallery button in the field to insert `/images/<name>`.
* [button ph-image] **Fallback URL:** A secondary URL to display if the primary image fails to load.
* [button ph-textbox] **Raw SVG Code:** Available when Source Type is SVG. Enter raw SVG code directly here, or bind this field to an MQTT topic.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Opacity:** Sets the transparency level of the image (0-100%).
* [button ph-check-square] **Enable Live Refresh:** Automatically reloads the image at a specified interval (ideal for camera snapshots or radar images).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Refresh Interval / Interval Unit:** How often the image should reload (for example every 1 second, or every 10 minutes).
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Tip: Live Camera Streams & Radar**
To display a camera feed, use the camera's snapshot URL and enable **Live Refresh**. Set the interval to a low value like `0.5` or `1` second. The widget automatically bypasses browser caching by appending a unique timestamp to each request, creating a smooth, pseudo-video feed without the heavy overhead of an actual stream.

You can also use this for external sources, like a weather radar map (e.g., `https://api.buienradar.nl/image/1.0/RadarMapNL?w=720&h=600`), by setting the refresh interval to a few minutes.

::: alert info magic-wand
**Authentication for Local Cameras**
If your local camera snapshot requires a username and password, you can often include it directly in the URL using this format: `http://Username:Password@192.168.1.10:80/snap.jpg`.
:::

### 2. Appearance
Control how the image sits inside its container layout.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Fit Container:** If checked, the image stretches or shrinks to fill the widget's bounding box.
* [button ph-check-square] **Proportional:** Visible if Fit Container is enabled. Ensures the image maintains its aspect ratio without stretching.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Scale %:** Visible if Fit Container is disabled. Zooms the image in or out from its center point.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Move X / Move Y:** Nudges the image horizontally or vertically for precise cropping or alignment.
:::

### 3. Text & Typography
Every Image widget includes an integrated text label that renders securely on top of the image layer.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Text:** The caption label content.
* [button ph-text-t] **Typography Controls:** Standard font family, size, color, case, alignment, and Offset X/Y controls.
:::### 4. Animations & Effects
When the image source changes, either via a bound URL topic or during a live refresh cycle, you can apply a smooth transition.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Content Animation:** Choose the swap effect (such as **fade**, **slide**, or **scale**).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Animation Duration:** The length of the transition effect in seconds.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
The widget intelligently limits the maximum animation duration based on your Live Refresh interval. For instance, if you are refreshing the image every 1 second, the animation duration is capped at 0.9s to prevent overlapping transition glitches.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Label
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Label](help/images/widget_label.jpg)

::: lead
The **Label** widget is a lightweight, high-performance element for displaying plain text strings, captions, and titles. It renders pure text directly without running Markdown parsing or complex layout trees, making it the ideal choice for simple labels and annotations.
:::

### Label vs. Text Widget

Dashboard Studio provides two dedicated widgets for displaying text. Choose the one that matches your needs:

* **[Label](help://Widgets/label):** Renders plain text directly to the DOM using `textContent`. Because it skips Markdown compilation and HTML sanitization, it has minimal CPU overhead and virtually zero memory footprint. It is the recommended choice whenever you need a fast, simple caption, room name, or status label.
* **[Text](help://Widgets/text):** A full-featured Markdown display engine. It supports headings, bold and italic styles, bullet lists, tables, inline icons, custom colors, and live template placeholders with `{{topic}}`. This rich feature set requires full parsing and sanitization pipelines on every update.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Performance Recommendation**
When you simply need to place a title above a group of controls, show a sensor readout without formatting, or add quick static notes, prefer the [Label](help://Widgets/label) widget over the [Text](help://Widgets/text) widget. This keeps dashboards responsive, especially on low-power wall tablets and screens with dozens of active widgets.
:::

### 1. Text Settings

Configure the core text content and spatial orientation:

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Text:** The text string to display. Enter static copy, or bind to a live topic or Homey variable [badge: Homey Pro] to show dynamic text.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Vertical Alignment:** Aligns the text vertically within the widget box (**Top**, **Middle**, or **Bottom**).
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Rotation:** Rotates the entire text element in degrees (`-360` to `360`). Ideal for vertical card tabs, side headers, or diagonal badges.
:::

### 2. Layout & Dimensions

Adjust how the widget sizes itself relative to its text content:

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Auto Width (Fit to Content):** Automatically sizes the widget width to match the exact pixel width of the text. When disabled, the widget keeps its manually specified Width.
* [button ph-check-square] **Auto Height (Fit to Content):** Automatically adjusts the widget height to accommodate the text lines. When disabled, the widget keeps its fixed Height.
:::

In **Fixed Resolution** and in **Responsive Columns** using **Rescale** mode, auto-sizing lets you position quick labels without worrying about extra container padding or manual pixel clipping.

The same auto-size applies inside an open group. Closed-group Rescale and Resize use that fitted box, so the label keeps the same proportions as the text.

Label text stays on the lines you type. It does not wrap when the widget, column, or help panel gets narrower.

### 3. Text & Typography

The Label widget provides complete styling control through the nested typography system:

::: grid
* [button ph-text-t] **Label:** Opens the typography slideout to configure **Font Family**, **Font Size**, **Case** (UPPERCASE, Capitalize, lowercase, None), **Bold**, **Italic**, **Horizontal Alignment** (Left, Center, Right), **Color**, **Opacity**, and fine-tuning **Offset X** / **Offset Y** adjustments.
:::

Leaving any typography field blank or unset allows it to gracefully inherit your dashboard's global typography defaults.

### 4. Appearance & Container

Like other widgets, the Label widget inherits the standard container styling engine:

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Container:** By default, this option is turned off so labels sit cleanly on top of cards, images, or canvas backgrounds without an opaque border or card fill. Turn it on to give your label a distinct card background, border stroke, corner radius, or glow effect.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Padding:** Controls inner clearance around the text inside the container.
:::

### Related topics

* [Text](help://Widgets/text) for rich Markdown, tables, and inline icons.
* [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor) for binding labels to live sensor topics.
* [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes) for auto-sizing across Fixed, Scale, and Responsive layouts.

widgetSubpages.title: Light Grid
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Light Grid](help/images/widget_lightgrid.jpg)

::: lead
The Light Grid widget provides a compact, touch-friendly interface to manage multiple lights from a single dashboard component. It pairs a clean grid of on/off toggles with a universal, draggable Control Panel for adjusting brightness, colors, and temperature. You can also use it as a **button panel**: set a row's **Output Mode** to **Switch** to send On/Off values (or trigger page/URL actions) without opening the color panel.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=1) [muted: (demo, page 1)]

### 1. Overview & Philosophy

While Dashboard Studio is generally designed for broad, mood-based automation, the Light Grid exists specifically for manual light management. Each row in **Configured Lights** uses **Output Mode** **Light** by default (full light control with the Control Panel). Set **Switch** when you want a compact button that only publishes values to its output topics, similar to a Switch / Button widget tile in a grid.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Note:**
"This widget uses a grid of presets instead of a color wheel, as simple color and white-point tiles are much easier to touch on a wall tablet."
:::

### 2. Data & Binding ([Unified Light State](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state))

For rows in **Light** output mode, the Light Grid expects a **[Unified Light State](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state) (JSON)** payload on each row's output topics.

* **Capability Requirement:** In your Dashboard Studio app configuration on Homey, you must enable the **[Unified Light State](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state) (JSON)** virtual capability for the lights you wish to control. This ensures Homey translates the JSON output from the dashboard into the correct device-specific commands (hue, saturation, brightness, temperature, state).
* **Grouping Lights:** Each configured light in the grid can accept **multiple topics**. When you toggle a light or select a preset, the widget sends the exact same JSON payload to every topic listed for that light. This allows you to easily group multiple physical bulbs under a single grid tile without writing complex Homey flows [badge: Homey Pro].

**Pick Live Lights** opens the lights that are already publishing a Unified Light State. Each light shows its name, live color, and brightness. Lights already in this grid start checked and are marked **In Grid**. **Apply to Light Grid** adds newly checked lights as their own devices and removes lights you unchecked. A light that shares a device with other topics is taken off that device only. The rest of the device stays.

Check two or more devices, then press **Combine**, to move their topics into the device you choose. Open a device that has more than one output topic and press **Split into Its Own Device** to give that light its own row, using the light's name.

**Switch rows** do not require light JSON for display. They use a local **State (On/Off)** on the row and send your configured **On Value** / **Off Value** strings to the same **Output Topics** when tapped.

### 3. Switch Output Mode (Button Panel)

Use **Switch** when a row should behave like a dashboard button, not a full light controller.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Output Mode:** In **Configured Lights**, set **Output Mode** to **Switch** (default is **Light**).
* [button ph-check-square] **State (On/Off):** Sets the row's starting toggle position in the editor. Runtime toggle state is local to the row.
* [button ph-caret-down] **On Click:** **Send Topic**, **Go to Page + Topic**, or **Open URL + Topic**. Includes optional Target Page #, Target URL, and New tab when relevant.
* [button ph-textbox] **On Value / Off Value:** The payloads sent to output topics when the row turns on or off.
:::

**Color Presets** and **Override Master** are hidden in Switch mode (those apply only to Light rows). Tapping the tile or its toggle flips the row and sends the active value to all Output Topics without opening the Control Panel.

### 4. Tile Layout

The main visual component is a responsive grid of tiles.

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Tile Layout:** Configure **Columns**, **Item Height (px)**, **Item Width (px)**, and **Item Spacing (px)**. Leave a dimension at `0` for automatic sizing.
* [button ph-palette] **Tile Styling:** Under **Appearance**, customize **Tile Background Color**, **Hover Color**, and toggle colors for On vs Off.
* [button ph-palette] **Tile Opacity & Blur:** Fade tiles with **Tile Background Opacity**, and frost whatever shows through them with **Tile Background Blur**.
* [button ph-palette] **Tile Outline & Inner Glow:** Frame tiles with **Tile Outline Width**, **Tile Outline Color** and **Tile Outline Opacity**. **Tile Inner Glow** paints a soft halo inside the tile edge.
:::

Set **Tile Inner Glow** above `0` to reveal its color and opacity. **Tile Background Blur** frosts the backdrop only while tiles are translucent, so lower **Tile Background Opacity** below `100` to see it. Tile settings left unset use the Light Grid master defaults. Combine translucent tiles with **Tile Background Blur** and a soft light inner glow for a frosted-glass grid.

### 5. The Control Panel (Popover)

When a user taps the body of a **Light** row (not the small toggle switch), the **Control Panel** opens. **Switch** rows never open this panel.

::: grid
* [button ph-sliders] **Panel Slider:** A custom, thick slider adjusts brightness. Its height and thumb size can be customized for optimal touch targets.
* [button ph-grid-four] **Presets Grid:** Configure a grid of predefined colors and color temperatures, globally or per-light.
* [button ph-check-square] **Auto Deselect/Hide:** Enable auto-deselect and set a timeout (such as 10 seconds) to close the panel when idle.
:::

*Freely Positionable:* In **Fixed Resolution** and **Scale to Fit Screen**, drag the Control Panel anywhere on the canvas. In **Responsive Columns**, the panel stacks below the light grid in the same cell.

### 6. Icons & Appearance

Each light in the grid can have its own distinct icon to represent the physical fixture (e.g., a ceiling lamp vs. a floor lamp).

::: grid
* [button ph-star] **Per-Light Icons:** In **Basic Settings**, each light row has a Phosphor **Icon** picker. **Advanced** keeps the full Icon Style slideout (source, weight, custom image).
* [button ph-check-square] **Use Actual Light Color:** By default, enabled on Light rows to dynamically tint the grid icon and active toggle to match live bulb color or temperature. If disabled, falls back to static Icon Color (On) and Icon Color (Off).
:::

### 7. Text & Typography

The Light Grid implements the standard nested typography system, allowing granular control over text rendering.

::: grid
* [button ph-text-t] **Widget Label:** An optional master label positioned around the entire grid.
* [button ph-text-t] **Light Name:** The text displayed on each individual grid tile.
* [button ph-text-t] **Panel Title:** The header text displayed inside the popover Control Panel.
:::

As always, typography settings can be selectively overridden on the widget, with unset values elegantly falling back to your Global Settings.
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Tile On:** Plays an audio clip when a grid tile turns on.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Tile Off:** Plays an audio clip when a grid tile turns off.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Panel Open:** Plays an audio clip when the popover control panel opens.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Panel Close:** Plays an audio clip when the popover control panel closes.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: List / Log
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: List / Log](help/images/widget_listlog.jpg)

::: lead
The List / Log widget is a highly versatile component designed to display arrays of data or continuous events. It can function as a simple scrolling activity log, a live data feed, or a fully interactive to-do list with checkboxes and outbound MQTT triggers.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=10) [muted: (demo, page 10)]

### 1. Data & Behavior

::: alert info book-open
**Format & Trigger Guide**
For a complete reference on supported incoming data arrays, pipe-delimited strings, and interactive trigger topics, please read the [List / Log Data Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/list-log-data-formats) documentation.
:::

This section defines how incoming data is interpreted and added to the list buffer. The widget intelligently parses several data formats:

* **Single Strings**: Appends a new line to the top of the list. Older items are pushed down until they hit the **Max Lines** limit.
* **Delimited Strings**: You can send multiple items at once by separating them with a comma (`,`). You can also pass icon and state data in a single string using the pipe (`|`) delimiter. Format: `checked|icon|text` (e.g., `true|ph-check|Task completed`).
* **JSON Arrays**: Send a JSON array of objects to completely replace the list content. Expected object format: `{ "state": boolean, "icon": "string", "text": "string", "timestamp": number }`.

::: alert info magic-wand
**Tip:** If you just want to dump data exactly as it comes in (such as a raw JSON payload) without parsing it into list items, enable the **Raw Data** toggle. This will pretty-print JSON and display it as a single block.
:::

### 2. Output & Trigger

When **Show Checkboxes** is enabled, the list becomes interactive. This section configures how and when the widget reports its current state.

::: grid
* [button ph-broadcast] **Output Topic:** The destination topic where the list state will be published.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Output Mode:** Choose **On Any Change** to instantly publish on every checkbox tap, or **On Trigger Topic Only** to publish only when a message arrives on the Trigger Topic.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Output Format:** Defines the published payload shape: **JSON Array** (full objects including text and checked state) or **Boolean Array** (simple array of true/false values).
* [button ph-tag] **Control Topics:** Link specific topics to **Select All**, **Deselect All**, or **Delete Selected** items. Sending any message to these topics executes that action on the list buffer.
:::

### 3. Timestamp Format

When **Show Timestamp** is enabled in Appearance, this section allows you to format how the time and date are displayed.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Time Format:** Choose between `Hours:Minutes`, `Hours:Minutes:Seconds`, or hide the time entirely.
* [button ph-check-square] **24 Hour Clock:** Toggle between 24-hour time and 12-hour AM/PM format.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Date Format:** Select DD-MM, DD-MM-YYYY, MM-DD, MM-DD-YYYY, or None.
:::

### 4. Appearance

Control the layout and visibility of the list components.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Visibility Toggles:** Instantly show or hide **Icons**, **Timestamps**, and **Checkboxes** across the entire list.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Item Spacing:** Adjust the vertical gap between individual list rows.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Checkbox Alignment:** Place checkboxes on the Left or Right side of each row.
* [button ph-check-square] **Read Only:** Shows checkboxes but prevents user interaction, making the list strictly a visual display driven by data.
* [button ph-check-square] **Strikethrough (Checked):** Adds a strikethrough and dims completed items.
:::

### 5. Icon

The List widget maintains three separate icon slots:

::: grid
* [button ph-star] **Default Row Icon:** The base icon shown next to list items as a fallback. Overridden if incoming JSON data contains a specific row icon.
* [button ph-star] **Icon (On):** The icon used when a checkbox is checked (defaults to `ph-check-square`).
* [button ph-star] **Icon (Off):** The icon used when a checkbox is unchecked.
::: 

::: alert info lightbulb
**Tip:** The **Icon (Off)** slot automatically inherits its styling, size, and custom image settings from **Icon (On)** to keep your design consistent. It only maintains a separate glyph (defaulting to :ph-bold ph-square:).
:::

### 6. Text & Typography

Customize the text styling for the different parts of the list.

::: grid
* [button ph-text-t] **Widget Label:** The main title displayed above the list.
* [button ph-text-t] **List Item:** Controls the text styling of entries, including **Line Height** and a **Wrap Text** toggle.
* [button ph-text-t] **Timestamp:** Independent typography controls for the timestamp text.
:::
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Checkbox On:** Plays an audio clip when a list checkbox is checked.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Checkbox Off:** Plays an audio clip when a list checkbox is unchecked.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Menu
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Menu](help/images/widget_menu.jpg)

::: lead
The Menu widget provides a navigational list of actions: opening pages, sending commands, or opening links. It can be displayed constantly or hidden behind dynamic, sliding panels.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=17) [muted: (demo, page 17)]

::: alert info magic-wand
**Pro Tip: Auto Width & Height** 

Enable **Auto Width** or **Auto Height** in the Layout settings to have the menu automatically shrink or grow to fit the exact size of your items.
:::

### 1. Menu Behavior

Under **Menu Behavior**, define the core characteristics of your menu.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Layout Direction:** Choose between a vertical column or a horizontal row of items.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Menu Slide Style:** Controls how the menu appears: **Static (Always visible)**, **Dropdown / Dropup Menu**, **Slide Left / Right Panel**, or **Instant (no slide)**.
:::

### 2. Triggering & Status Topics

If your menu is hidden (not Static), it requires a trigger. This is typically controlled by a Switch widget acting as the menu button.

::: grid
* [button ph-broadcast] **Trigger Activation Topic:** Local topic (such as `local/menuTrigger`). The menu opens when this topic receives `true` and closes on `false`.
* [button ph-broadcast] **Output Status Topic:** Publishes menu open/closed state (`true` for open, `false` for closed) whenever it changes or upon dashboard load.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Close Method:** Dictates auto-closing behavior: **Never** (stays open until trigger closes it), **Close except toggle items** (closes on normal taps but remains open for toggle items), or **Always** (closes after any item interaction).
:::

::: alert info info
**Local vs. Global Topics** 

A **Global Topic** connects to hardware through your driver (e.g. MQTT or Homey). A **Local Topic** (starting with `local/`) only exists inside your dashboard in the browser. 

**Highly Recommended:** Use **Local Topics** whenever you want to bind widgets directly together (like a button opening a menu). It's faster and cleaner. *See [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#global-vs-local-topics) for details.*
:::

### 3. Menu Items

Build your menu structure under **Menu Items**. You can drag to reorder, duplicate, or delete items. **Batch Add Weblinks** pastes a list of URLs (optional labels, favicon, auto-title, new-tab) into new rows.

**Item Modes:**

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Item Mode:** Choose **Push Button** (acts momentarily on press), **Toggle Switch** (maintains on/off state), or **Separator** (inactive spacing or visual divider line).
:::

**On Click Actions:**

Items can simultaneously perform an action (Go to Page, Open URL) and publish a payload to an **Output Topic**. For Toggle items, you can specify separate **On Value** and **Off Value** payloads.

::: alert info checks
**Automatic Highlight (You are here)** 

If an item's mode is **Toggle Switch** and its action is **Go to Page**, it will automatically highlight when the dashboard is on that specific page. No extra wiring is needed. Additionally, if you fill in an **Output Topic**, the topic will also fire when the item is tapped. This is useful for dual actions: for example, you can switch the view to a page containing a graph, while simultaneously nudging your system to fetch fresh data for that graph.
:::

### 4. Selection Groups

For Toggle items, you can define a **Selection Group** (e.g., `main_tabs`) to create mutual exclusivity (like radio buttons). Activating one item within the group will automatically turn off the others. Checking "Send Off When Turned Off by Group" ensures the off payload is still sent when another item takes over. With **Mode** set to **Toggle Switch**, the row editor exposes the same **Selection Group ID**, **Send Off When Turned Off by Group**, and **State (On/Off)** behavior as the Switch/Button widget, including cross-widget exclusion on the same page.

The **Selection Group ID** field is a filterable list: type to narrow existing ids, pick one, or press Enter or leave the field to commit a new id (defaults apply). **Allow empty selection** (per group id, shared across the dashboard) lets users turn an active item off by tapping it again. When disabled, that behavior matches the classic “always one on” group.

### 5. Appearance & Text & Typography

Customize the visual style under **Appearance** (item backgrounds On/Off/Hover with matching **Opacity** values, corner radii, **Icon Location**, separator lines) and **Text & Typography** (group label and menu item fonts). **Label Hint** shows the full item label in a tooltip (**When Label Is Truncated** by default, or **Always** / **Disabled**). Icons can sit to the **Left**, **Right**, **Top**, or **Bottom** of each label.

Optional **Menu Item Width (px)** gives every item the same fixed width. Leave it empty or zero for automatic sizing. When a width is set, long labels truncate with an ellipsis instead of stretching the row.

Under **Appearance**, refine rows further with **Background Blur**, **Item Outline Width**, **Item Outline Color**, **Item Outline Opacity**, and **Item Inner Glow** with its color and opacity. Set **Item Inner Glow** above `0` to reveal its color and opacity. **Background Blur** frosts the backdrop only while an item background is translucent. Appearance settings left unset use the Menu master defaults. Combine translucent item backgrounds with **Background Blur** and a soft light inner glow for a frosted-glass menu.

::: alert info hand-tap
**Mini Guide: Opening a Menu with a Switch** 

1. Add a **Switch / Button** widget to your page. In **Data & Behavior**, set **Mode** to **Toggle Switch**. 
2. Set the switch's *Output Topic* to a new local topic, for example: `local/myMenuTrigger`. 
3. Select your **Menu Widget**. In its *Menu Behavior* section, set the *Trigger Activation Topic* to precisely the same string (`local/myMenuTrigger`). 
4. To ensure the switch automatically **deactivates** (returns to its inactive state) when the menu closes, set the menu's *Output Status Topic* to a different local topic, like `local/myMenuStatus`. 
5. Finally, select the Switch again and bind its *State (On/Off)* :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400: parameter to that exact same status topic (`local/myMenuStatus`). 

:::
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Menu Open:** Plays when the menu opens.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Item Select:** Plays when a push item is chosen.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Item Toggle On:** Plays when a toggle item turns on.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Item Toggle Off:** Plays when a toggle item turns off.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **Menu Close:** Plays when the menu closes. When a selection also closes the menu and its item sound is set, you hear that item sound.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Slider
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Slider](help/images/widget_sliders.jpg)

::: lead
The Slider widget provides a highly customizable control for adjusting numeric values like light brightness, speaker volume, or thermostat temperatures. It features robust anti-bounce behavior, fractional steps, custom display ranges, and vertical orientation support.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=8) [muted: (demo, page 8)]

### 1. Data & Behavior

Connect the slider to a data source to both read and update values.

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Value:** The current numeric position of the slider. Typically bound to an MQTT or Homey capability topic.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Send Value:** Choose **Send value on release** (waits until touch/mouse release to minimize traffic) or **Send value directly on movement** (streams continuously during drag).
* [button ph-broadcast] **Output Topic:** The destination topic where slider changes are published.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min / Max:** The minimum and maximum numeric boundaries of the slider. Enter a higher Min than Max to reverse the physical direction.
* [button ph-check-square] **Fractions & Fraction Step:** Essential for decimal scales. Use Fraction Step to constrain dragging to specific increments (such as `0.5` or `0.01`).
* [button ph-check-square] **Custom display range:** Decouples the underlying data value from the value shown on the screen (such as displaying 0-100% while sending 0-255).
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
The widget includes a 1-second "anti-bounce" delay after interaction to prevent incoming data updates from snapping the slider back to a previous value while you are still making adjustments.
:::

Use the faders icon :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: on **Value** for [Binding Options & Payload Formulas](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas).

### 2. Appearance

Style the slider's track, fill area, and thumb handle.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Vertical:** Flips the slider 90 degrees for vertical orientation (great for window blinds or volume faders).
* [button ph-palette] **Track Color, Fill Color & Thumb Color:** Customize the background track, active fill, and draggable thumb button colors.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Track Height & Fill Height:** Adjust component thicknesses. Setting a larger track height with smaller fill height creates an inset track look.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Thumb Size:** The diameter of the draggable handle, with optional Thumb Shadow.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Track Outline Width, Color & Opacity:** Adds a customizable border stroke around the entire slider track. **Track Outline Opacity** fades the stroke.
* [button ph-palette] **Track Opacity & Blur:** Fade the track with **Track Opacity**, and frost whatever shows through it with **Background Blur**.
* [button ph-palette] **Track Inner Glow:** Paints a soft halo inside the track edge. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Track Inner Glow Color** and **Track Inner Glow Opacity**.
* [button ph-palette] **Fill Opacity, Outline & Inner Glow:** Fade the fill with **Fill Opacity**. Stroke it with **Fill Outline Width**, **Fill Outline Color**, and **Fill Outline Opacity**. **Fill Inner Glow** paints a soft halo inside the fill edge. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Fill Inner Glow Color** and **Fill Inner Glow Opacity**.
* [button ph-palette] **Thumb Outline & Inner Glow:** Stroke the handle with **Thumb Outline Width**, **Thumb Outline Color**, and **Thumb Outline Opacity**. **Thumb Inner Glow** paints a soft halo inside the handle. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Thumb Inner Glow Color** and **Thumb Inner Glow Opacity**. Outline color and opacity stay hidden until the matching outline width is above `0`.
:::

**Background Blur** frosts the backdrop only while the track is translucent, so lower **Track Opacity** below `100` to see it. Appearance settings left unset use the Slider master defaults. Combine a translucent track with **Background Blur** and a soft light inner glow for a frosted-glass slider.

### 3. Text & Typography

Control the text elements displayed around and inside the slider.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Caption:** The primary label text displayed near the slider.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Slider Label Location:** Position the caption at **Top** (default), **Bottom**, **Left**, or **Right**.
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Value:** Toggles the numeric readout on or off.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Value Location:** Position the value overlay at **Middle** (on the track), **Top**, **Bottom**, **Left**, or **Right**.
* [button ph-textbox] **Unit Text:** An optional suffix appended to the value (such as `%` or `°C`).
:::

When label and value share a side, order is label, then value, then unit.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Scroll Wheel Support**: You can adjust the slider by hovering over it and using your mouse's scroll wheel. This increments or decrements the value precisely according to your **Fraction Step** setting.
:::
### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Value Sent:** Plays an audio clip whenever a new slider value is published.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Switch / Button
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Switch / Button](help/images/widget_switch.jpg)

::: lead
The Switch widget is a highly versatile interactive element in Dashboard Studio. It can act as a standard toggle switch, a momentary push button, an image-only button, or even an invisible overlay for creating custom clickable regions.
:::

[See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=5) [muted: (demo, page 5)]

### 1. Mode & Behavior

The core functionality of the widget is determined by its **Mode** and **Action Type**, configured in the **Data & Behavior** slideout :ph-bold ph-lightning:.

::: grid
* [button ph-caret-down] **Mode:** Choose between **Toggle Switch** (maintains on/off state) and **Push Button (Momentary)** (reverts to off upon release).
* [button ph-caret-down] **Action Type:** Select **Send Topic**, **Go to Page** (dashboard navigation), or **Open URL** (external links or in-app `help://` links).
* [button ph-check-square] **Hold to Activate:** Under On Click, delay action execution until the button has been held for the duration configured in Dashboard Environment.
* [button ph-check-square] **Require Confirmation:** Show a Yes/No confirmation dialog before running the action.
:::

::: alert info lightbulb
**Radio Buttons / Mutual Exclusion**
If you want multiple switches to act like radio buttons (where turning one on automatically turns the others off), assign them the same **Selection Group ID**. This applies when the Action Type is `Send Topic` or `Open URL`. If the Action Type is `Go to Page`, Dashboard Studio automatically handles mutual exclusion based on the currently active page.
:::

### 2. Linking to Devices

To use the switch to turn a light or device on/off:

1. Enable the device in the Homey Dashboard Studio configuration.
2. Find the capability topic in the Data Stream Explorer.
3. Paste the topic into the **Output Topic** field.
4. **Important:** To ensure the switch reflects the correct state if the light is turned on via another method (like the Homey app [badge: Homey Pro] or a physical wall switch), paste the same topic into the **Initial State** field. This creates a two-way binding.

5. **[Binding Options](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas) (optional):** Click the faders icon :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: on **Initial State** to map custom on/off words or use **Numeric Payload Formula** when the topic sends numbers. See [Binding Options & Payload Formulas](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas).

**Additional Output Topics:** Use **Add Output topic** in the same slideout to send extra topics on the same press, so one button can run several functions at once (a light plus a scene, for example). Each extra row has its own On/Off values.

Give the same button a short-press job and a long-press job by leaving **Hold to Activate** off on one topic and checking it on another. A tap runs the unchecked action. Holding for the duration runs the checked action.

### 3. Confirmation Dialog

Turn on **Require Confirmation** (next to **Hold to Activate**) to show a Yes/No overlay before this button runs its action.

::: grid
* [button ph-check-square] **Confirm When Turning Off:** By default Toggle Switch confirms turning On. Check this in Confirmation Dialog Appearance if turning Off should confirm too.
* [button ph-check-square] **Preview in Edit Mode:** Place and resize the dialog overlay directly on the canvas during design. Confirm and Dismiss do not run actions in the editor.
:::

Push Button always confirms the press (or completed hold). Open **Confirmation Dialog Appearance** :ph-bold ph-warning: to customize the message, labels, and styling.

Dismiss, Escape, or a page change cancels. Only one dialog is open at a time.

For size, icons, typography, and **Modal Mode**, see [Dialog Box](help://Widgets/dialog-box#2-panel-look-and-placement).

### 4. Visual Styles

The widget supports several distinct visual styles, selectable under Appearance:

- **Switch (Pill):** The classic iOS-style toggle pill.
- **Button (Rect):** A customizable rectangular button, ideal for dashboards.
- **Image Only / Text Only:** Strips away the button background, leaving just the content. Great for minimalist designs.
- **Invisible:** Renders no visible UI at all. 

::: alert info magic-wand
**Pro Tip: The Invisible Style**
Use the `Invisible` style to layer a clickable region over any other widget! For example, place an invisible momentary button on top of a graph or a camera feed to trigger an action when that area is tapped.
:::

### 5. Icons

The switch supports an **Icon (On)** and an **Icon (Off)**, configured under the **Icon** :ph-bold ph-star: slideout.

::: grid
* [button ph-star] **Icon (On) & Icon (Off):** The Off icon inherits shape, weight, size, and **Hover color** from the On icon unless overridden. Supports built-in Phosphor icons, custom Image URLs, or SVGs.
* [button ph-check-square] **Show Icon:** Force icons to appear on Pill and Text Only button styles where they are hidden by default.
:::

### 6. Text & Typography

The **Text & Typography** slideout :ph-bold ph-text-t: offers extensive control over the widget's text.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Outside Label:** Text positioned outside around the widget (Top, Bottom, Left, or Right).
* [button ph-textbox] **Inside Label:** Text rendered directly inside the button face (applicable for Button style).
:::

Both label roles support dual colors based on the On/Off state.

### 7. Appearance & Effects

Under the **Appearance** slideout :ph-bold ph-palette:, you can fine-tune the button's aesthetics:

::: grid
* [button ph-palette] **Colors:** Independent color controls for Background, Thumb, and Hover states across on and off states.
* [button ph-palette] **Background Opacity & Blur:** Fade the button face with **Background Opacity**, and frost whatever shows through it with **Background Blur**.
* [button ph-palette] **Glow, Outline & Inner Glow:** Add a soft drop-glow or sharp border tied to the on/off state to make active buttons pop. **Outline Opacity** fades the border. **Inner Glow** paints a soft halo inside the button edge.
* [button ph-palette] **Thumb Outline & Inner Glow:** On the Pill style, stroke the moving thumb with **Thumb Outline Width**, **Thumb Outline Color**, and **Thumb Outline Opacity**. **Thumb Inner Glow** paints a soft halo inside the thumb. Set a width above `0` to reveal **Thumb Inner Glow Color** and **Thumb Inner Glow Opacity**. Outline color and opacity stay hidden until the matching outline width is above `0`.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Label Hint:** Choose **Disabled**, **When Label Is Truncated** (default), or **Always** to show the full button label in the browser tooltip.
:::

Set **Inner Glow** above `0` to reveal **Inner Glow Color** and **Inner Glow Opacity**. **Background Blur** frosts the backdrop only while the face is translucent, so lower **Background Opacity** below `100` to see it. Appearance settings left unset use the Switch master defaults. Combine a translucent face with **Background Blur** and a soft light **Inner Glow** for a frosted-glass button.

### Audio

Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode.

::: grid
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Press:** Plays an audio clip when the button is pressed.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Release:** Plays an audio clip when the button is released.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Toggle On:** Plays an audio clip when switched on.
* [button ph-speaker-high] **On Toggle Off:** Plays an audio clip when switched off.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Text
widgetSubpages.content:
![content: Text](help/images/widget_text.jpg) ::: lead The **Text** widget is your primary tool for displaying textual content on the dashboard. It supports rich formatting via [**Markdown**](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting), allowing you to easily create headings, tables, lists, links, and embed images without any HTML knowledge. ::: [See examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=11) [muted: (demo, page 11)] ::: alert info lightbulb **Simple Text Without Formatting?** If you only need a quick caption, title, or status readout without Markdown formatting, tables, or inline icons, use the [Label](help://Widgets/label) widget instead. The Label widget renders pure text with minimal overhead, offering superior performance and lower memory usage on wall tablets and dense dashboards. ::: ### 1. Text Settings Configure the layout and spacing of your text block: ::: grid * [button ph-textbox] **Text Content:** The actual text or Markdown you want to display. Use the Full editor for a large editing area, toolbar, and find-and-replace, or bind directly to a live topic. * [button ph-caret-down] **Horizontal Alignment & Text Case:** Set these to **Use Typography Settings** to follow per-role controls in Text & Typography, or pick a fixed alignment or case to override every element. * [button ph-caret-down] **Vertical Alignment:** Pin the text block to the Top, Middle, or Bottom of widget boundaries (in Responsive Columns, stays pinned to Top). * [button ph-caret-down] **Link Open Behavior:** Choose **Use Markdown Setting (per link)**, **Always Open in New Tab**, or **Always Open in Same Tab**. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Rotation, Offset X, Offset Y:** Precisely tilt and position the text block within the widget. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Vertical Spacing (px):** Controls empty space between distinct Markdown blocks (paragraphs, headers, tables). * [button ph-check-square] **Wrap Text:** When on, long lines break inside the widget frame. Turn this off for a single-line ticker. * [button ph-check-square] **Auto-Fit Text to Frame:** Shrinks the text so the whole block fits the widget. * [button ph-check-square] **Scroll Overflow Content:** Adds a scrollbar when the text is taller or wider than the widget. ::: ::: alert info brackets-curly **Live Data Placeholders** Inject live values with `{{device_id/capability}}`. Wrap a payload formula in the same braces to choose text, an icon, or other markdown from live topics, for example `{{if({{homey/temp}} > 20, "hot", "cold")}}`. The widget updates whenever those topics change. See [Markdown Formatting Reference](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting#payload-formulas) and [formula examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=18) [muted: (demo, page 18)]. ::: ### 2. Markdown Tables, column layout, and non-text accents can be deeply customized to match your dashboard's theme: ::: grid * [button ph-caret-down] **Table Style:** Choose from over 20 predefined table layouts, ranging from minimal lists and grid systems to calendars and kanban boards. * [button ph-caret-down] **Table Column Width Mode:** Choose **Align table columns (same column count)**, **Equal Table Column Widths**, **Fixed Table Column Width**, or **Custom Column Width**. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Fixed Table Column Width (px, 0 = Auto):** Applies one fixed width to all table columns. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Amount of Columns:** In **Custom Column Width**, sets how many column width fields to show until a table is available. `0` shows no column fields. A table in **Text Content** sets the column count and hides this field. The same happens for the current value of a **Text Content** topic after you confirm that topic, and while this widget stays selected. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Custom Column Width (px, 0 = Auto):** Shows one width spinner per column to set specific pixel widths or auto. * [button ph-palette] **Element Colors:** Defines specific colors for Table Borders, Headers, Rows, Alternate Rows, Markdown inline icons, and Horizontal Rules (`---`). ::: For complete Markdown syntax (headers, lists, links, icons, table cell backgrounds, and more), see the [Markdown Formatting Reference](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting). Use `[label](help://Topic)` or `help://Topic/slug#section` to open Documentation from the dashboard. ### 3. Text & Typography Instead of a single font setting, the Text widget offers individual typography slideouts for each semantic element: ::: grid * [button ph-text-t] **Paragraph:** Typography slideout for standard text lines. * [button ph-text-t] **Header 1, Header 2, Header 3:** Typography slideouts for title headings (H4 through H6 map to H3). * [button ph-text-t] **Table Header & Table Text:** Typography slideouts targeting text inside Markdown tables. :::

4. Full editor

When the **Text Content** field is not bound to a topic, the **Full editor** button opens a large, movable window so you can write and format Markdown with a toolbar. The dashboard preview updates from your edits. To keep the editor responsive, the canvas may refresh slightly *after* you type instead of on every single keystroke. You can drag the title bar to move the window, drag the bottom-right corner to resize, and your last size and position are remembered in this browser. On **Homey**, the toolbar can insert an image from the same **[Image Gallery](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager)** as the header (pick an image, then **Insert** or the **+** action on a thumbnail). Other platforms can still add images by URL. #### Keyboard shortcuts (inside Full editor) Use *Ctrl* on Windows/Linux or *⌘* on macOS where noted. | Action | Shortcut | | --- | --- | | Bold (wrap with `**`) | Ctrl / ⌘ + B | | Italic (wrap with `*`) | Ctrl / ⌘ + I | | Insert link (URL + Same tab / New tab) | Ctrl / ⌘ + K | | Undo last edit in this session | Ctrl / ⌘ + Z | | Redo | Ctrl / ⌘ + Y or Ctrl / ⌘ + Shift + Z | | Close the "Find & replace" strip (when it is open), or close Full editor | Escape | Native browser undo may still apply for very recent typing. The in-editor undo stack is meant for toolbar actions and longer edits in one session (up to about 50 steps).

5. Calendars [badge: Homey Pro]

[See calendar examples on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=12) [muted: (demo, page 12)] The Text widget is the perfect place to show your family or work schedules from **Apple iCloud**, **Google Calendar**, **Outlook**, or any provider that offers an **iCal** subscription link. You do not paste calendar web links into the widget itself. Instead, Homey does all the retrieval and formatting through Homey Flows using Dashboard Studio's calendar cards: **Load & filter iCal** downloads your schedule, and **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** turns it into clean table views. Your flow then uses **Send … with value … to Dashboard** to push the finished table to your Text widget. **Configuring your calendar:** * **Calendar behavior and icons:** Open the Homey app settings under **More → Apps → Dashboard Studio → Configure App → Calendar**. Here you can set the start day of the week, date formats, icon keywords, and color blocks. * **Table styling on the dashboard:** Select your Text widget in the editor and expand **Markdown**. Pick from over 20 predefined layouts in **Table Style**, including specialized calendar presets like **Calendar - Week Planner**, **Calendar - Month View**, or **Calendar - Simple Grid**, as well as compact list layouts like **Card Rows** or **Timeline View**. **Connecting data:** Bind your widget **Text Content** to `homey/event/your_calendar_topic`, or embed it into custom text with `{{homey/event/your_calendar_topic}}`. ::: alert info calendar **Full walkthrough and flow examples:** Open [Homey Flow Cards → Calendar & iCal](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/calendar-ical) to learn how to obtain iCal links, set up one-time downloads for multiple views, and combine multiple family calendars. ::: *For developers and Homey Script users, see [Load & Filter iCal: Filtered Events (JSON)](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/load-filter-ical).* ### Animations & Effects Content-change **Animation** plays when **Text Scroll** is **None** and the text is replaced, from a bound topic, or from inline `{{topic}}` values when **Animate When Inline Topics Change** is on. **Duration** and **Preview** apply to that swap. When **Text Scroll** is on, live text updates stay in the moving block. **Text Scroll** moves the whole Markdown block inside the widget frame. ::: grid * [button ph-caret-down] **Text Scroll:** **None**, **Horizontal**, or **Vertical**. Horizontal is a ticker (text moves left). Vertical is a credits roll (text moves up). **Reverse** flips the direction. * [button ph-caret-down] **Motion:** **Loop** wraps the block so the start follows the end. **Bounce** travels to the far end and back at the same speed. **Reset** travels to the far end, holds, fades out, then fades in at the start. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Speed:** Pixels per second. A higher value is faster. * [button ph-check-square] **Only When Text Overflows:** Motion runs only while the block is larger than the frame. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Gap:** Space between the two copies in **Loop**. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Start Hold (s)** and **Hold (s):** For **Loop**, wait before the first move. For **Reset**, wait at the far end before the fade. * [button ph-number-square-five] **Fade (s):** Length of the fade out and fade in for **Reset**. ::: **Wrap Text** still controls line breaking while **Text Scroll** is on. A single-line ticker uses **Wrap Text** off. ### Audio Open the **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes: to play a clip from the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery#per-widget-audio) when this widget fires a trigger. Assign a file to a trigger. Playback runs in view mode. ::: grid * [button ph-speaker-high] **On Text Change:** Plays an audio clip whenever the bound text content updates. :::

topics.title: Tools
topics.content:
![header: Tools](help/images/header_tools.jpg)

::: lead
**Tools** are extra scripts that automate jobs inside Dashboard Studio. They sit in the hammer menu and run on demand, beside the widget inspector.
:::

Open **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: in **Editor Tools** on the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#2-editor-tools). Pick a script to run it.

::: grid
* [button ph-table] **[Widget Preset Editor](help://Tools/widget-preset-editor):** Edit factory packs and **My Presets** in a multi-column workspace.
* [button ph-arrow-square-out] **[Set Link Open Behavior](help://Tools/set-link-open-behavior):** Set **New Tab** or **Same Tab** on URL actions across selected widget types.
* [button ph-link-break] **[Make All Dynamic Values Fixed](help://Tools/make-all-dynamic-values-fixed):** Copy the current value of every topic-linked setting and keep that value on the setting.
* [button ph-squares-four] **[Auto-Widget Gallery](help://Tools/auto-widget-gallery):** Generate live widget previews from incoming topics and add the ones you check to the canvas.
:::

widgetSubpages.title: Widget Preset Editor
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Tools](help/images/header_tools.jpg)
::: lead
The **Widget Preset Editor** is a spreadsheet-style workspace for built-in presets and **My Presets**. Open it from **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer:, pick a widget type, then include, edit, duplicate, and save the looks you reuse.
:::

### Open the editor

1. Click **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: in **Editor Tools**.
2. Choose **Widget Preset Editor**.
3. Pick a **Widget Type**. The left list then shows **My Presets** and **Built-in Presets**.

Check one or more presets in the list to open them as columns. Each column is one variant (main preset or sub-preset).

Saving **My Presets** on Homey needs Homey file storage. [badge: Homey Pro]

### The settings grid

Rows are widget settings. Columns are the presets you checked.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Filter Settings:** Searches the settings tree by name.
* [button ph-sliders] **All / Included / Differing:** **All** shows every setting. **Included** shows only settings stored in at least one open column. **Differing** highlights values that are not the same across those columns.
:::
* Each cell has an **Include** checkbox. A preset only writes **included** (checked) settings. Those values replace the matching fields when the preset is applied. Unchecked settings keep the widget's previous value.
* Edit a value in a cell to change that variant. Select several cells to toggle **Include** or apply one edit to all of them.

Changed fields in the main editor use a blue outline. Include only the settings you want the preset to own.

### My Presets and built-ins

::: grid
* [button ph-copy] **To My Presets:** Copies a built-in (or a selection) into My Presets so you can edit it.
* [button ph-stack-plus] **Duplicate:** Copies a preset or a sub-preset.
* [button ph-cloud-arrow-up] **Save / Save All:** Writes the current My Preset or all modified My Presets to Homey storage. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-download-simple] **Export:** Downloads a `.json` file for any open preset (built-in or mine).
:::

Add, delete, and reorder variants directly from the column header.

Delete applies to selected **My Presets**. Built-in packs stay in the factory list.

### Related topics

* [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets) for applying a look on a selected widget, and for the inspector **Save** dialog.
* [Tools](help://Tools) for the other editor scripts.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode) for **Editor Mode**.
* [Styling & Layering](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#1-the-styling-cascade-master-vs-local) for theme colors versus a preset on one widget.

widgetSubpages.title: Set Link Open Behavior
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
**Set Link Open Behavior** applies **New Tab** or **Same Tab** to URL actions across the widgets you select. Open it from **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: when you want one choice for many links at once.
:::

### Open the tool

1. Click **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: in **Editor Tools**.
2. Choose **Set Link Open Behavior**.
3. Pick **New Tab** or **Same Tab**.
4. In the type tree, keep the widgets you want (every matching widget starts checked). Expand a type to pick individual widgets.
5. Click **Apply**.

The dialog lists widgets that have a URL action or Markdown links.

| Widget | What it updates |
| --- | --- |
| [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#1-mode-behavior) | **Open URL** |
| [Edit Box](help://Widgets/editbox) | **Open URL** |
| [Menu](help://Widgets/menu) | Per-row URL targets |
| [Light Grid](help://Widgets/lightgrid) | Per-light URL actions |
| [Text](help://Widgets/text) | Markdown `[label](url)` links (new tab uses a trailing `^`) |

Each updated widget is one undo step.

### Related topics

* [Markdown Formatting Reference](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting#links-opening-in-a-new-tab) for the caret marker on Text links.
* [Tools](help://Tools) for the Tools menu.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#2-editor-tools) for **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: in **Editor Tools**.

widgetSubpages.title: Make All Dynamic Values Fixed
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
**Make All Dynamic Values Fixed** writes the current value of every topic-linked setting onto that setting, across the whole dashboard. Open it from **Tools** :ph-bold ph-link-break: when the dashboard should keep what it is showing right now.
:::

### What it changes

It checks widget settings, group settings, and **Dashboard Settings**.

::: grid
* [button ph-link-break] **Widgets:** A setting linked to a topic keeps the value that topic currently has. Inline `{{topic}}` values and formulas inside **Text Content** in [Text](help://Widgets/text) widgets are replaced with their current evaluated values as fixed text.
* [button ph-stack] **Groups:** **Visibility**, **Override Page(s)**, and **Blur Background When Visible** keep their current value when those are linked.
* [button ph-gear] **Dashboard Settings:** A linked dashboard setting keeps its current value.
:::

The topic link is removed from each of those settings. **Undo** restores every topic link from this run in one step.

### Related topics

* [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29) for linking a setting to a topic.
* [Tools](help://Tools) for the Tools menu.
