* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#2-editor-tools) for **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: in **Editor Tools**.

widgetSubpages.title: Auto-Widget Gallery
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Tools](help/images/header_tools.jpg)
::: lead
**Auto-Widget Gallery** builds live widget previews from the topics already arriving on your dashboard. Check the ones you want and add them to the canvas together.
:::

### Where to open it

::: grid
* [button ph-hammer] **Tools:** Click **Tools** :ph-bold ph-hammer: in **Editor Tools** and choose **Auto-Widget Gallery**.
* [button ph-squares-four] **Data Stream Explorer:** In **Dashboard Settings**, open **Data Stream Explorer** and click **Auto-Widget Gallery** above the topic list.
* [button ph-trash] **Reset Canvas:** The last step of the setup wizard, **Populate Your Canvas**, shows the same gallery before the new dashboard is created. **Platform** starts on **Homey**. Choosing another platform reloads the topic list and rebuilds the widget cards. If no device topics are coming in yet, the wizard asks you to enable a few capabilities first. **OK** closes the wizard. **Ignore** continues.
:::

### Choose widgets

Each card is a real preview of a gauge, slider, switch, text block, or another widget that matches the topic.

::: grid
* [button ph-textbox] **Search:** Filter cards by name or topic.
* [button ph-check-square] **Only show unused topics:** Hide topics that already appear on the dashboard. This stays on while the gallery is open from **Tools** or **Data Stream Explorer**. The setup wizard does not show this control because the new canvas starts empty.
* [button ph-sort-ascending] **Sort:** Order cards by live activity, name, widget type, or writable topics first.
* [button ph-arrows-clockwise] **Refresh Values:** Ask Homey to send the last known value for every topic again. This appears when the dashboard is connected to Homey.
* [button ph-checks] **Select All Visible** and **Clear Selection:** Check or clear the cards currently on screen.
:::

Use the **Select** checkbox on a card to check that widget. Checking another card leaves the ones you already checked in place. Clicking the preview does not change the selection.

If the name is wider than the card, hover the name to read all of it.

When a value can be more than one kind of widget, a type list under the name lets you pick another type. The preview changes to that widget. Read and write access uses the same colored tag as Data Stream Explorer.

Hover a card and click the template name to open every built-in template for that widget. A template with sub-presets, such as Small, Medium, and Large, opens a second menu. A template without sub-presets applies as soon as you click it. The preview fills the thumbnail, and the widget placed on the canvas uses the template size. In the setup wizard, previews use the theme you picked on the step before.

**Default Widget Presets** applies one template to every thumbnail of that widget type. Open the widget, then the preset, then a sub-preset when that preset has one. A check marks the preset in use. The choice lasts for this visit to the editor. **Reset to Default** in that menu brings every card back to the look the gallery first built. Choosing a template on a card keeps the other cards in place. Pick a sort again when you want a new order.

A graph uses **Line Graph** with points on the X axis. When those points are dates or times, the X axis shows the date and hour. A value made of numbered samples, with keys 0, 1, 2 and numeric values, becomes a graph. A checklist of rows that each have text, a checked state, and a timestamp becomes a list.

A card marked **In Use** already has that topic on the dashboard. Each value that arrives briefly highlights the card, including when the value is the same as before. Numeric previews widen their range as live values arrive, so a gauge or slider fits what the topic is sending.

### Add them

Click **Add Selected to Canvas** to place every checked widget on the current page. An on/off topic becomes a pill switch with the label above the control. **Undo** removes that whole batch in one step.

If a widget does not fit on the current page, it is added to the next page and a message tells you so. The page you are on stays open. Use the arrows beside the page name in the editor sidebar to open another page.

In **Reset Canvas**, **Create Dashboard** adds the checked widgets after the blank canvas is ready. **Skip / Create Blank** keeps your editor mode, layout, and theme and adds no widgets. **Back** returns to the theme step with your checks still in place.

### Related topics

* [Tools](help://Tools) for the Tools menu.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#10-data-stream-explorer) for **Data Stream Explorer**.
* [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor) for how topics reach widgets.

topics.title: Styling & Layering
topics.content:
![header: Styling & Layering](help/images/header_styling.jpg)

::: lead
Design visually stunning dashboards by combining themes, frosted glass effects, layered widget frames, and global style defaults. Learn how to craft cohesive palettes and optimize layout performance across all your screens.
:::

### Page Index

* [1. The Styling Cascade (Master vs. Local)](#1-the-styling-cascade-master-vs-local)
* [2. Themes & Theme Explorer](#2-themes--theme-explorer)
* [3. Glass Mode Style (Frosted Glassmorphism)](#3-glass-mode-style-frosted-glassmorphism)
* [4. Layering & Stacking Order](#4-layering--stacking-order)
* [5. Combined Groups in Responsive Columns](#5-combined-groups-in-responsive-columns)

---

### 1. The Styling Cascade (Master vs. Local)
![content: Theme Settings](help/images/styling_settings.jpg)
Dashboard Studio uses a hierarchical styling cascade. Styling flows from global defaults down to individual widget overrides:

#### 1. Global Defaults (Master Settings)
Configured under **Dashboard Settings** (gear icon :ph-bold ph-gear: in the left sidebar). Master settings govern:

* **Container Style:** Universal card backgrounds, gradients, borders, corner radiuses, and blur filters.
* **Typography:** Global font families, font sizes, text case, and default label colors.
* **Theme Colors:** Semantic palette tokens (`@primary`, `@accent`, `@background`) mapped across widgets.
* **Master Widget Settings:** Baseline defaults for individual widget types such as [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch), [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge), and [Slider](help://Widgets/slider).

When you modify a value in Master Settings, every widget on your canvas updates immediately unless it has a local override.

#### 2. Local Overrides (Widget Settings)
Selecting an individual widget opens its own inspector panel. Changing any appearance property here applies exclusively to that specific widget:

* Overridden properties display a blue accent outline and a small **Reset Arrow** button :ph-bold ph-arrow-counter-clockwise: next to the input.
* Clicking the **Reset Arrow** clears the custom override and instantly reconnects the property to its Master default.

::: alert info arrow-counter-clockwise
**Reverting Styling via Toolbar:**

Use the toolbar buttons in **Selected Widget Tools** to reset styling quickly. Click **Current** to restore the active widget to current theme defaults, or click **All** to reset styling across every widget on the canvas.
:::

---

### 2. Themes & Theme Explorer

::: p #help-theme-explorer
Themes bundle complete color schemes, typography choices, and widget styling rules into reusable design presets.
:::

#### Full Themes vs. Adjustment Themes
Dashboard Studio provides two distinct kinds of themes:

* **Full Themes:** Complete design systems that define backgrounds, semantic color slots, typography, and widget chrome. Applying a full theme completely replaces the current styling look across your dashboard. Examples include **Default Dark**, **Cyberpunk Neon**, **Dark Glass**, and **Ivory Glass**.
* **Adjustment Themes:** Targeted modifier themes that transform specific visual characteristics while leaving your existing colors intact. For instance, **Convert Flat to Glass** introduces frosted translucency and inner glows to your current layout, while **Convert Glass to Flat** strips away blurs and returns your widgets to solid cards.

#### The Theme Explorer Gallery
Click the **Theme Explorer** button :ph-bold ph-squares-four: in the top toolbar to open the visual theme browser:

* **Visual Card Grid:** Browse visual thumbnails organized by **My Themes** (stored on Homey) and **Built-in Themes**, with tags distinguishing **Full** from **Adjustment** themes.
* **Live Canvas Preview:** Click any theme card to preview it instantly on your live canvas in real time.
* **Reset Current Look First:** Check this box in the dialog footer when applying a custom user theme. It restores original factory colors and widget chrome before applying the theme, ensuring a clean slate without residual styling. Built-in full themes always replace the look automatically.
* **Apply or Cancel:** Click **Apply Theme** to save the selected style, or click **Cancel** (or close the window) to discard changes and revert your canvas to its exact prior snapshot.

#### Toolbar Theme Controls
Quickly manage themes using the toolbar:
::: grid
* [button ph-caret-left] **Previous Theme:** Step backwards through your theme list.
* [button ph-caret-right] **Next Theme:** Step forward through your theme list.
* [button ph-squares-four] **Theme Explorer:** Open the visual gallery modal to browse, preview, and apply themes.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Select Theme:** Pick any built-in theme, adjustment theme, or stored user theme from the dropdown.
* [button ph-cloud-arrow-up] **Save Theme:** Save your current colors, typography, and container styles to Homey as a reusable custom theme. [badge: Homey Pro]
* [button ph-download-simple] **Export Theme:** Download your active styling as a `.json` theme file to your computer.
* [button ph-folder-open] **Import Theme:** Load an exported theme `.json` file from your computer.
:::

#### Theme Colors & Semantic Tokens
Under **Dashboard Settings** → **Theme Colors**, customize the semantic palette slots:

* **Semantic Slots:** Tokens like `@background`, `@primary`, `@accent`, `@cardBackground`, and `@danger` keep your dashboard harmonious. Assigning a token instead of a static hex code ensures your widgets update whenever the theme changes.
* **Live Data Binding:** Bind any theme color slot directly to live topic data (such as RGB lighting or time of day) to shift dashboard accents dynamically.
* **Theme Corrections:** Fine-tune the entire palette simultaneously using four adjustment sliders:
    * **Color Tone:** Rotates all palette colors around the color wheel from `-180°` to `+180°`.
    * **Color Intensity:** Adjusts color intensity from `0%` (monochrome grayscale) to `200%` (vibrant).
    * **Brightness:** Adjusts the overall lightness of every theme color from `0%` to `200%`.
    * **Contrast:** Spreads dark tones darker and light tones lighter from `0%` to `200%`, expanding symmetrically around your chosen brightness setting.
    * Click the reset icon next to the section title to return all four sliders to their center defaults.

---

### 3. Glass Mode Style (Frosted Glassmorphism)

If you want a modern, Apple-inspired interface, you can configure Dashboard Studio with a sleek frosted glass look. Frosted glass uses soft translucency, backdrop blur, subtle edge highlights, and luminous inner sheens to create depth and sophistication.

#### Quick Glass Setup
The fastest ways to activate glass mode:

* **Choose a Built-in Glass Theme:** In **Theme Explorer** or the **Select Theme** dropdown, pick one of the ready-made glass styles such as **Dark Glass**, **Ivory Glass**, **Forest Glass**, **Sunset Glass**, or **Slate Glass**.
* **Convert an Existing Theme:** In the **Select Theme** dropdown, select the **Convert Flat to Glass** adjustment theme. This overlays glass translucency, blur filters, and edge sheens onto your existing colors.

#### Crafting Custom Glass: The Container Recipe
To create a custom glass effect manually, adjust the container appearance. You can configure this globally in **Container Style** under **Dashboard Settings**, or on an individual [Container](help://Widgets/container) widget:

1. **Lower Start Opacity and End Opacity:** Set **Start Opacity** to around `20%` and **End Opacity** to around `40%`. This makes the container surface translucent so underlying elements peek through.
2. **Increase Background Blur:** Set **Background Blur** to `8` or higher (up to `20`). This diffuses and softens whatever is behind the container, creating an authentic frosted glass appearance.
3. **Add a Crisp Border Edge:** Set **Border Width** to `1`, choose a light border color (such as white `#ffffff` or light gray), and set border opacity to `80%`. This simulates light catching the sharp glass rim.
4. **Apply an Inner Glow Sheen:** Set **Inner Glow** to `20`, choose a light color, and increase **Inner Glow Opacity** to `60%`. This produces a gentle top sheen and light refraction across the surface.

::: alert tip lightbulb
**Universal Container Styling:**

Configure these four ingredients once in **Container Style** under **Dashboard Settings**. Every container and card across your dashboard will instantly inherit the frosted glass aesthetic, saving you from styling widgets individually.
:::

#### Recommended Backdrop: Background Image
To get the most visual impact out of frosted glass, configure a backdrop image:

* Open **Dashboard Settings** → **Dashboard Environment**.
* Enter a high-resolution image URL in **Background Image URL**.
* Set **Image Fit** to **cover**.
* A vibrant wallpaper or subtle abstract texture behind blurred containers makes the frosted glass effect truly stand out.

#### Widgets with Native Glass and Surface Chrome
Beyond the container, several interactive widgets feature their own independent blur, outline, and inner glow controls:

* **Switch / Button:** Customize **Background Blur**, **Inner Glow**, **Inner Glow Opacity**, button outline width, and thumb inner glow for floating pill buttons.
* **Slider:** Set **Track Background Blur**, **Track Inner Glow**, track outline, fill inner glow, and thumb inner glow.
* **Gauge:** Configure **Track Background Blur**, **Track Inner Glow**, track outline, and bar inner glow for glowing circular meters.
* **Light Grid:** Style individual tiles with **Tile Background Blur**, **Tile Inner Glow**, and tile outline width.
* **Menu:** Customize floating rows with **Item Background Blur**, **Item Inner Glow**, and item outline width.

::: alert warning warning-circle
**Hardware Performance Notice:**

Backdrop blurs and translucent layers require significant real-time graphics rendering. Older hardware, particularly legacy wall-mounted tablets or budget displays, can experience dropped framerates or sluggish touch responses when rendering heavy blurs.
If you notice unacceptable performance dips on older hardware, disable blur or restrict it strictly to key focal areas.
:::

::: alert tip lightbulb
**Performance Tip:** If there is nothing behind a container (such as a solid canvas background without wallpaper or overlapping elements), applying blur is unnecessary. There is nothing behind the container to frost, yet the tablet browser still performs the expensive blur calculation. Keep blur off for plain, flat backgrounds to preserve maximum performance.
:::

---

### 4. Layering & Stacking Order

Widgets in Dashboard Studio exist in a 3D visual stack. Layering lets you compose rich, multi-part controls by positioning widgets on top of each other:

![content: Widget Layering](help/images/styling_layers.jpg)

#### Selecting Stacked Widgets
When widgets overlap on the canvas, selecting items underneath the top layer is effortless:

* **Middle Mouse Click:** Click the middle mouse wheel on any widget stack to cycle selection sequentially through every widget underneath.
* **Alt + Left Click:** Hold the **Alt** key on your keyboard and left-click the stack to step through layers behind the top widget.

#### Visual Frames & Background Panels
Use a [Container](help://Widgets/container) widget as a visual backdrop or grouped panel:

* Place a Container on the canvas, then place switches, gauges, and text widgets directly on top of it.
* The container acts as a structured card frame for the enclosed controls.
* Pure visual layering arranges widgets spatially on the canvas, but does not bind them into a single scaling unit. For scaling groups in responsive layouts, see [Combined Groups in Responsive Columns](#5-combined-groups-in-responsive-columns) below.

#### Hiding the Container Box
Every widget includes a container envelope. To create borderless, floating elements:

* Open the widget settings and uncheck **Show Container** in **Container Style** (or in **Basic Settings**).
* The outer card frame disappears, leaving only the active interactive elements (such as the switch knob, slider track, or icon) visible against the background.

#### Adjusting Z-Index Order
Control which widget appears in front or behind using the top toolbar:

* Click **Bring to Front** :ph-bold ph-caret-double-up: to pull the selected widget forward one layer in the stack.
* Click **Send to Back** :ph-bold ph-caret-double-down: to push the selected widget backward one layer in the stack.

---

### 5. Combined Groups in Responsive Columns

When designing for tablets and smartphones in **Responsive Columns** layout mode, you can combine multiple overlapping widgets into a single adaptive card cell.

#### Creating Responsive Combined Cards
In standard fixed or scale layouts, grouping widgets simply links them for moving or duplicating. In **Responsive Columns** mode, groups provide an additional capability:

* Select several widgets (such as a Container background, an Icon, and two Text labels) and click **Group** in the top toolbar.
* In Responsive Columns mode, this group occupies a single cell in the responsive column grid.
* Open the group settings and set **Scale Mode** to **Rescale**.
* When viewed on narrower mobile screens or rotating tablets, the entire group scales its internal elements proportionally as a single cohesive unit, maintaining precise relative alignment between icons, labels, and frames.

For detailed configuration examples and column layout options, see [Layout Modes: Combined Groups](help://Layout%20Modes#combined-widgets-groups).

topics.title: Image Gallery Manager
topics.content:
![header: Gallery](help/images/header_gallery.jpg)

::: lead
The **Image Gallery** is a built-in file manager for uploading and hosting images on your Homey. This is ideal for floor plans, custom icons, and backgrounds without external hosting. [badge: Homey Pro]
:::

### Opening the gallery

In the Editor, click the **Image Gallery** button :ph-bold ph-images-square text-cyan-400: in the **Editor Tools** strip at the top. The gallery is only available when Dashboard Studio is connected in Homey mode.

### Toolbar and views

The gallery uses a compact **two-row toolbar**: the first row switches views, filters, and sizes the previews. The second row handles bulk selection and delete.

::: grid
* [button ph-squares-four] **Thumbnail grid & List:** Toggle between a responsive thumbnail card grid and a detailed list view showing filename, size, and modified time.
* [button ph-textbox] **Search:** Filter images in real time by filename (partial match, not case-sensitive).
* [button ph-caret-down] **Sort:** Order files by name (A to Z / Z to A), size (largest/smallest), or date (newest/oldest).
* [button ph-sliders] **Thumb size:** Scale thumbnail preview tiles (about 72px to 200px). List view remembers its own preview size separately.
* [button ph-check-square] **Select all & Clear:** Bulk select all images in view or clear the current selection.
* [button ph-trash] **Delete:** Permanently removes all selected images after confirmation.
:::

**Total size** on the right summarizes storage used and how many files are on Homey.

### Uploading images

* **Multiple files:** Drag and drop several files onto the upload zone, or click it and choose multiple files in the file dialog.
* **Formats:** JPG, PNG, GIF, SVG, and WEBP.
* **Size:** Each file must be under 8MB. You may be warned above about 600KB because large files slow dashboards down.
* **Name already exists:** You can **Replace** the file on Homey, **Save as copy** (auto-renamed), or **Skip** that file.

Upload progress appears above the image area while files are being sent.

### Opening, selecting, and quick actions

* **Click** an image (not on the overlay buttons) to open a **large preview**. Use **Copy**, **Download**, or **Rename** in the preview bar. Press **Escape** or the backdrop to close the preview.
* **Ctrl** (Windows/Linux) or **Cmd** (Mac) + click toggles that image in the selection.
* **Shift** + click extends the selection across a range (from the last anchor row). The first Shift-click selects a single anchor row.
* **Hover** over a thumbnail or list preview to show **Copy path** and **Delete** for that file only.

### Using paths in widgets

Copy copies a path suitable for widgets, e.g. `/images/your-file.png` (leading slash). Close the gallery, select a widget, and paste into the matching field, such as the **URL** in the Image widget’s **Data & Source** section, or **Image URL** inside an **Icon** style slideout (Gauge, Switch, List, and similar).

### Insert from a field

On Homey, image URL fields show a gallery icon inside the edit box. Click it to open the gallery in insertion mode. Pick an existing file, or upload or drag a new one, to write `/images/<name>` into that field.

This picker appears on the Image widget **URL** and **Fallback URL**, master **Background Image URL**, and Custom Icon **Image URL** fields. The Text widget Full editor still inserts Markdown (`![alt](/images/name)`). The preview **+ Insert** button appears only while a field is picking a file.

### Rename

From the preview, **Rename** changes the filename on Homey. The extension must stay the same. Any widget still using the old path will need updating.

![content: Image Gallery](help/images/gallery_interface.jpg)
### Related topics

* [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery) for sound clips on Homey.
* [Icons & Images](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/icons-images) for Phosphor icons and custom image URLs.
* [Image widget](help://Widgets/image) for placing pictures on the canvas.

topics.title: Audio Gallery
topics.content:
![header: Audio](help/images/header_audio_gallery.jpg)

::: lead
Host short sound clips on Homey and play them from topic changes or from widget actions. The **Audio Gallery** stores the files. **Dashboard Audio** decides when they play.
:::

Audio playback runs in view mode. After load, playback stays muted for a few seconds so Homey cache replay does not fire every clip at once.

### Audio Gallery [badge: Homey Pro]

In the Editor, click the **Audio Gallery** button :ph-bold ph-music-notes text-cyan-400: in the **Editor Tools** strip, next to **[Image Gallery](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager)**. The gallery is available when Dashboard Studio is connected in Homey mode.

The gallery is a list of files on Homey:

* **Built-in** clips ship with the app. They are tagged **Built-in**, play like any other track, and cannot be deleted or renamed.
* **Upload** files, or drag them onto the list.
* **Search** and **Sort** by name, size, or date.
* Select uploaded rows to **Delete** (multi-select), **Rename**, or **Download**.
* **Copy** copies a widget path such as `/audio/chime.mp3`.
* **Play** starts the track on that row. The active row expands with seek and stop.

::: alert info music-notes
**Kenney sound effects**

The **Built-in** clips are a preselection of free sound effects from [Kenney](https://kenney.nl/). If you want the full library, download the files there and **Upload** them into the gallery.
:::

Loop, mute, and volume preferences apply to gallery playback.

| Item | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| **Formats** | `mp3`, `wav`, `ogg`, `m4a`, `aac`, `webm`, `flac` |
| **Size** | Each file must be 15 MB or smaller |
| **Path** | `/audio/your-file.mp3` |

You can also list audio files in **Homey App Settings** → **File Manager**. Uploaded files can be deleted there. **Built-in** clips have no delete action.
![content: Audio Gallery](help/images/audio_gallery.jpg)
### Topic Audio

Open **⚙️ Dashboard Settings** → **Audio**. **Topic Audio** is a map of topics to files.

When a listed topic receives a new payload, the dashboard plays that clip. Use this for doorbells, alarms, or status sounds that are not tied to one widget.

Click **Add Topic Audio**, pick a topic, then choose a file. On Homey, the field opens the gallery in pick mode so **Insert** writes `/audio/...` into the row.

### Per-widget Audio

These widgets have an **Audio** slideout :ph-bold ph-music-notes:. Each trigger can point at a gallery file or a path you paste. Assign a file to play it. Playback runs in view mode.

| Widget | Triggers |
| --- | --- |
| [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#audio) | **On Press**, **On Release**, **On Toggle On**, **On Toggle Off** |
| [Menu](help://Widgets/menu#audio) | **Menu Open**, **Menu Close**, plus per-item **On Press**, **On Release**, **On Toggle On**, **On Toggle Off** |
| [Light Grid](help://Widgets/lightgrid#audio) | **On Tile On**, **On Tile Off**, **On Panel Open**, **On Panel Close** |
| [List / Log](help://Widgets/list#audio) | **On Checkbox On**, **On Checkbox Off** |
| [Slider](help://Widgets/slider#audio) | **On Value Sent** |
| [Clock](help://Widgets/clock#audio) | **Every Second**, **Every Minute**, **Every Hour**, **Every Day** |
| [Text](help://Widgets/text#audio) | **On Text Change** |
| [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge#audio) | **On Value Change** |
| [Icon](help://Widgets/icon#audio) | **On Activated**, **On Deactivated** |
| [Battery](help://Widgets/battery#audio) | **On Full**, **On Empty**, **On Charging**, **On Stop Charging** |

The gallery button lives in the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#2-editor-tools).

### Related topics

* [Image Gallery Manager](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager) for pictures and backgrounds on Homey.
* [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29) for topic names used in **Topic Audio**.

widgetSubpages.title: Basic Beginners Tutorial [badge: Homey Pro]
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Basic Beginners Tutorial](help/images/header_basic_tutorial.jpg)

::: lead
Welcome to the beginners tutorial for Dashboard Studio. If you want to create a clean, beautiful smart home dashboard as quickly and easily as possible without getting tangled in advanced settings or complex formulas, you are in the right place.
:::

This walkthrough is designed for users who want the simplest, fastest path to get up and running with their smart home. It relies on automatic matching and keeps technical settings tucked away.

If you want a deeper look at building custom interfaces from scratch, explore [Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide). That guide covers detailed layout positioning, custom flow logic, and advanced insights. It is easy to follow and great for beginners too.

### What you will do

* [Understand how Dashboard Studio talks to Homey](#how-it-works)
* [Enable your device capabilities](#step-1-enable-capabilities-in-homey) in Homey settings
* [Open Dashboard Studio](#step-2-open-dashboard-studio) in your web browser
* [Enter Edit Mode](#step-3-enter-edit-mode) using the gear button
* [Run the Reset Canvas Wizard](#step-4-start-the-reset-canvas-wizard)
* [Pick Basic Mode](#step-5-choose-basic-mode) for a clean, simplified editor
* [Select your Layout Mode](#step-6-choose-your-layout-mode-and-screen-size) and canvas resolution
* [Choose a visual theme](#step-7-pick-a-theme-style)
* [Let the Auto-Widget Gallery](#step-8-select-widgets-in-the-auto-widget-gallery) generate your widgets
* [Arrange widgets and apply presets](#step-9-arrange-and-customize-your-canvas)
* [Switch between Basic and Advanced settings](#step-10-basic-mode-versus-advanced-mode) when you need more power
* [Save your dashboard](#step-11-save-your-dashboard-and-display-it) and open it on your display

---

### How it works

Dashboard Studio runs as a private web application hosted locally on your Homey. You design and view your dashboards directly from any web browser on your computer, tablet, or phone.

To share information between Homey and your dashboard, Dashboard Studio uses data channels called [topics](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29). These topics originate from the standard MQTT protocol.

Each topic holds a single live value:

* **True or false:** Light turned on, door opened, motion detected
* **Numbers:** Room temperature, energy consumption, dim level
* **Text:** Sensor status, song title, weather description

Almost every setting in Dashboard Studio can be connected to a topic to make it dynamic. While that makes the editor extraordinarily flexible, you do not need to wire anything manually in this tutorial. The built-in automatic systems will do all the heavy lifting for you.

---

### Step 1: Enable capabilities in Homey

::: p #step-1-enable-capabilities-in-homey
Dashboard Studio only receives data for capabilities you explicitly enable. This keeps your home network fast, lightweight, and secure.
:::

![content: Homey Configuration capability selection](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_homey_settings.jpg)

* Open the **Homey App** on your computer or mobile device.
* Navigate to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration**.
* Expand the devices you want to control or monitor.
* Check the box beside each capability you want on your dashboard.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Less is more:**

Only enable the capabilities you genuinely want to display. If you only want to see the temperature of a bedroom sensor, check **Temperature** and leave humidity, battery, or tamper alarm unchecked. This keeps your setup clean and organized.
:::

#### Controlling lights the easy way

If you want individual widgets for every single light attribute (such as separate sliders for brightness, color tone, or color intensity), you can enable each capability individually.

However, Dashboard Studio also features a dedicated, all-in-one [Light Grid](help://Widgets/lightgrid) widget. This widget controls power, dimming, and color controls in a single compact interface using a special capability called **[Unified Light State (JSON)](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state)**.

* **Helpful Tip:** In the Homey **Configuration** tab, type `unified` into the filter box at the top. This immediately displays the Unified Light State capability for all your lights so you can enable them with one click.

#### Flows, Moods, and User Variables

If you also want to start flows, set zone moods, or update Homey logic variables directly from your dashboard, Homey requires a [Personal API Key](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#creating-a-personal-api-key). You can generate this key in your Homey account and paste it into **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings**.

---

### Step 2: Open Dashboard Studio

::: p #step-2-open-dashboard-studio
Dashboard Studio is accessible from any web browser on your local home network.
:::

![content: Url Location](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_url_location.jpg)

* In Homey **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration**, locate your dashboard web address at the top of the page.
* Click the link or type the URL into your browser (for example `http://192.168.1.50:5050/editor.html`).
* On a fresh installation, Dashboard Studio greets you with an interactive demonstration dashboard. Each widget displays sample data so you can see how it looks and behaves.
* You never need to worry about losing this demo. You can reopen it at any time by loading `demo.json` from the dashboard file menu in the editor.

---

### Step 3: Enter Edit Mode

::: p #step-3-enter-edit-mode
To start designing your own dashboard, switch into Edit Mode.
:::
![content: Step 3: Enter Edit Mode](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_3_enter_edit_mode.jpg)

* Click the round **Edit Mode** button with the gear icon located in the bottom right corner of the screen (or press `Ctrl+E` on your keyboard).
* The editor panel slides open on the left side of your screen.
* While Edit Mode is active, you can freely click, move, and resize widgets.
* Interactive actions (such as tapping buttons or sliding dimmers) are temporarily paused so you can adjust your layout without accidentally triggering devices in your home.

---

### Step 4: Start the Reset Canvas Wizard

::: p #step-4-start-the-reset-canvas-wizard
The Reset Canvas Wizard guides you through creating a fresh dashboard layout step by step.
:::

![content: Step 4: Start the Reset Canvas Wizard](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_4_start_the_reset_canvas_wizard.jpg)

* In the left editor panel under the dashboard tools, click the red **Reset Canvas** button.
* If you have not enabled any device capabilities in Homey yet, the wizard presents an **Enable Capabilities First** notice. Return to Step 1, turn on a few device capabilities, and click **Reset Canvas** again.
* If capabilities are already active, the 4-step wizard opens automatically.

---

### Step 5: Choose Basic Mode

::: p #step-5-choose-basic-mode
Keep your editing experience simple, focused, and beginner-friendly.
:::

![content: Step 5: Choose Basic Mode](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_5_choose_basic_mode.jpg)

* The first screen asks you to select your editor experience: **Basic Mode** or **Advanced Mode**.
* Select **Basic Mode** (highlighted with the badge **Recommended for beginners**).
* Basic Mode hides hundreds of complex styling properties, formulas, and technical options. It shows only the essential controls you need to create a beautiful dashboard.
* You can switch back and forth between Basic and Advanced modes at any time without losing any settings.
* Click **Next**.

---

### Step 6: Choose your Layout Mode and screen size

::: p #step-6-choose-your-layout-mode-and-screen-size
Select how your widgets are arranged and sized across the screen.
:::
![content: Step 6: Choose your Layout Mode and screen size](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_6_choose_your_layout_mode_and_screen_size.jpg)

Dashboard Studio supports three distinct [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes):

* **Fixed Resolution:** The default choice for wall-mounted tablets and displays. It provides complete, pixel-accurate control over the exact position and size of every widget on your canvas.
* **Scale to Fit Screen:** You design on a fixed canvas just like Fixed Resolution, but during viewing the dashboard automatically scales proportionally to fill the entire screen on any phone, tablet, or monitor.
* **Responsive Columns:** Arranges widgets into fluid columns that reflow vertically when the browser window or phone is rotated or resized. This is the ideal option for browser startpages featuring [bookmarks](help://Widgets/switch#1-mode-behavior), [RSS news feeds](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/rss-news-reader), search engines, and notes.

You can freely switch between **Fixed Resolution** and **Scale to Fit Screen** later in Dashboard Settings. Switching to **Responsive Columns** requires organizing widgets into columns because some widgets are designed specifically for freeform positioning.

* Choose **Fixed Resolution** or **Scale to Fit Screen**.
* Pick a screen size preset that matches your tablet or monitor (such as iPad Air 1180x820 or Full HD 1920x1080), or enter custom dimensions.
* Click **Next**.

---

### Step 7: Pick a theme style

::: p #step-7-pick-a-theme-style
Themes give your dashboard an instant, professional appearance with harmonious colors.
:::

![content: Step 7: Pick a theme style](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_7_pick_a_theme_style.jpg)

* Browse the visual theme cards (such as Default Dark, Midnight, Slate, or Cyberpunk).
* Select the color style you like best.
* Your widgets will automatically use matching backgrounds, text colors, and vibrant accent highlights.
* You can easily change this theme later in the editor toolbar or customize individual [Theme Colors](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#theme-colors-semantic-tokens).
* Click **Next**.

---

### Step 8: Select widgets in the Auto-Widget Gallery

::: p #step-8-select-widgets-in-the-auto-widget-gallery
The Auto-Widget Gallery automatically matches your incoming Homey device data with the best widget types.
:::

![content: Step 8: Select widgets in the Auto-Widget Gallery](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_8_select_widgets_in_the_auto_widget_gallery.jpg)

* Dashboard Studio inspects your active Homey capabilities and proposes ready-to-use widgets:
  * Temperature sensors become stylish [Gauges](help://Widgets/gauge).
  * On/off switches and plugs become [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) widgets.
  * All lights with Unified Light State are combined into a single, organized [Light Grid](help://Widgets/lightgrid).
* **Customize suggestions:** Hover over any card in the gallery to choose an alternative visual preset, or pick a different widget type from the dropdown menu.
* **Choose what to include:** Place a checkmark on each widget you want to place on your canvas.
* Click the blue **Create Dashboard** button.

---

### Step 9: Arrange and customize your canvas

::: p #step-9-arrange-and-customize-your-canvas
Your selected widgets are now placed directly on your canvas.
:::

![content: Step 9: Arrange and customize your canvas](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_9_arrange_and_customize_your_canvas.jpg)

* **Moving and Resizing:** Click and drag any widget to position it. Grab any corner handle to make a widget wider or taller.
* **Widget Presets:** Click on any widget to select it. In the left inspector panel, click through the [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets) carousel to transform its look with a single click.
* **Fixed Aspect Widgets:** Certain circular widgets like the [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge) maintain strict circular proportions rather than freeform stretching. To change their size, select the widget and pick one of the size presets in the left panel.

---

### Step 10: Basic Mode versus Advanced Mode

::: p #step-10-basic-mode-versus-advanced-mode
Basic Mode keeps your workspace clean, while Advanced Mode gives you complete creative freedom.
:::

![content: Step 10: Basic Mode versus Advanced Mode](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_10_basic_mode_versus_advanced_mode.jpg)

While in Basic Mode, only the most essential settings are visible. When you want to explore deeper customization:

* **For a single widget:** Select the widget and click **Show advanced settings** at the bottom of the inspector panel to reveal detailed appearance and behavior slideouts.
* **For the entire editor:** Click anywhere on the empty canvas background. The left sidebar displays **Dashboard Settings**. Scroll down to the **Environment** section, find **Editor Mode**, and select **Advanced**. You can return to **Basic** just as easily at any time.

---

### Step 11: Save your dashboard and display it

::: p #step-11-save-your-dashboard-and-display-it
Make sure to save your new dashboard to your Homey hub.
:::

![content: Step 11: Save your dashboard and display it](help/images/basic_beginners_tutorial_step_11_save_your_dashboard_and_display_it.jpg)

* In the left sidebar, click **Save to Homey**.
* Enter a name and confirm. If you save your layout as `dashboard` (or `Dashboard`), it automatically becomes your default home dashboard whenever you open Dashboard Studio.
* You can save as many different dashboards as you want, such as dedicated layouts for tablets, mobile phones, or wall displays. Every saved layout is directly accessible using [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters#1-load-dashboard-dashboard-or-cfg) with `?dashboard=name`.
* Click the gear button in the bottom right corner (or press `Ctrl+E`) to exit Edit Mode and interact with your new live dashboard.
* To display your dashboard on a dedicated wall tablet without editor controls or browser bars, click **Viewer URL** in the editor toolbar or explore our guide on [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display).

---

### Where to go from here

Congratulations on building your first Homey dashboard. When you are ready to expand your dashboard with multi-page navigation, custom flows, and advanced styling, explore these comprehensive guides:

* **[Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide):** Our in-depth walkthrough covering device binding, flow integration, and kiosk mounting.
* **[Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29):** Learn how MQTT topics and Homey capabilities link directly to widget properties.
* **[Homey Flow Cards](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards):** Trigger flows on button taps, stream Insights graphs, and show calendar schedules.
* **[Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes):** Explore Fixed, Scale, and Responsive column architectures.
* **[Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets):** Discover built-in preset libraries and create your own design packs.

widgetSubpages.title: Homey: The Complete Guide [badge: Homey Pro]
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Homey Guide](help/images/header_homey.jpg)

::: lead
Welcome. This walkthrough takes you from a blank canvas to a live Homey dashboard. You will enable two devices, place a temperature [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge) and a light [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#1-mode-behavior), bind live [topics](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29), then open a [kiosk](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display) view.
:::

Blue text links directly to detailed reference pages. Feel free to stay here and finish this walkthrough first.

### What you will do

* [Enable devices](#help-step-1) in Homey so Dashboard Studio can see them
* [Open a blank canvas](#help-step-2) and pick Advanced Mode, Fixed Resolution, and a theme
* [Add a Gauge](#help-step-3) for temperature
* [Bind the temperature topic](#help-step-4) so the Gauge updates live
* [Add a Switch](#help-step-5) to turn a light on and off
* [Use pages](#help-step-6) when one screen is not enough
* [Sync theme colors](#help-step-7) to a colored light
* [Talk to Homey Flows](#help-step-8)
* [Save the file](#help-step-9), then open it as a [kiosk](#help-step-10)

### How it works

Dashboard Studio runs as a web app hosted locally on your Homey. You design and monitor dashboards straight from any web browser. Homey publishes values (numbers, text, boolean states, and more) to specific [topics](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29). Canvas widgets listen to those topics and update in real time.

![content: Homey on the left, Dashboard Studio in the browser on the right](help/images/architecture.jpg)

The setup covers two distinct sides:

* **Homey (left):** Under **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration**, you choose which device capabilities to expose. Every enabled capability creates a dedicated [topic](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#enabling-items-in-configuration).
* **Dashboard Studio (right):** The web workspace where you place [widgets](help://Widgets), style the layout, and bind topics.

::: alert info tag
**What is a topic?**

A topic functions like a named mailbox for data, similar to a Homey variable or tag. Dashboard Studio uses the term **topic** because it matches standard [MQTT](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29) terminology. The editor supports MQTT over WebSockets alongside native Homey communication.
:::

You can also send values directly from [Homey Flows](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards). Dedicated flow cards support booleans, numbers, strings, [Insight](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/insights) graph JSON, and [calendar](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/calendar-ical) [Markdown](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting). Any payload you push becomes an accessible topic in the dashboard.

#### Styling hierarchy

Styling uses a three-tier cascade to save you from formatting widgets individually:

* **[Theme Colors](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#theme-colors-semantic-tokens)** sit at the root level. Changing **Background** or **Accent** automatically propagates to every matching element.
* **Master defaults** live in **Dashboard Settings**. If you have several [Gauges](help://Widgets/gauge), tweaking the Gauge master profile updates all of them at once.
* **Individual widgets** can override specific attributes. Overridden settings ignore the master profile until you click the **Reset** icon :ph-bold ph-arrow-counter-clockwise text-slate-400: beside the input field.

### Step 1: Enable devices

::: p #help-step-1
Dashboard Studio only receives data for capabilities you explicitly enable. This keeps network traffic light and secures your setup.
:::

![content: Homey Configuration with devices and capabilities](help/images/homey_config_app.jpg)

* Open the **Homey App** in your browser (desktop works best).
* Go to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration**.
* Expand a temperature sensor and check **Temperature**.
* Expand a light and check **Turned on**.

Every capability shows its access permission badge:

::: access-legend
* [access: R] **Read only**. The dashboard displays the value.
* [access: W] **Write only**. The dashboard sends commands.
* [access: RW] **Read / write**. The dashboard displays status and transmits commands back.
:::

::: alert info clipboard-text
**Copy Topic**

Click **Copy Topic** beside any enabled capability to save its path to your clipboard for quick pasting. You can also pick it later inside the [Data Stream Explorer](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#10-data-stream-explorer).
:::

#### User Variables and Flows in Configuration

Homey **Variables** appear near the bottom of the configuration list. By default, they have [access: R] **Read only** status, allowing your dashboard to display live values on gauges, labels, and graphs. Directly beneath Variables, Homey also lists all your **Flows** and Advanced Flows as [access: W] **Write only** trigger channels.

To enable two-way [access: RW] **Read / write** access for variables and to unlock direct flow execution, you can add a **Personal API Key** in the **Settings** tab.

#### Why a Personal API Key is Necessary

Homey enforces a strict security sandbox for third-party applications. When Dashboard Studio runs on your Homey, it uses Homey's built-in application token. Athom grants this application token read-only permission to inspect logic variables and read flow names. However, Athom strictly forbids third-party app tokens from modifying variables or triggering flows directly.

To perform those administrative actions, Homey requires owner-level authorization. Athom provides this through Personal API Keys, which you create in the Homey Web App. A Personal API Key carries your personal account credentials. When you provide this key to Dashboard Studio, the app connects to Homey's local interface using your authorized permissions.

This unlocks two capabilities:
* **Two-way Variables**: Variables upgrade to [access: RW] **Read / write**. You can bind switches to boolean flags, sliders to numbers, and edit boxes to text. Changes on your dashboard immediately update the variable in Homey.
* **Direct Flow Triggering**: The **Flows** section below Variables becomes available with [access: W] **Write only** trigger channels.

#### Setting Up Your Personal API Key

1. Open the **Homey Web App** in your browser.
2. Go to **Settings** and select **API Keys**.
3. Create a new key, making sure to grant access to **Variables** and **Flows**.
4. In the Homey app, go to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings tab**.
5. Paste your key into the **Personal API Key** field and click outside the box.
6. A green **OK** badge confirms that Homey verified your key locally.

If the key is ever revoked or entered incorrectly, a red **Wrong** badge appears and the key remains unused. Variables safely revert to read-only status until a valid key is provided.

### Step 2: Canvas and connection

::: p #help-step-2
In Homey Settings, find your local web link at the top under **Open your local dashboard:**. The address looks like `http://[local IP]:5050/`.
:::

![content: Local dashboard URL in Homey Settings](help/images/homey_local_dashboard_url.jpg)

* Open that URL to launch Dashboard Studio.

The interface opens with a pre-configured **demo** layout using simulated data. We will replace this with a clean dashboard containing your temperature [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge) and light [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#1-mode-behavior).

* Click the **Gear** :ph-bold ph-gear: at the bottom right to open the [editor](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide) sidebar.

![content: Reset Canvas in the editor](help/images/homey_reset_canvas.jpg)

* Click **Reset Canvas** and confirm when prompted.

The setup wizard will appear.

![content: Wizard step 1, Basic Mode or Advanced Mode](help/images/homey_wizard_editor_mode.jpg)
**Basic Mode** focuses on quick [presets](help://Widgets/presets) and hides granular controls. **Advanced Mode** exposes every panel and custom property. Choose **Advanced Mode** here to see the full toolset. You can always change this later in **Editor Environment** or per widget.

* Select **Advanced Mode** and click **Next**.

![content: Wizard step 2, layout mode](help/images/homey_wizard_layout_mode.jpg)

Next, choose your [Layout Mode](help://Layout%20Modes):

* **Fixed Resolution:** Places widgets on an exact pixel grid. Ideal for dedicated wall tablets.
* **Scale to Fit Screen:** Uses the same pixel grid, scaling the entire canvas proportionally to fill the browser window.
* **[Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns):** Organizes widgets in a reflowing column grid using **Order**, **Column Span**, and **Preferred Column**. Best for desktop browsers and variable window sizes. See the [Responsive Website: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/responsive-website-complete-guide) walkthrough.

::: alert warning warning-circle
**Pick the layout you really want**

**Fixed Resolution** and **Scale to Fit Screen** share identical coordinate structures, so you can freely toggle between them. Switching to **Responsive Columns** forces elements into grid columns, which prevents freeform overlapping unless you [group](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#6-selected-widget-tools) widgets beforehand.
:::

* Pick **Fixed Resolution**.
* Click **Next**.

![content: Wizard step 3, choose a theme](help/images/homey_wizard_theme.jpg)

The third step is **Choose Your Theme Style**. Pick a look from the preview grid. **My Themes** appear first when you have any, then **Built-in Themes**. You can change this later from **[Theme](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#help-theme-explorer)**.

* Choose **Default Dark** (or another theme).
* Click **Next**.

![content: Step 2: Canvas and connection 7](help/images/homey_the_complete_guide_step_2_canvas_and_connection_7.jpg)

The fourth step is **Populate Your Canvas**. Here, the [Auto-Widget Gallery](help://Tools/auto-widget-gallery) displays ready-made widgets generated automatically from your incoming Homey topics.

Because this tutorial teaches you how to design your own dashboard from scratch, leave all checkboxes unselected and click **Create Dashboard**.

You now have a clean blank canvas.

![content: Dashboard Environment and Platform Connection](help/images/homey_canvas_settings2.jpg)

* Click an empty area of the canvas, or select **⚙️ Dashboard Settings** in the **Selected Widget** dropdown.
* Open **Platform Connection** and make sure **Platform** is set to **Homey**.
* Open **Dashboard Environment**.
* Set your target **Width** and **Height**, or select a **Resolution Preset**.
* Open **Editor Environment**.
* Keep **Snap to Grid** enabled (default **Grid Size** `10` px) for clean alignment. **Show Grid Overlay** draws the same grid on the canvas. You can turn snap off anytime or type exact values under **Layout & Dimensions**.

### Step 3: Add a Gauge

::: p #help-step-3
Add a [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge) widget to monitor temperature.
:::

![content: Create Widget dropdown with Gauge selected](help/images/homey_create_widget.jpg)

* Open the **Create Widget** menu.
* Select **Gauge** and click **Add**.

![content: New Gauge in the center of the canvas](help/images/homey_gauge_on_canvas.jpg)

The Gauge will appear selected in the center of your screen, loading its properties into the inspector panel.

* Deselect by clicking the canvas background whenever you want global settings back.
* Drag the widget to reposition it.
* Drag the blue bounding handles to resize it.
* Open **Layout & Dimensions** to enter exact X, Y, Width, and Height values manually.

![content: Gauge presets and sub-presets](help/images/homey_gauge_presets.jpg)

* Open **Presets** under the **Widget** tab to try pre-built designs.

### Step 4: Bind the temperature

::: p #help-step-4
Connect the Gauge to your live Homey sensor [topic](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor) so it displays real values.
:::

* Click the canvas background to reveal **Dashboard Settings**.
* Open the **Data Stream Explorer**.

![content: Data Stream Explorer with live topics](help/images/homey_data_stream_explorer.jpg)

Your two enabled capabilities will show up in this list.

* Hover over the temperature entry.
* Click the **Tag** icon :ph-bold ph-tag text-slate-400: to copy the topic name.
* Select the Gauge on your canvas.

::: alert info link
**Almost any setting can be live**

Clicking the **Link** icon :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400: converts regular fields into live [topic](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor) subscriptions. You can bind numbers, colors, strings, dimensions, icons, or [Visibility](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering).
:::

* Open **Data & Behavior**.
* Hover over **Value** and click the **Link** icon :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400:.

![content: Value field bound to a topic](help/images/homey_bind_value.jpg)

* Paste your copied topic, or pick the temperature topic directly from the dropdown.

The Gauge now tracks live data from Homey.

::: alert info faders
**Need to scale the number?**

Click **Binding Options** :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: next to a bound field to write a [payload formula](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas#numeric-payload-formula) like `value * 1000` for scaling, offset math, or data clamping.
:::

* Change **Max** from `100` down to `30` (or your local room temperature range) for practical visual feedback.

### Step 5: Control a light

::: p #help-step-5
Use a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) to transmit state changes back to Homey.
:::

![content: Create Widget dropdown with Switch / Button selected](help/images/homey_create_switch.jpg)

* From **Create Widget**, add a **Switch / Button**.
* Select the new widget and open **Data & Behavior**.
* Under **Output Topic**, select the light **Turned on** topic created in Step 1.

The canvas remains non-interactive while editing so you can freely select and move items.

* Exit Edit Mode by clicking the **Gear** :ph-bold ph-gear: (or press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>E</kbd>). Hold the backtick key <kbd>`</kbd> anytime to preview interactions without closing the editor.
* Click the switch on and off to verify the physical light responds.

To keep the switch synchronized when lights are turned on or off via wall switches or the mobile app, bind its input state:

* Re-enter the editor via the **Gear** icon.
* Select the switch and open **Data & Behavior**.
* Hover over **State (On/Off)**, click the **Link** icon :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400:, and assign the identical light **Turned on** topic.

![content: Configure Switch / Button selected](help/images/homey_configure_switch.jpg)

The button now provides true two-way sync with Homey.

Use the settings panel to change the switch behavior from a toggle to a momentary **Push Button**, adjust visual themes, assign icons, or add sound triggers via the [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery).

### Step 6: Pages

::: p #help-step-6
Use [Pages](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#8-page-navigator-utilities) to structure complex dashboards across multiple screens.
:::

![content: Page(s) field and page navigator](help/images/homey_pages.jpg)

* Select a widget and configure its visibility in **Page(s)**:
    * `1` displays it only on page 1
    * `1, 2, 3` shares it across specific pages (useful for status bars and navigation docks)
    * `1, 2, 7-12` supports mixed ranges
* Add or remove views using **Insert Page** and **Delete Page** in Universal Actions. The editor automatically handles index shifts.
* Relocate selected elements to different views using **Move to Page** :ph-bold ph-arrow-square-out:.
* Build custom navigation using a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) set to **Go to Page**, or place a persistent [Menu](help://Widgets/menu).
* In **Dashboard Environment**, map **Active Page** to a topic like `homey/event/page` to automate remote page switching across your displays.
* Link straight to specific views with URL query parameters such as `?page=2`, detailed in [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters#2-jump-to-page-page).

### Step 7: Theme colors

::: p #help-step-7
Select from ready-made color palettes or construct a custom scheme from scratch.
:::

Color definitions follow the standard hierarchy:

* **[Theme Colors](help://Styling%20%26%20Layering#theme-colors-semantic-tokens)** govern the system-wide palette (**Background**, **Background Accent**, **Border Accent**).
* **Master defaults** bind individual widget types to these global tokens or custom static hex codes.
* **Widget overrides** adjust colors on isolated components while keeping the rest of the canvas unified.

Colors can also update [dynamically](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/dynamic-colors) based on room conditions or ambient fixtures.

To drive dashboard accents from an RGB lamp:

* Open **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration** in Homey.
* Select an RGB or RGBW fixture and check **Unified Light State (JSON)**.

![content: Light capabilities including Unified Light State](help/images/homey_light_capabilities.jpg)

::: alert info lightbulb
**[Unified Light State](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/unified-light-state)**

This data bundle groups power state, brightness, hue, saturation, and color temperature into one readable payload.
:::

* Click **Copy Topic**.
* Return to the canvas editor, open **Dashboard Settings**, and expand **Theme Colors**.
* Hover over **Background**, click the **Link** icon :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400:, and paste the copied path.

![content: Background bound to Unified Light State](help/images/homey_theme_bind_background.jpg)

Changing the bulb color will immediately shift the background tone. If the backdrop becomes too bright:

* Click **Binding Options** :ph-bold ph-faders text-cyan-400: on the **Background** row.
* Turn on **Apply Corrections** under **Color Adjustments**.
* Dial back **Brightness**, or set it to **Fix** so light intensity changes do not wash out the canvas.

![content: Color Adjustments for color tone, color intensity, and brightness](help/images/homey_color_correction.jpg)

To build a polished accent gradient:

* Map **Background Accent** to the same light topic, tweaking color tone and brightness offsets.
* Map **Border Accent** to the light topic with elevated brightness for crisp borders.

### Step 8: Homey Flows

::: p #help-step-8
Integrate dashboard elements directly with Homey automation logic using direct flow triggers or [Homey Flow Cards](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards).
:::

![content: Dashboard Studio cards in the Homey Flow editor](help/images/homey_flows.jpg)

#### Direct Flow Triggering

The fastest way to start a Homey Flow is to trigger it directly from a dashboard widget without building intermediate bridge flows.

* In **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Configuration**, expand the **Flows** section.
* Check the **Trigger** box beside each flow you want to control from your dashboard.
* In the dashboard editor, place a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) or [Menu](help://Widgets/menu).
* Bind its **Output Topic** to your flow's trigger topic (for example `good-night/trigger`).
* Tapping the widget starts the flow immediately in Homey.

::: alert info timer
**10-Second Cooldown Limiter**

Every direct flow trigger includes a built-in 10-second cooldown per flow. Once a flow runs, subsequent taps on that same flow within 10 seconds are safely ignored. This protects your Homey from being overwhelmed by accidental double-taps or rapid button presses.
:::

Direct flow triggers require a valid [Personal API Key](#setting-up-your-personal-api-key) configured in the **Settings** tab. If no key is set, the Flows section displays a reminder to add one.

#### Dashboard to Homey (When...)

* Add a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) and set **Mode** to **Push Button (Momentary)**.
* Set **Output Topic** to an event identifier, like `movie_scene`.
* In Homey Flow editor, add the trigger card **Dashboard Studio 'movie_scene' triggered**.

::: alert info info
**Three tags, one value**

Trigger cards automatically map received values across **Text**, **Number**, and **Boolean** tags depending on what gets passed from the canvas.
:::

Widgets configured with click actions like **Go to Page** or **Open URL** can still simultaneously publish an **Output Topic**.

#### Homey to Dashboard (Then...)

* In your flow action, add **Send 'alert' with value 'Door Open' to Dashboard**.
* Place a [Text](help://Widgets/text) or [List / Log](help://Widgets/list) widget on your canvas.
* Bind the widget content field to `homey/event/alert`.

To push metrics to a [Graph](help://Widgets/graph), use the Send Insight action. Review [Data Types & Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats) for list, chart, and [Markdown](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting) schema specifications.

### Step 9: Save and files

::: p #help-step-9
Your completed layout is saved directly on your Homey hub as a JSON configuration file.
:::

![content: Save to Homey and Load from Homey](help/images/homey_save_to_homey.jpg)

* Click **Save to Homey**.
* Name the layout `dashboard` to load it as your default workspace.

You can manage multiple profiles (such as `wallpanel` or `phone`) and target them directly via URL arguments like `?dashboard=name`, explained in [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters#1-load-dashboard-dashboard-or-cfg).

* To review older iterations, open **Load from Homey** and expand **Previous Versions** to restore automatic backups.

Configure version history limits via **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings** under **Maximum Snapshots To Keep** (default is 10). Download local `.json` exports whenever you want permanent archival backups on your computer.

![content: File Manager in Homey Settings](help/images/homey_file_manager.jpg)

Use the **File Manager** inside Homey Settings to manage dashboards, custom themes, [images](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager), and [audio](help://Audio%20Gallery) assets. The default **demo** file is permanent and protected from deletion.

### Step 10: Kiosk mode

::: p #help-step-10
Run the finished dashboard in full-screen display mode without toolbars or edit controls.
:::

![content: Viewer URL in the editor](help/images/homey_kiosk_viewer.jpg)

* Click **Viewer URL** in the editor toolbar to open or copy the display link (`/viewer.html`).
* Alternatively, navigate directly:

::: code-block Example
http://192.168.1.50:5050/viewer.html?dashboard=dashboard
:::

Swap the IP address and target configuration name to match your environment.

To permanently lock client devices to display-only mode:

* Go to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings**.
* Check **Viewer mode only**.
* Keep `/editor.html` bookmarked on your admin computer for design changes.

See [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display) for fullscreen browser flags and tablet mounting suggestions.

### Step 11: Outside your network

::: p #help-step-11
The dashboard operates locally on your LAN by default. Accessing it remotely requires routing external traffic through your home gateway.
:::

Direct port forwarding exposes your dashboard port to the open internet. If you use port forwarding, configure a [Security Token](help://Security%20%26%20Remote%20Access#1-the-security-token) to require token authentication in the URL string. Setting up a WireGuard or Tailscale VPN back to your local network remains the most secure method for off-site access.

Refer to [Security & Remote Access](help://Security%20%26%20Remote%20Access#4-the-recommended-approach) for detailed remote networking configurations.

widgetSubpages.title: Responsive Website: The Complete Guide
widgetSubpages.content:
![header: Responsive Website Guide](help/images/header_responsive_website.jpg)

::: lead
Learn how to build a flexible browser start page and responsive dashboard in Dashboard Studio. This walkthrough covers the responsive grid layout, adding web bookmarks in batch with live favicons, clock banners, live RSS news feeds, cell height modes, smart home controls, widget scale modes, and multi-engine search bars that reflow automatically to any browser window or screen resolution.
:::

### The responsive difference

::: p #help-responsive-difference
Unlike a dedicated wall tablet that runs at a locked pixel resolution, a responsive dashboard behaves like a modern website. It automatically reorganizes and resizes widgets whenever you resize your browser window, switch between laptop and desktop monitors, or view your page on a mobile device.
:::

![content: Responsive start page layout with bookmarks, clock, and smart home controls](help/images/responsive_startpage_overview.jpg)

Designing in [Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns) involves a different design mindset:

* You trade absolute pixel coordinates for structured grid columns that flow naturally.
* Widgets automatically rearrange into fewer columns when the window becomes narrow.
* You can combine everyday web tools (bookmarks, search engines, clocks, and weather) with smart home domotica controls (lighting scenes, heating adjustments, and window blind sliders) on a single homepage.

---

### Step 1: Start fresh with the Reset Canvas Wizard

::: p #help-step-1-reset
To begin with a clean workspace, reset your canvas to the responsive layout mode.
:::

![content: Reset Canvas Wizard layout step](help/images/responsive_reset_wizard.jpg)

1. Click **Reset Canvas** in the top toolbar or quick actions.
2. In the **Reset Canvas Wizard**, pick **Advanced** under **Editor Mode**. This ensures you have full access to all responsive cell properties.
3. On the next step, select **Responsive Columns** under **Layout Mode**.
4. Choose your favorite **Theme** and click **Create Dashboard**.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Changing layout settings later**
You do not need to reset your dashboard if you want to modify your layout later. Open the left sidebar, navigate to **Dashboard Environment**, and expand **Layout Mode**. You can fine-tune column counts, minimum widths, gaps, or switch between layout modes at any time without losing any of your placed widgets.
:::

---

### Step 2: Grid architecture and column strategy

::: p #help-step-2-columns
In **Responsive Columns**, every widget sits inside a column grid cell. Understanding column distribution makes designing intuitive and versatile.
:::

![content: Column grid architecture diagram](help/images/responsive_grid_columns.jpg)

#### The 6 or 9 column technique
When planning a dashboard with three main columns of content, do not set your grid to 3 columns. Instead, set **Column Count** to **6** or **9** in **Dashboard Environment**.

Using a higher column count unlocks enormous layout flexibility:
* Set your primary content widgets (like bookmark groups or charts) to a **Column Span** of `2` on a 6-column grid, or `3` on a 9-column grid. This gives you three balanced visual columns.
* Set compact widgets (like single scene buttons or mini sensor indicators) to a **Column Span** of `1`. This allows small controls to sit neatly side by side in the grid without stretching.
* Set wide elements (like header clocks, search bars, or alert banners) to a **Column Span** of `6` or `9` to span the entire screen width.

#### Key grid settings in Dashboard Environment

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Column Count:** The maximum number of columns shown on wide screens (recommended: `6` or `9`).
* [button ph-check-square] **Reduce Columns to Fit:** Automatically reduces active columns when the display width drops below **Min Column Width**. This prevents horizontal scrollbars on mobile phones and narrow browser splits.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Min Column Width:** The minimum pixel width required for each column before the grid drops a column.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Max Column Width:** Caps maximum column growth. Set to `0` to let columns expand and fill the entire window frame.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Column Alignment:** Determines how columns align (**Left**, **Center**, **Right**, or **Stretch**) when the dashboard has fixed width limits.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Gap (px):** Spacing in pixels between adjacent grid cells.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Page Padding:** Outer margin insets around the dashboard perimeter (Left, Right, Top, and Bottom).
:::

#### Per-widget placement controls
Select any widget to customize its cell under **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**:

::: grid
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Column Span:** The number of grid columns this cell occupies.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Preferred Column:** Set to `0` for automatic grid flow. Set to a specific column number (`1`, `2`, `3`...) to request that column. If the column has space, the widget sits there. If not, it flows dynamically to the next opening and returns when space allows.
* [button ph-number-square-five] **Order:** Controls the visual sequence within columns. Widgets with lower order numbers appear first.
* [button ph-caret-down] **Cell Height Mode:** **Auto** sizes the cell to match its inner content. **Fixed** enforces an exact pixel height. **Fill** expands downward to occupy remaining vertical space.
:::

---

### Step 3: Bookmarks with the Menu widget and batch import

::: p #help-step-3-bookmarks
Create an organized bookmark launchpad for all your favorite websites using the [Menu](help://Widgets/menu) widget.
:::

![content: Batch Add Weblinks dialog with URL list and options](help/images/responsive_batch_weblinks.jpg)

1. Click **+ Add Widget** in the top bar and select **Menu**.
2. In the widget inspector, expand **Data & Behavior**.
3. Under **Menu Items**, click the **Batch Add Weblinks** button.
4. In the dialog, paste your URLs (one URL per line). You can optionally add a comma and a title after each URL.

::: code-block
https://github.com, GitHub
https://news.ycombinator.com, Hacker News
https://homey.app
https://www.youtube.com, YouTube
:::

5. Configure the batch options:
   * **Use favicon from site:** Fetches official website icons automatically through high-resolution favicon caching.
   * **Use title from site if not provided:** Automatically retrieves the website title in the background, falling back to clean domain names.
   * **Open in new tab:** Ensures that clicking your bookmarks opens the destination site in a new browser tab.
6. Click **OK** to generate all bookmark items instantly.

---

### Step 4: Widget Presets for bookmark styling

::: p #help-step-4-presets
Transform the look of your bookmark launcher instantly using [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets).
:::

![content: Menu widget presets showing list and icon grid styles](help/images/responsive_menu_presets.jpg)

1. Select your bookmark menu widget and click the **Presets** button on the quick toolbar.
2. Choose a layout that fits your workflow:
   * **List:** Displays bookmarks as a clean vertical list with icons aligned beside text labels.
   * **Icon Grid:** Renders bookmarks as compact app tiles with icons placed directly above labels.
   * **Horizontal Menu:** Arranges bookmarks side by side in a sleek navigation bar.
3. Fine-tune your bookmark appearance:
   * In **Appearance**, adjust **Background Color**, **Background Opacity**, and **Border Radius** to blend with your wallpaper.
   * In **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**, set **Column Span** to `2` or `3` to match your column strategy.
   * Under **Menu Items**, drag items up or down to reorder your bookmarks.

---

### Step 5: Full-width clock banner and live RSS news feeds

::: p #help-step-5-clock-news
Add live time, date, and news information across the top of your start page.
:::

![content: Wide clock widget banner and live RSS news feed](help/images/responsive_clock_rss.jpg)

#### Adding a prominent clock
1. Click **+ Add Widget** and select [Clock](help://Widgets/clock).
2. In **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**, set **Column Span** to `6` (or `9`) to span the entire top width of your dashboard.
3. In **Data & Behavior**, select your desired clock mode (**Digital**, **Flip Clock**, or **Analog**).
4. In **Appearance** and **Text & Typography**, choose 12-hour or 24-hour time format, show date, and adjust font size.
5. In **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**, set **Scale Mode** to **Rescale**. This keeps your clock numerals and date label proportionally sized when resizing your browser window.

#### Adding an RSS news feed
A live news feed keeps your browser start page informative and fresh.
1. Add a [Text](help://Widgets/text) widget to your dashboard.
2. Set up the [RSS News Reader](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/rss-news-reader) HomeyScript to fetch headlines from your favorite news source and format them as Markdown.
3. Bind the Text widget content to your news topic.
4. Set **Column Span** to `3` (or `2`) so the news feed sits alongside your bookmarks or widgets.

### Step 6: Controlling vertical space with Cell Height Mode

::: p #help-step-6-cell-height
By default, responsive cells grow vertically with their content. Using **Cell Height Mode** gives you full control over row alignment, scrolling, and vertical balance.
:::

In **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**, every widget has three options for **Cell Height Mode**:

#### Auto (Default)
The cell sizes itself directly to fit its inner content.
* **When to use:** Perfect for single buttons, clocks, short menus, or controls with predictable dimensions.
* **Limitation:** If a widget contains a large amount of content (such as an RSS feed with 20 headlines), **Auto** will stretch the widget down the entire screen, pushing the rest of your dashboard out of view.

#### Fixed
Forces the cell to stay at the exact pixel height typed into **Cell Height** (for example, `340` px).
* **When to use:** Essential for long lists, logs, and RSS news feeds.
* **Result:** Content that exceeds the fixed height stays inside the cell and creates clean vertical scrollbars, keeping your start page neat and compact.

#### Fill
Automatically expands the cell downward to fill any empty vertical space down to the next widget that shares any of its columns.

Imagine placing two text widgets side by side in two columns:
* Column 1 holds a long bookmarks list or RSS news feed.
* Column 2 holds a brief weather summary or quick notes widget that is much shorter.
* Beneath both columns sits a wide widget spanning both columns.

With **Cell Height Mode** left on **Auto**, Column 2 leaves an awkward empty gap above the bottom widget:

![content: Fill mode disabled showing uneven vertical gap](help/images/responsive_fill_mode_off.jpg)

By setting the shorter widget's **Cell Height Mode** to **Fill**, the cell automatically stretches downward to meet the widget below. Both columns align flush and balanced:

![content: Fill mode enabled stretching cell flush to widget below](help/images/responsive_fill_mode_on.jpg)

---

### Step 7: Smart home domotica controls

::: p #help-step-7-domotica
Integrate everyday home controls directly onto your start page so you can adjust lights, blinds, and scenes without leaving your browser.
:::

![content: Smart home sliders and scene buttons in responsive columns](help/images/responsive_domotica_widgets.jpg)

#### Adding a dimmer or blind slider
1. Add a [Slider](help://Widgets/slider) widget to your canvas.
2. Bind the slider to your dimming or window covering topic.
3. In **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**, set **Column Span** to `2` (or `3`).
4. In **Appearance**, select a horizontal or vertical slider track with glowing thumb accents.

#### Adding quick scene buttons
1. Add a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) widget.
2. In **Data & Behavior**, set **Mode** to **Push Button (Momentary)** for scenes or **Toggle Switch** for devices.
3. Set **On Click** to **Send Topic** to trigger your flow or light group.
4. Set **Column Span** to `1` in **Responsive Layout & Dimensions**. Compact single-column buttons slot neatly into your multi-column grid, sitting side by side with sliders or stacked into dedicated control strips.

---

### Step 8: Scale modes explained: Resize vs Rescale

::: p #help-step-8-scale-modes
Widgets in Dashboard Studio were natively created for pixel-accurate positioning. In a responsive column grid, you can choose how each widget adapts to changing cell dimensions.
:::

![content: Comparison of Resize mode and Rescale mode in responsive cells](help/images/responsive_scale_modes.jpg)

Open the **Responsive Layout & Dimensions** slideout on any widget to select its **Scale Mode**:

#### Resize (Default)
The widget container expands and contracts to fill the width of the grid cell. The internal HTML elements reflow according to web styling rules.
* **Best for:** [Menu](help://Widgets/menu) bookmarks, [Text](help://Widgets/text) articles, [List / Log](help://Widgets/list) entries, and [Edit Box](help://Widgets/editbox) fields.
* **Why:** Text wraps naturally, buttons adjust width cleanly, and lists scroll or expand gracefully without distortion.

#### Rescale
The widget treats its original width and height as a virtual design canvas. When placed in a responsive cell, the entire interior scales up or down proportionally from the center to fit the cell width.
* **Best for:** [Clock](help://Widgets/clock), [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge), [Icon](help://Widgets/icon), and composite [Group](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#6-selected-widget-tools) cards.
* **Why:** Outer borders, corner radii, and padding remain sharp at their exact pixel settings, while circular gauges, clock dials, and custom icons maintain their intended geometry without distortion or clipping.

---

### Step 9: Advanced composite cards: Grouping in responsive grids

::: p #help-step-9-groups
Combine multiple related controls into a single cohesive card that moves and scales together.
:::
