![content: Grouped composite card with label, slider, and buttons](help/images/responsive_grouped_card.jpg)

1. Place related widgets on your canvas (for example, a room title label, two scene buttons, and a brightness slider).
2. Select all of them by dragging a selection rectangle or holding Shift while clicking each widget.
3. Click **Group** in the top toolbar.

In **Responsive Columns**, a closed group functions as a **single grid cell**:
* The group receives its own **Responsive Layout & Dimensions** panel. Set its **Column Span** to `2` or `3` to place the entire card into your grid.
* Double-click the group or click **Open Group** to enter the group authoring canvas. Here you have free-form positioning with snap-to-grid to arrange buttons, sliders, and text with pixel precision.
* Click **Close Group** when finished.
* Set the group's **Scale Mode** to **Rescale**. Now your custom multi-widget composition scales uniformly on wide screens, laptops, and mobile phones without disturbing your pixel-aligned layout.

---

### Step 10: Example: Multi-engine search bar with Edit Box and buttons

::: p #help-step-10-search
Add a versatile search engine bar to your homepage that can execute searches across Google, YouTube, Wikipedia, or other engines.
:::

![content: Multi-engine search bar combining Edit Box with search buttons](help/images/responsive_search_bar.jpg)

#### Option A: Quick search on Enter
1. Add an [Edit Box](help://Widgets/editbox) widget.
2. In **Data & Behavior**, set **Send Behavior** to **Open URL**.
3. Set **Prefix URL** to `https://www.google.com/search?q=`.
4. Check **New tab** and set **Clear on Send** if desired.
5. In **Text & Typography**, enter a helpful **Custom Placeholder** such as `Search Google...`.
6. Pressing `Enter` in the box opens your query directly in Google in a new browser tab.

#### Option B: Multi-engine search bar with dedicated buttons
One [Edit Box](help://Widgets/editbox) holds the query and opens the address. Each dedicated [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) selects an engine and triggers the search at the same time. The button sends the search engine address to a single shared topic. That topic updates **Prefix URL** on the Edit Box and immediately triggers it to launch the search in your browser.

Use a single [local topic](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#global-vs-local-topics) so this stays entirely inside the browser: `local/searchtrigger`.

1. Add an [Edit Box](help://Widgets/editbox).
2. In **Data & Behavior**, set **Send Behavior** to **Open URL**.
3. Set **Trigger Topic** to `local/searchtrigger`.
4. On **Prefix URL**, click the **Link Icon** :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400: and bind `local/searchtrigger`.
5. Check **New tab** to open each result in a new browser tab.
6. Turn off **Clear on Send** to keep your search query visible when you want to try another engine.
7. Set **Custom Placeholder** to `Enter your search query...`.
8. Add a [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch) for your first search engine.
9. In **Data & Behavior**, set **Mode** to **Push Button (Momentary)**. Leave **On Click** on **Send Topic**.
10. Set **Output Topic** to `local/searchtrigger`.
11. Set **On Value** to the search query URL of that engine. For Google, enter `https://www.google.com/search?q=`.
12. In **Text & Typography**, set **Button Label** to `Google`. In **Appearance**, set **Visual Style** to **Button (Rect)**.
13. Duplicate the button for each additional search engine. Update each duplicate with its own **Button Label** and **On Value**:
    * Bing: `https://www.bing.com/search?q=`
    * DuckDuckGo: `https://duckduckgo.com/?q=`
    * YouTube: `https://www.youtube.com/results?search_query=`
    * Wikipedia: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Search?search=` (or `https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/`)
14. Type a query into the Edit Box and click any engine button. The button passes its URL to `local/searchtrigger`, updating the search address and opening the result tab instantly.
15. Group the Edit Box and the buttons. Set the group **Column Span** to `2` and **Scale Mode** to `Rescale`.

---

### Step 11: Setting up as your browser homepage

::: p #help-step-11-homepage
Once your responsive dashboard is complete, make it your daily starting point.
:::

1. Save your dashboard configuration by clicking **Save to Homey** (or your local storage).
2. Click **Viewer URL** in the top toolbar to open the clean display view (`/viewer.html?dashboard=...`).
3. Copy the URL from your address bar.
4. In your web browser settings (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari), set your **Homepage** and **New Tab page** to this URL.
5. Test resizing your browser window. Notice how bookmarks reflow, columns compress smoothly, and your smart home controls remain accessible at all times.

---

### Related topics

* [Layout Modes](help://Layout%20Modes) for full technical specifications of fixed, scale, and column engines.
* [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#help-editor-mode) for details on Dashboard Environment, editor mode toggles, and group tools.
* [Widget Presets](help://Widgets/presets) for rapid restyling of menus, clocks, and indicators.
* [RSS News Reader](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/rss-news-reader) for setting up live news feeds with HomeyScript.
* [Binding Options & Payload Formulas](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas) for data transformations and dynamic URLs.
* [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display) for launching full-screen browser sessions without borders or address bars.
* [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters) for controlling startup pages, themes, and tokens through web links.

topics.title: Homey Flow Cards
topics.content:
![header: Homey Flow Cards](help/images/header_flowcards.jpg)

::: lead
Dashboard Studio comes with a dedicated set of flow cards to create powerful bidirectional interactions between your home logic and your interface. Use them to react when someone taps the dashboard, push text and graphs into widgets, refresh layouts remotely, and turn calendar feeds into beautiful Markdown tables on your wall. [badge: Homey Pro]
:::

![content: Flow cards inside the Homey Flow editor](help/images/flowcards_overview.jpg)

### All flow cards at a glance

Each card lives in Homey under the **Dashboard Studio** group when you add a trigger or action. Pick a row below to jump to the chapter that explains it in context.

#### When… (triggers)

* **[Dashboard Studio … triggered](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/send-receive-data#when-dashboard-studio-event-triggered)**: Starts a flow when the dashboard publishes an event name you choose (matches **Output Topic** on buttons, switches, or menu items).
* **[Dashboard Loaded / Refreshed](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/loading-saving#dashboard-loaded-refreshed)**: Runs when a browser opens or refreshes a dashboard file and exposes which file loaded.
* **[Dashboard Saved](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/loading-saving#dashboard-saved)**: Runs after you successfully save a layout to Homey from the editor.

#### Then… (actions)

* **[Send … with value … to Dashboard](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/send-receive-data#then-send-with-value-to-dashboard)**: Sends text, numbers, booleans, or JSON to `homey/event/<your name>` so widgets can bind or embed it.
* **[Send Insight … for … with resolution … to Dashboard](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/insights#send-insight-for-with-resolution-to-dashboard)**: Fetches Homey Insights history and pushes a Graph-ready series to the dashboard.
* **[Get Insight Data (Advanced)](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/insights#get-insight-data-advanced)**: Same data pipeline plus flow tags for raw JSON, min, max, and average.
* **[Reload Dashboard](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/loading-saving#reload-dashboard)**: Tells open browsers to reload a saved dashboard file from Homey (ideal for wall panels after an edit elsewhere).
* **[Load & filter iCal from …](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/calendar-ical#the-calendar-flow-cards)**: Downloads a calendar URL, filters it to a date window, and outputs compact JSON for next steps.
* **[Convert iCal JSON to Markdown](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/calendar-ical#the-calendar-flow-cards)**: Turns filtered events into **Calendar Markdown** for the Text widget.
* **[Combine calendar events from … and …](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/calendar-ical#the-calendar-flow-cards)**: Merges two event payloads (for example two feeds or two loader passes).
* **[Fetch RSS Feed to Markdown](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/rss-feeds)**: Downloads and converts one or more RSS or Atom feeds into a clean Markdown table.

::: alert info book-open
**Topics refresher:** Anything sent with **Send … to Dashboard** arrives on `homey/event/<name>`. Insight snapshots arrive on `homey/insight/<log name>`. If you are new to binding fields, read [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor) and the [Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide) first.
:::

*Deep dives:* [Send & receive data](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/send-receive-data) · [Loading, saving & reload](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/loading-saving) · [Insights](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/insights) · [Calendar & iCal](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/calendar-ical#the-calendar-flow-cards) · [RSS Feeds](help://Homey%20Flow%20Cards/rss-feeds)

widgetSubpages.title: Send & Receive Data
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
These cards form the main bi-directional bridge between Homey Flows and your dashboard widgets: taps and toggles can wake automations, and automations can push fresh values straight into what you see on screen.
:::

### When: Dashboard Studio event triggered

This is the primary way to let Homey react when someone interacts with the dashboard.

* **Event Name:** Pick a short, unique name (for example `cinema_mode`). It must match the **Output Topic** on your Switch, Button, or Menu item when you want Homey to notice that action.
* **Tags:** The card exposes `Value (String)`, `Value (Number)`, and `Value (Boolean)`. Dashboard Studio tries to interpret what was sent so you can wire the tag that fits your next cards.

::: alert info lightbulb
**Example:** A button uses Output Topic `movie_start`. Flow: **When** “Dashboard Studio `movie_start` triggered” → **Then** start your scene or AV routine.
:::

For **Selection Group** toggles (Switch/Button or Menu items), enabling **Send Off When Turned Off by Group** still publishes the “off” payload when another member of the same group becomes active, including when the control uses **Go to Page** or **Open URL** as its tap action.

### Then: Send … with value … to Dashboard

Publishes any payload your widgets can bind to or embed in Markdown.

* **Event Name:** Becomes the last segment of `homey/event/<name>` (for example `homey/event/my_alert`).
* **Value:** Plain text, a number, booleans (`true` / `false`), or richer strings such as JSON for lists. These should match what your widget expects. See [Data Types & Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats) for examples.

::: alert info arrows-out-simple
**Example:** When power drops below 5 W, send event `alert` with value `Laundry done`, then bind a Text or List widget to `homey/event/alert`.
:::

If you type `{{topic/path}}` inside the Text widget body, it will inline live values. This is handy for mixing fixed wording with live data. Full syntax lives under [Widgets → Text](help://Widgets/text).

widgetSubpages.title: Loading, Saving & Reload
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
These cards help your automations notice when dashboards open, when you save work, and when a panel should fetch a fresh file from Homey.
:::

### Dashboard Loaded / Refreshed

Fires whenever a browser loads or manually refreshes your dashboard.

* **Dashboard Name tag:** Tells you which file opened (for example `dashboard` or `wallpanel`).
* **Tip:** App-level **State Caching** already restores the last known widget values quickly after a reload, so you only need extra logic here when you truly want a startup ritual.

### Dashboard Saved

Fires right after a successful **Save to Homey** from the editor. Use it to log changes, notify someone, or chain a reload on another device.

### Reload Dashboard

Asks every connected viewer that currently has the matching file open to reload that JSON from Homey. The name must match the saved file without `.json` (use `tablet` for `tablet.json`).

**Why it matters:** Picture editing a layout on a PC, saving to Homey, and letting a wall tablet or kiosk tucked behind furniture pick up the new design automatically without needing a ladder or a manual refresh. Pair **Dashboard Saved** on the editor side with **Reload Dashboard** aimed at the wall file, or trigger reloads from any other flow when you publish updates.

Reload runs only in display mode. The editor stays put so you do not interrupt an active session accidentally.

widgetSubpages.title: Insights
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
Homey Insights stores histories for many devices. These cards package that history for Dashboard Studio’s Graph widget (and give power-users extra tags).
:::

### Send Insight … for … with resolution … to Dashboard

Pulls a log, resamples it to the number of points you choose, and pushes it to the dashboard.

* **Insight Source:** Pick any Insights log (energy, temperature, logic variables, and more).
* **Time Range:** Includes rolling windows (last hour, last 24 hours, last 7 days, …) and **Today**, which spans midnight-to-midnight local time. Every range is resampled to evenly spaced timestamps across the full period, and stable values are forward-filled from the last known reading. Slots before the first measurement or after the current time (on Today) have no value. The flow card sets `v` to JSON `null` (empty) for those times, so the graph keeps the full time axis but skips draw a line there.
* **Resolution (Datapoints):** Default 20. Fewer points mean lighter work on Homey, while more points look smoother. Samples are spread evenly across the range so the curve stays readable.
* **Custom Topic (Optional):** Optional custom topic identifier. When omitted or left blank, the card publishes to `homey/insight/<log name>` (matching the log title in Homey). When specified, it publishes to `homey/insight/<your topic>`, always keeping the prefix and allowing multiple cards for the same log without topic collision.

Each snapshot is an array of `{ "t": "<ISO timestamp>", "v": <number or null> }` objects. Example (Today, mid-afternoon, where morning and future hours empty):

::: code-block
[
 { "t": "2024-06-01T00:00:00.000Z", "v": null },
 { "t": "2024-06-01T06:00:00.000Z", "v": null },
 { "t": "2024-06-01T12:00:00.000Z", "v": 21.5 },
 { "t": "2024-06-01T18:00:00.000Z", "v": null }
]
:::

The line is drawn from 12:00 onward. Slots with `"v": null` stay on the X axis for timing but show no line, bar, or point. Min / max / average tags ignore null slots.

The snapshot lands on `homey/insight/<log name>` (or your **Custom Topic** if entered). Bind your Graph widget's data topic to that path so each run replaces the chart. Because the card executes once per flow run, schedule it with an **Every X minutes** trigger or another periodic pulse if you want continuous updates.

For the JSON shape and axis tips, open [Graph Data Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/graph-data-formats). When timestamps arrive in UTC, enable local conversion under **Axes & Labels** so labels match your wall clock.

![content: Example Insight graph on a dashboard](help/images/flowcards_insight_graph.jpg)

### Get Insight Data (Advanced)

Same pipeline as above, plus tags for **Raw Data JSON**, **Highest**, **Lowest**, and **Average**. Use it when you want both a refreshed chart and numeric diagnostics for Logic, notifications, or follow-up math. The extra tags also help when you **stack several Graph widgets** (or overlay series) and need every layer to use the **same time range and point count** so the axes line up.

widgetSubpages.title: Calendar & iCal
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
Display your family agendas, school rosters, or work schedules right on your dashboard walls. With Dashboard Studio calendar flow cards, Homey handles all the heavy lifting: downloading your calendar, filtering out unwanted dates, and formatting the events into attractive Markdown tables ready for your Text widgets.
:::

### How calendar settings work

Setting up your calendar views is split into two straightforward parts:

* **Calendar data and formatting options:** How the flow cards process your events is configured in Homey app settings under **More → Apps → Dashboard Studio → Configure App → Calendar**. Here you can set your preferred start of the week (Monday or Sunday), choose your date format, enable event icons, map keyword colors, and define how event details appear.
* **Visual appearance on your dashboard:** How the resulting table actually looks on your screen is configured directly inside the **Text** widget. Open your Text widget settings, expand **Markdown**, and select your favorite **Table Style**. Dashboard Studio offers specialized calendar layouts like **Calendar - Week Planner**, **Calendar - Month View**, or **Calendar - Simple Grid**, as well as clean lists like **Card Rows**, **Timeline View**, or **Minimal**.

### What is an iCal link?

An iCal link (often ending with `.ics` or starting with `webcal://` or `https://`) is an online web address that shares your calendar appointments automatically. Most popular calendar services provide this link so external devices and apps can read your schedule without needing your private account password.

Once you copy this link from your calendar provider, you paste it into the **Load & filter iCal** flow card.

#### Finding your subscription link

* **Google Calendar:** Open Google Calendar in your web browser. Next to your calendar on the left, click the three dots and choose **Settings and sharing**. Scroll down to the **Integrate calendar** section and copy the **Secret address in iCal format**.
* **Apple iCloud Calendar:** Open [icloud.com/calendar](https://www.icloud.com/calendar/) in your web browser. Click the share icon next to your calendar name, turn on **Public Calendar**, and copy the web address shown. On an iPhone or iPad, you can also view subscribed calendars under **Settings → Calendar → Accounts → Subscribed Calendars**.
* **Microsoft Outlook / Office 365:** Open Outlook on the web, click the gear icon for **Settings**, navigate to **Calendar → Shared calendars**, publish your calendar, and copy the **ICS link**.

::: alert warning key
**Privacy reminder:** Anyone who possesses your secret iCal link can view the events on that calendar. Keep these links private and do not share them publicly.
:::

### The calendar flow cards

* **Load & filter iCal from … for …**: Downloads your calendar link, removes any dates outside your selected timeframe, and saves the events into a reusable **Filtered Events (JSON)** flow tag.
* **Convert iCal JSON … to … markdown**: Takes your loaded calendar events and turns them into a clean Markdown table view (such as *Today*, *This week*, or *Month View*) ready to display. You can optionally fill in **Dashboard Topic (Optional)** to send the table straight to `homey/event/<topic>` on your dashboard in a single step.
* **Combine calendar events from … and …**: Merges two event tokens together into one combined schedule so you can display multiple family or work calendars in the same view.

### The two-step workflow

Getting calendar events onto your dashboard follows two easy steps:

1. **First retrieve and filter your events:** Use the **Load & filter iCal** card in your flow. Choose a broad timeframe so all dates you care about are included. This card outputs a **Filtered Events (JSON)** tag.
2. **Then create your Markdown views:** Add one or more **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** cards. Choose the view layout you want (for example *Today* or *This week*). You can either fill in the optional **Dashboard Topic** directly on the card to send the Markdown straight to your dashboard in one step, or pass the resulting **Calendar Markdown** tag to a separate **Send … with value … to Dashboard** card.

### Recommended setup: Download once, show multiple views

Calendar feeds can be quite large. Downloading and parsing them takes processing power on your Homey. To keep your Homey fast and prevent unnecessary internet traffic, always download your calendar feed **once** with a generous timeframe, and then extract all your desired views from that single download.

A great choice for the loader is the **Previous, current and next month** option. This single card gives you a complete three-month window of events.

From this one download, you can immediately run several conversion cards side by side in the same flow:

* Use **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** with format *Today* → send to event topic `homey/event/cal_today`
* Use **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** with format *This week* → send to event topic `homey/event/cal_week`
* Use **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** with format *Next week* → send to event topic `homey/event/cal_next_week`
* Use **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** with format *Month View* → send to event topic `homey/event/cal_month`

All four dashboard views update together from a single network download, giving you great performance and zero redundant work for your Homey.

### Understanding date ranges and common pitfalls

The **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** card can only display appointments that exist inside the data handed to it from the loader. It cannot search the internet for missing dates.

Here is an easy mistake to avoid:

* If you set **Load & filter iCal** to only load **This month**, Homey purposefully discards events from last month.
* If today is the 1st day of the month and you ask the converter for *Yesterday* or *Previous week*, the table will be completely empty. Those days belong to last month, which was not loaded.
* Setting **Load & filter iCal** to **Previous, current and next month** avoids this problem completely. Yesterday, today, upcoming weeks, and next month will all be available. This three-month range is also ideal for users who want to build their own custom Markdown or advanced routines from the generated JSON tag using **Homey Script**.

### Combining multiple family or work calendars

If you have separate calendars for different family members or work schedules, you can easily merge them into a single unified dashboard view.

#### Serial loading (gentle and recommended)

Load one calendar at a time in sequence: Load calendar A → Load calendar B → combine them with **Combine calendar events** → convert the combined result to Markdown. If you have three or more feeds, simply combine each new load into the previous combined token. This gentle sequence keeps Homey memory and CPU usage low and smooth.

![content: Serial iCal loading flow in Homey](help/images/flowcards_serial_ical.jpg)

#### Parallel loading

You can also start multiple **Load & filter iCal** branches simultaneously. Use Homey's built-in **All** card so the flow waits until every branch has finished, combine the tokens with **Combine calendar events**, and convert to Markdown.

![content: Parallel iCal loading with Combine cards](help/images/flowcards_parallel_ical.jpg)

::: alert warning warning
**Memory and performance:** Personal calendar feeds often contain many years of recurring entries. Fetching several large feeds at the exact same instant can briefly increase memory usage. Whenever possible, prefer the serial pattern or the single broad download pattern described above.
:::

### Do not hammer calendar downloads (rate limits and etiquette)

Downloading calendar feeds over the internet takes several seconds, and running download requests too often can cause major issues:

* **Never trigger downloads on button taps or page navigation:** Do not run the **Load & filter iCal** card every time a user taps a dashboard button or navigates to a calendar page. Downloading remote feeds is slow, which creates an annoying delay on the screen. Even worse, hammering calendar hosts with frequent download requests will trigger automatic rate limits, causing Google, Apple, or Microsoft to temporarily ban your Homey from accessing your calendar feed.
* **Use a regular hourly schedule:** The most logical approach is to run your download flow on a steady schedule, such as once every **15 to 60 minutes**. Calendars do not change from second to second, so an hourly schedule keeps your dashboard accurate with zero risk of bans.
* **Fast on-demand view switching with Homey Logic variables:** If you have an interactive dashboard where a user taps buttons to switch between different views (for example switching a single Text widget between *Today*, *This week*, and *This month*), do not download the feed when the button is tapped. Instead, download the calendar feed on an hourly timer and store the **Filtered Events (JSON)** tag in a Homey Logic text variable. When the user taps a button, a fast flow simply takes that stored variable, runs **Convert iCal JSON to Markdown** for the requested view, and sends the Markdown to the Text widget. The view switches instantly with zero download delay and zero external web requests.

If you want to build custom formatting scripts using **Homey Script**, see [Data Types & Formats → Load & Filter iCal JSON](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/load-filter-ical) for technical details on every available JSON field.

**Related:** [Text widget](help://Widgets/text) for Markdown details · [Markdown Formatting Reference](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting)

widgetSubpages.title: RSS Feeds
widgetSubpages.content: ::: lead Fetch live news headlines and blog articles directly into Dashboard Studio with zero scripting. The **Fetch RSS Feed to Markdown** flow card downloads one or more RSS or Atom feeds, automatically sorts articles chronologically, and renders a clean Markdown table ready for your Text widgets. [badge: Homey Pro] ::: ![content: RSS Feeds](help/images/rss_feeds.jpg) ### What is an RSS or Atom feed? An RSS or Atom feed is a standardized web address that publishes new articles, blog posts, or breaking news in a structured XML format. News outlets, tech blogs, weather agencies, and community forums provide these feeds freely so other apps can read summaries without loading the entire website. Dashboard Studio downloads your favorite feeds directly on your Homey, extracts the latest headlines and thumbnails, and formats them into a responsive Markdown table styled to match your dashboard theme. ### Polite streaming and caching Fetching news feeds over the internet requires care to keep your Homey responsive and prevent news servers from rate-limiting your home IP address: * **Early-abort streaming:** The card reads incoming XML data in small chunks. As soon as your configured article limit is satisfied, the connection is closed immediately to save memory and network bandwidth. * **5-minute in-memory cache:** Feeds are cached in memory for five minutes. If several wall tablets open at the same time, Homey delivers the cached table instantly with zero extra web requests. * **Proportional image scaling:** When thumbnails are included, height scales automatically from original proportions to prevent distorted or stretched images. ### Card settings and parameters * **RSS / Atom URL(s):** Paste your feed address. For multiple feeds, put each URL on its own line. You can optionally add custom labels, icons, and chip colors using pipe characters. * **Layout:** Choose your desired visual density: * **Standard:** Headline with a clean summary and published time (Default). * **Full with Images:** Includes thumbnail previews, headlines, summaries, and time. * **Compact:** Single-line rows with headline and time (no summary). * **Headlines Only:** Ultra-dense list of titles without dates or summaries. * **Preview Image Width:** Optional pixel width for preview thumbnails in Full layout (default `180` px). Height scales proportionally from the original picture. * **Max Articles:** Maximum number of rows to display (default `10`, maximum `50`). * **Date Format:** Inherits your global date format from app settings by default, or you can force relative wording (Today/Yesterday), explicit date and time, time only, or hide the date column. * **Dashboard Topic (Optional):** Type a topic name such as `rssfeed`. When entered, the card automatically sends the Markdown directly to `homey/event/rssfeed` on your dashboard, giving you a complete 1-card setup. ### Multi-feed styling and pipe syntax When displaying news from multiple sources in a single widget, you can style each feed individually. On each line, separate properties with pipe symbols (`|`): ::: code-block Multi-Feed Pipe Format URL | Custom Label | ph-icon | Color ::: The order of label, icon, and color is completely flexible and all are optional: * **Icon:** Any Phosphor icon starting with `ph-` (for example `ph-newspaper`, `ph-broadcast`, or `ph-cpu`). Use `none` if you wish to omit the icon entirely. * **Badge Color:** Theme token (such as `@markerTint1` or `@primary`) or a fixed hex color (such as `#23212F` or `#E11D48`). * **Source Label:** Any text token that is not a URL, icon, or color becomes the custom label on the source badge. #### Examples: ::: code-block https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/rss.xml | BBC News | ph-newspaper | @markerTint1 https://feeds.nos.nl/nosnieuwsalgemeen | #23212F | ph-broadcast | NOS https://tweakers.net/feeds/nieuws.xml | ph-cpu ::: When multiple feeds are provided, Dashboard Studio combines all articles, sorts them newest first, and automatically displays a **Source** column with your colored badges. ### Popular feeds Here is a collection of tested news, community, and technology feeds that you can copy directly into your flow card: | Source / Company | Ready-to-Use Feed Configuration (URL \| Label \| Icon) | | :--- | :--- | | :ph-chats: **Homey Community Forum** (Latest Topics) | https://community.homey.app/latest.rss \| Homey Forum \| ph-chats | | :ph-newspaper: **BBC News** (World News) | https://feeds.bbci.co.uk/news/world/rss.xml \| BBC News \| ph-newspaper | | :ph-broadcast: **CNN** (Top Stories) | http://rss.cnn.com/rss/edition.rss \| CNN \| ph-broadcast | | :ph-newspaper: **The Guardian** (World News) | https://www.theguardian.com/world/rss \| The Guardian \| ph-newspaper | | :ph-newspaper: **The New York Times** (World News) | https://rss.nytimes.com/services/xml/rss/nyt/World.xml \| NY Times \| ph-newspaper | | :ph-globe: **Al Jazeera** (English News) | https://www.aljazeera.com/xml/rss/all.xml \| Al Jazeera \| ph-globe | | :ph-broadcast: **Deutsche Welle** (English News) | https://rss.dw.com/rdf/rss-en-all \| DW News \| ph-broadcast | | :ph-radio: **NPR** (Headlines) | https://feeds.npr.org/1001/rss.xml \| NPR \| ph-radio | | :ph-cpu: **TechCrunch** (Technology) | https://techcrunch.com/feed/ \| TechCrunch \| ph-cpu | | :ph-laptop: **The Verge** (Technology & Science) | https://www.theverge.com/rss/index.xml \| The Verge \| ph-laptop | | :ph-circuitry: **Ars Technica** (Technology) | https://feeds.arstechnica.com/arstechnica/index \| Ars Technica \| ph-circuitry | | :ph-lightning: **Wired** (Top Stories) | https://www.wired.com/feed/rss \| Wired \| ph-lightning | | :ph-rocket: **NASA** (News Releases) | https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/feed/ \| NASA \| ph-rocket | ### Flow tokens (Drop tags) If you prefer to route data manually, update Homey logic variables, or trigger push notifications, the card provides these flow tags: * **Markdown:** The complete rendered Markdown table string. * **Article Count:** Total number of articles returned. * **Latest Headline:** The title of the newest article. * **Latest Link:** Web link to the newest article. * **Latest Summary:** Plain-text summary or excerpt of the newest article (HTML tags, entities, and URLs removed). * **Latest Image URL:** Image or thumbnail web address of the newest article. ### Displaying on your dashboard 1. Add a **Text** widget to your canvas. 2. In widget settings, open **Text Settings** and locate **Text Content**. 3. Click the chain link icon next to **Text Content** to make it dynamic, and enter your event topic (for example `rssfeed`). 4. In **Text Settings**, enable **Scroll Overflow Content** and set **Vertical Alignment** to **Top**. Because an RSS feed contains multiple articles and summaries, it usually exceeds the height of a fixed text widget. Enabling scroll overflow lets you comfortably scroll through all stories, and aligning to the top ensures your newest headlines start at the top of the frame instead of centering vertically. *(Note: If your dashboard uses **Responsive Columns** layout mode with **Auto** cell height, the widget grows to fit the entire table automatically).* 5. Expand **Markdown** to pick your favorite **Table Style** (such as **Solid Header**, **Classic**, or **Card Rows**). 6. Set **Table Column Width Mode** to **Equal Table Column Widths** for balanced layout. ::: alert info text-aa **Headline and excerpt spacing** Headlines use **Header 3** (`###`). If you want to tighten the spacing between the headline and the summary text, open **Text & Typography** in the Text widget, select **Header 3**, and set **Vertical Spacing (px)** to around `-15`. ::: **Related:** [Text widget](help://Widgets/text) · [Markdown Formatting Reference](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/markdown-formatting) · [Connecting Widgets & Data (Topics)](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#binding-in-the-editor)

widgetSubpages.title: Layering Widgets
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
Dashboard Studio's free-form canvas allows you to stack widgets on top of each other to create entirely new, complex controls.
:::

For example, placing a functional volume slider directly over a circular media gauge.

1. Place your base widget (e.g., the Gauge) on the canvas.
2. Add your second widget (e.g., the Slider) and drag it over the first.
3. **The Trick:** To make it look like a single seamless UI element, select the top widget (the Slider) and uncheck **Show Container**.

This hides the top widget box, leaving only its interactive track and thumb visible floating above your base widget. For a combined control that should scale on phones, use **Group** with **Scale Mode** **Rescale** in [Responsive Columns](help://Layout%20Modes#help-responsive-columns).

widgetSubpages.title: Live Camera Feeds
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
Dashboard Studio has no built-in video stream player. To show a camera, you use a normal still snapshot URL that your camera can regularly produce.
:::

This is often a single JPEG refreshed over and over.

#### 1. Check your camera manual

Look for a **snapshot**, **still image**, or **JPEG URL** (sometimes under HTTP API or ONVIF). You need one fixed address that returns a fresh picture each time it is requested.

#### 2. Image widget + Live Refresh

Add an **Image** widget, set **Source Type** to **URL** in **Data & Source**, and paste the snapshot address into **URL**. Enable **Enable Live Refresh** and set **Refresh Interval** (for example every 1 to 3 seconds). The dashboard reloads the snapshot on that interval so the picture stays roughly up to date.

#### 3. When refresh pauses

If the widget is **not visible** (hidden or assigned to another page than the one you are viewing), it **skips load new snapshots**. Nothing is fetched until it is shown again. That saves load on your camera and network when nobody is looking at that tile.

#### 4. Login in the URL

Some cameras allow `http://username:password@192.168.x.x/…/snapshot.jpg`. That often works in **Firefox**. **Chrome** and **Edge** frequently block username and password inside the address for security, so the same URL may fail there. A **browser extension** that adds HTTP authentication for local addresses can be a workaround. Check your browser’s extension store and use a well-reviewed one.

widgetSubpages.title: Dynamic Colors
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
You can dynamically change any color property on your dashboard based on Homey logic [badge: Homey Pro].
:::

A great use case is turning a thermostat icon red when the heater is actively heating, and green when it is idle. [badge: Homey Pro]

#### 1. The Homey Flow [badge: Homey Pro]

Create a flow that compares the current temperature with your target temperature. Depending on the outcome, send a specific color value to Dashboard Studio.

![content: Thermostat Color Flow](help/images/thermostat_color_flow.jpg)

* **Event Name:** Invent a unique name, such as `ThermostatColor`. Make sure not to reuse this name for other functions.
* **Value:** Use a standard CSS Hex color code (e.g., `#F54927` for red, `#0BB00B` for green). You can easily find these codes using a [Hex Color Picker](https://htmlcolorcodes.com/color-picker/ ^).

#### 2. Binding the Color

Once you trigger the flow, the color data is sent to the dashboard.

1. **Optional Verification:** Open the **Data Stream Explorer** in ⚙️ Dashboard Settings. You should see `homey/event/ThermostatColor` pop up with your hex value.
2. Select your widget (like an Icon or Gauge) and locate the color property you want to change (e.g., "Icon Color").
3. Click the **Link Icon** :ph-bold ph-link text-cyan-400: to enable binding.
4. Fill in your topic name. *Pro Tip:* You can paste the full path (`homey/event/ThermostatColor`) from the Explorer, or simply type your custom name (`ThermostatColor`). The dashboard automatically understands both!

For color formats see [Data Types & Formats](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats#quick-reference-basic-types). For fallbacks, formulas, and **Color Adjustments**, see [Binding Options](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas#color-fields-color-adjustments).

widgetSubpages.title: Weather Widget using AI [badge: Homey Pro]
RSS News Reader [badge: Homey Pro]
Confirmation Dialogs
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
Create a custom confirmation dialog to prevent accidental triggers. This step-by-step guide explains how to show a dialog when a button is pressed and hide it based on your choice.
:::

::: alert info warning
**Built-in Confirmation Dialog**

For a simple Yes/No prompt, select the [Switch / Button](help://Widgets/switch#3-confirmation-dialog), turn on **Require Confirmation**, and style **Confirmation Dialog Appearance**. Shared defaults live in [Dialog Box](help://Widgets/dialog-box). Use the custom teleport recipe below when you need a fully designed overlay of your own widgets.
:::

[See a confirmation dialog example on the demo dashboard](?dashboard=demo&page=13) [muted: (demo, page 13)]

### 1. Configure the Main Button
We want the button to activate different parts. When turned on, it should activate the dialog. When turned off, it should directly deactivate the device.

* In the **Data & Behavior** section, set the mode to **Toggle Switch**. 
* Enable **Separate On and Off Topics** to be able to send different topics based on the state of the button.
* Set the **On Output Topic** to `local/laserWarning` (read about [Global vs. Local Topics](help://Connecting%20Widgets%20%26%20Data%20%28Topics%29#global-vs-local-topics) for more information). Set the **On Value** to your main page number (for example `1`). This teleports the dialog to your current page.
* Set the **Off Output Topic** to your device topic you want to deactivate (for example `Laser`). Set the **Off Value** to `false`.
* When the button is pressed, it goes to an "enabled" state, but if the user chooses "no" in the dialog, this should also deactivate the button again. To make the state dynamic, click the **Link Icon** :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400: next to the **State** setting and bind it to `local/buttonState`.
![content: Widget Layering](help/images/tip_warning_dialog_01.jpg)
::: alert info warning
**Hardcoded Page Numbers:** 

If you use specific page numbers like `1` or `2` for teleportation, you will need to update these values manually if you ever reorder your dashboard pages.
:::

### 2. Design the Dialog
Navigate to an unused page in your dashboard. This is where we are going to create the dialog and group it. Groups have the ability to teleport to a different page and show as a modal with a blurred background.

* Add a Container widget to serve as the background outline.
* Add a Text widget with your warning message (for example "Are you sure you want to activate the death laser?").
* Add two Button widgets below the text. 
* In the **Appearance** section for both buttons, set the **Visual Style** to **Button (Rect)** and in the **Data & Behavior** section the mode to **Push Button**.

### 3. Configure the YES Button
This button will activate the device and hide the dialog.

* Set the text to **YES!**.
* Set the **Output Topic** to `Laser` and the **On Value** to `true`.
* We also want this button to automatically hide the dialog when pressing the YES! button. We can do this by sending the dialog group back to the page it came from. Click **+ Add Output Topic**. Set this new topic to `local/laserWarning` and the **On Value** to the unused page number where you are building the dialog (for example `2`).

### 4. Configure the NO Button
This button has to hide the dialog and turn the activation switch to off.

* Set the text to **No**.
* Set the **Output Topic** to `local/buttonState` and the **On Value** to `false`. This will set the activation button back to off.
* Click **+ Add Output Topic**. Set this new topic to `local/laserWarning` and the **On Value** to the hidden page number (for example `2`). This will hide the dialog again after pressing No.

### 5. Group and Teleport
![content: Widget Layering](help/images/tip_warning_dialog_02.jpg)
* Select all the items needed for the dialog (container, text, and both buttons). 
* Click the **Group** button in the editor sidebar. This will create a group of the dialog.
* Select the newly created group.
* Click the **Link Icon** :ph-bold ph-link text-slate-400: next to the **Override Page(s)** setting to bind it to the topic `local/laserWarning`. Now the buttons teleport this page to other pages.
* The last step is to enable **Blur Background When Visible**. This will make the dialog modal and blur everything in the background.

widgetSubpages.title: Kiosk Display
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
If you are running Dashboard Studio on a dedicated wall-mounted tablet or kiosk, use the viewer for a light, editor-free session.
:::

You can open a dashboard in two ways:

* **Editor:** Keep the gear panel for designing. Bookmark `/editor.html` when you want the full designer.
* **Viewer URL:** In the editor, use **Viewer URL** to open or copy the view-only link. That page is `/viewer.html`. See [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters#7-dashboard-viewer-kiosk-mode) and the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide).

On Homey Pro, enable **Viewer mode only** in the Homey App Settings. Opening the main dashboard link then loads the lightweight **Dashboard Viewer** instead of the editor. Design work still uses `/editor.html`.

You can also open the viewer directly with your dashboard name as a parameter:

::: code-block Example
http://192.168.1.50:5050/viewer.html?dashboard=tablet
:::

See [Homey: The Complete Guide](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide#help-step-10) Step 9 for the same kiosk path in the beginner walkthrough.

widgetSubpages.title: Direct Events (The THEN Card Trick)
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
You do not always need to create Homey variables [badge: Homey Pro] to change widget visibility or other dynamic settings.
:::

There is a more direct way by using the Dashboard Studio's **THEN** flow card.

1. Use the **Dashboard Studio THEN** card in your flow.
2. Just invent a unique **Event Name** (for example, `ShowAlert`) and set the value to `true` or `false`.
3. In the Dashboard Studio editor, click the chainlink icon on a setting (like Visibility) to make it dynamic.
4. Type in your custom event name (`ShowAlert`) in the topic field.

You can now control the state of that widget directly from a flow without cluttering your Homey with extra variables!

widgetSubpages.title: Teleporting Groups (Dialog Overlays)
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
When you have a ton of layered groups stacked on top of each other that hide and show based on dynamic values, editing them can become a huge pain. You can solve this by "teleporting" groups from one page to another.
:::

This trick keeps your main dashboard page clean while still allowing complex dialog overlays.

#### 1. Create the Dialog on a Separate Page
Design your popup dialog (a container, some text, buttons) on an entirely different, hidden page (for example, Page 3) so it skips clutter your main view.

#### 2. Group the Dialog
Select all the dialog widgets and **Group** them together.

#### 3. Use the Override Page Setting
In the Group's settings, locate the **Override Page(s)** option. Click the chainlink icon to make it dynamic, and link it to a local topic (e.g., `local/dialogPage`).

#### 4. Trigger the Teleport
Create a button on your main page. Set its **Action Type** to `Send Topic`, and output to `local/dialogPage`. Set the button's ON value to your main page number (e.g., `1`), and its OFF value back to the hidden page (e.g., `3`). 

When you press the button, the dialog is instantly "teleported" to your current page, and closing it sends it back to the hidden page!

widgetSubpages.title: Auto-Hiding Controls [badge: Homey Pro]
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
You can create controls like pop-up sliders that automatically hide themselves a few seconds after you interact with them.
:::

#### 1. Setup the UI
1. Add a **Switch** widget configured as `Image Only` to act as your trigger button.
2. Add a **Slider** widget that will pop up. Make its **Visibility** dynamic and link it to a topic like `sliderVisible`.
3. Link the Switch's **State (On/Off)** to the same `sliderVisible` topic. Also set the Switch's **Output Topic** to `sliderVisible`.

#### 2. Broadcast to Homey
Make sure you use a global topic (like `sliderVisible` instead of `local/sliderVisible`) so Homey can see when it is opened. Also set the Slider's **Output Topic** to something like `sliderValue` so Homey knows when the slider is moved.

#### 3. The Auto-Hide Flow
Create a flow in Homey that triggers when `sliderValue` changes. Add a delay (e.g., wait 5 seconds), and then use a Dashboard Studio THEN card to send `false` to the `sliderVisible` topic.

Now, when you tap the icon, the slider appears. You adjust the value, and 5 seconds later, it seamlessly vanishes and resets the trigger button!

widgetSubpages.title: External Web Images (Rain Radar)
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
You can display live external images from the internet, such as a rain radar or weather map, directly on your dashboard.
:::

Instead of scraping websites, find a direct image API URL. For example, Buienradar provides a direct map image: `https://api.buienradar.nl/image/1.0/RadarMapNL?w=720&h=600`.

1. Add an **Image** widget to your dashboard.
2. Set the **Source Type** to `URL` and paste the API link.
3. Enable **Live Refresh**.
4. Set the **Refresh Interval** to something reasonable for weather data (for example, every `10` minutes).

This keeps your dashboard professional and avoids the cluttered look of embedding full website iframes.

widgetSubpages.title: Timed Countdown Button [badge: Homey Pro]
widgetSubpages.content:
::: lead
Create a push button that starts a timed countdown, disables itself to prevent repeated clicks while active, displays the remaining time directly on the button label, and automatically resets when the timer finishes.
:::

Dashboard Studio communicates with Homey using topics. Because Dashboard Studio focuses on rapid interface design and live rendering, timing logic belongs in Homey. Homey manages the countdown transition, while Dashboard Studio handles the dynamic display, label text, button deactivation, and visual state in real time.

#### 1. Create and Configure the Button

First, place a button widget on your canvas.

![content: Reset Canvas](help/images/tip_timer_button_01.jpg)

If you are starting from a blank setup, reset the canvas and click **Skip Wizard** to open the canvas editor.

1. Click **Create Widget** and choose **Switch / Button**.
2. Select a push button style preset, such as **Button Label Inside**.

![content: Create Switch Button](help/images/tip_timer_button_02.jpg)

![content: Select Button Preset](help/images/tip_timer_button_03.jpg)

3. Open the **Data & Behavior** section in the inspector.
4. Ensure **Mode** is set to **Toggle Switch** (default).
5. In the **Output Topic** field, type a unique topic name without spaces, such as `Enable_Climate_Control`.

![content: Configure Output Topic](help/images/tip_timer_button_04.jpg)

Whenever you click the button, Dashboard Studio sends `true` (or `false`) to Homey on this topic.

#### 2. Create the Homey Advanced Flows [badge: Homey Pro]

To run a countdown that emits the remaining seconds every second, install a transition app in Homey such as [Chronograph](https://homey.app/nl-nl/app/nl.fellownet.chronograph/Chronograph/).

##### Flow 1: Start the Transition Timer

Create an Advanced Flow to start the countdown when the button is pressed:

1. Add a **Dashboard Studio Trigger** card listening to topic `Enable_Climate_Control`.
2. Connect it to a Homey Logic **is equal to 'yes'** card so the timer only starts on button activation (`true`).
3. Connect that card to a Chronograph **Start or replace transition** card.
4. Name the transition (for example `Climate_Control_Timer`).
5. For a 10-minute timer, configure from `600` to `0` in `601` steps over `10` minutes. This triggers one update every second.

![content: Homey Flow Timer Transition](help/images/tip_timer_button_05.jpg)

##### Flow 2: Send Remaining Seconds to the Dashboard

Next, send each second tick back to Dashboard Studio:

1. Add the Chronograph card **Transition has reached a step** with transition name `Climate_Control_Timer`.
2. Connect it to a Dashboard Studio **Send with value to Dashboard** action card.
3. In **Topic**, enter a new topic name such as `TimerTime`.
4. In **Value**, assign the **Transition value** tag from the Chronograph trigger card.

![content: Homey Flow Send Timer Value](help/images/tip_timer_button_06.jpg)

#### 3. Display the Countdown

Once Homey sends the remaining seconds on topic `TimerTime`, you can display the value in several ways.

##### Option A: Text or Label Widget

Add a [Label](help://Widgets/label) widget to the canvas. In **Text Settings**, click the chain link icon next to **Text** to make it dynamic, and enter `TimerTime`.

![content: Dynamic Text Binding](help/images/tip_timer_button_07.jpg)

##### Option B: Progress Gauge

Add a [Gauge](help://Widgets/gauge) widget using the **Horizontal / Icon Left** preset. In **Data & Behavior**, set **Min** to `600` and **Max** to `0`, then make **Value** dynamic and link it to topic `TimerTime`.

![content: Dynamic Gauge Value](help/images/tip_timer_button_08.jpg)

Because the minimum is set higher than the maximum, the gauge bar reverses and fills up over time as the seconds count down to 0. If you prefer the bar to empty instead, set **Min** to `0` and **Max** to `600`.

##### Option C: Directly on the Button Label

The cleanest setup displays the countdown directly inside the button text.

1. Select your button widget and expand the **Text & Typography** section.
2. Click the chain link icon next to **Button Label** and link it to `TimerTime`.
3. Click the formula icon (the slider icon next to the chain link) to open the [Payload Formula](help://Data%20Types%20%26%20Formats/binding-options-formulas) dialog.

![content: Button Label Formula Dialog](help/images/tip_timer_button_09.jpg)

To combine the label text with the remaining seconds, enter:

::: code-block
"Climate Control (" + value + "s)"
:::

To hide the seconds when the countdown reaches zero:

::: code-block
"Climate Control" + if(value > 0, " (" + value + "s)", "")
:::

To format the seconds into minutes and seconds (for example `2m27s`):

::: code-block
"Climate Control" + if(value > 0, " (" + round((value / 60) - 0.5) + "m" + (value - (round((value / 60) - 0.5) * 60)) + "s)", "")
:::

![content: Button Label Formatted Countdown](help/images/tip_timer_button_10.jpg)

#### 4. Disable the Button During the Timeout

To prevent users from clicking the button while the timer is running, disable interaction during the countdown.

1. With the button widget selected, locate the **Deactivated** toggle in the inspector.
2. Click the chain link icon to make **Deactivated** dynamic and enter `TimerTime`.
3. Click the formula icon and enter:

::: code-block
if(value > 0, 1, 0)
:::

When the timer has remaining seconds (`value > 0`), the formula evaluates to `1` (true), which locks the button. When it reaches `0`, it evaluates to `0` (false), unlocking the button.

![content: Deactivated Button Formula](help/images/tip_timer_button_11.jpg)

To clearly show when the button is locked, set **Deactivated Color** in the **Appearance** section to an active tint such as red or orange.

#### 5. Reset Button State on Expiration

When the countdown ends, the visual state of the switch must turn off so it is ready for the next press.

1. Expand the **Data & Behavior** section.
2. Click the chain link icon next to **State (on/off)** and bind it to `TimerTime`.
3. Add the same formula:

::: code-block
if(value > 0, 1, 0)
:::

![content: Dynamic Button State Formula](help/images/tip_timer_button_12.jpg)

While the countdown is active, the button state stays on (`1`). As soon as the timer reaches `0`, the button automatically turns off (`0`).

#### Bonus: Adding an Active Glow Outline

Disabled widgets do not render a button glow. If you want a glowing halo while the timer is active, place a [Container](help://Widgets/container) widget directly behind your button:

1. Enable **Glow** on the container and pick your glow color (e.g. red for heating, blue for cooling).
2. Make the container **Visibility** setting dynamic, link it to `TimerTime`, and assign the formula `if(value > 0, 1, 0)`.

topics.title: Advanced URL Parameters
topics.content:
![header: URL Parameters](help/images/header_urls.jpg)

::: lead
Dashboard Studio runs as a local web app hosted directly on your Homey. By appending URL query parameters to the web address, you can launch specific dashboard configurations, open chosen pages, apply themes, or lock wall displays into lightweight kiosk mode.
:::

### Where to find your dashboard URL

When Dashboard Studio is installed on your Homey Pro [badge: Homey Pro], it serves your dashboards over your local home network.

To find your base address:

1. Open the **Homey App** on your phone or computer.
2. Navigate to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings**.
3. Under **Open your local dashboard:**, you will find your primary local web link. The address looks like `http://[local IP]:5050/` (for example `http://192.168.1.50:5050/`).

![content: Local dashboard URL in Homey Settings](help/images/homey_local_dashboard_url.jpg)

You can click this link directly from Homey Settings, or copy it to create browser bookmarks on any device. Homey also provides a **Local Dashboard URL** tag for automated flows.

### Editor Mode vs. Viewer Mode (Kiosk Mode)

::: p #7-dashboard-viewer-kiosk-mode
Dashboard Studio provides two distinct operating modes depending on what you want to do:
:::

* **Editor (`/` or `/editor.html`):** The full design studio with toolbars, the widget palette, and the inspector sidebar. Use this on your desktop or laptop when building and styling dashboards.
* **Viewer (`/viewer.html`):** The lightweight, display-only mode for wall tablets and kiosks. It strips away all editor toolbars, menus, and inspector panels to reduce memory and battery usage.

In the editor toolbar, you can see and copy your direct **Viewer URL** under the dashboard controls:

![content: Reset Canvas and Viewer URL in the editor](help/images/homey_reset_canvas.jpg)

Click the **Viewer URL** icon to open the clean display view in a new tab, or use the attached copy button to copy the exact link. 

If you are setting up a dedicated wall tablet or kiosk where users should not access the editor, enable **Viewer mode only** in the Homey App Settings. The main dashboard link (`/`) then automatically redirects to the lightweight viewer. 

For mounting and fullscreen tips, see [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display) and the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#3-viewer-url-dashboard-files).

### How query parameters work

Query parameters let you pass instructions to Dashboard Studio inside the web address itself. Both the Editor and Viewer accept the exact same query parameters.

To add parameters, append a question mark `?` to the end of the URL, followed by the parameter name, an equals sign `=`, and your desired value. To combine multiple parameters, separate them with an ampersand `&`.

::: code-block Example
http://192.168.1.50:5050/viewer.html?dashboard=tablet&page=2
:::

### 1. Load Dashboard (`dashboard` or `cfg`)

Loads a specific dashboard JSON configuration file from Homey storage (`dashboards/` folder).

* `?dashboard=tablet` → Loads `dashboards/tablet.json`
* `?dashboard=mobile` → Loads `dashboards/mobile.json`
* `?dashboard=demo` → Loads the built-in factory demo layout

This is useful for creating separate dashboards for different rooms or screen sizes, such as a compact layout for phones and a dense grid for wall tablets.

### 2. Jump to Page (`page`)

Opens the dashboard on a specific page number as soon as it loads. This also opens that page when **Enable Startup Landing Page & Inactivity Return** is on.

* `?page=2` → Opens Page 2 immediately.
* `?page=4` → Opens Page 4 immediately.

Combine this with the viewer URL to bookmark specific rooms or sub-panels on different tablets around your home.

### 3. Apply Theme (`theme`)

Applies a specific visual theme when the dashboard loads.

* `?theme=Clean Slate` → Applies the Clean Slate theme.
* `?theme=Default Dark` → Applies the Default Dark theme.

### 4. Security Token (`token`)

Authenticates your session when the **Require Security Token** setting is enabled in Homey App Settings.

* `?token=mysecret` → Authenticates the session with the token 'mysecret'.

When token protection is active, requests without the valid token parameter are blocked. See [Security & Remote Access](help://Security%20%26%20Remote%20Access#1-the-security-token) for setup instructions.

### 5. Combining Parameters

You can mix and match any of the parameters above using the `&` symbol. This allows you to build targeted, device-specific launch links.

::: code-block Example
http://192.168.1.50:5050/viewer.html?dashboard=mobile&theme=Clean Slate&page=2&token=mysecret
:::

![content: Browser URL Bar](help/images/url_browser.jpg)

### 6. Editor loads & the address bar

When you load or import a dashboard through the editor, the app may **normalize or strip** redundant query parameters from the browser address bar to keep the URL clean. Your chosen dashboard, page, and theme still apply. Refresh the page if you intentionally pasted a long query string and need to re-verify it.

topics.title: Security & Remote Access
topics.content:
![header: Security Settings](help/images/header_security.jpg)

::: lead
Dashboard Studio runs directly on your local network. This page explains how to protect it with a Security Token and how to think about remote access. [badge: Homey Pro]
:::

### 1. The Security Token

The Security Token acts like a password for your dashboard. Instead of a login screen, the token is included directly in the URL, so you can save it as a bookmark and the dashboard opens instantly, without ever needing to type anything.

::: alert info info
**Why a URL token?** 

This is the right balance between convenience and security. Many dashboards run on wall-mounted tablets without a keyboard attached. If the tablet reboots after a power cut or a Wi-Fi drop, the dashboard should just come back on its own, nobody wants to hunt for a keyboard just to log in again. The token-in-URL makes this seamless.
:::

#### Setting it up

1. Open the **Homey App** on your smartphone.
2. Go to **Settings → Dashboard Studio → Settings tab**.
3. Toggle on **Require Security Token**.
4. Enter a custom **Security Token** (for example, a strong passphrase), or click **Generate Random** to create a secure, URL-friendly token.
5. Click **Save Settings**.

Once saved, any request without the correct token is blocked server-side on Homey, meaning the dashboard page itself is never served to unauthorized clients and none of your connected Homey devices can be read or controlled. This matters because the protection cannot be bypassed by simply opening the browser's developer tools or stripping the URL. 

As an additional layer, the server also enforces your device configuration: only the specific device capabilities you have enabled in the App Settings can be controlled, ensuring that the rest of your devices and capabilities remain fully out of reach at all times. For example, your full dashboard URL will look like this:

::: code-block
http://192.168.1.50:5050/?token=YOUR_TOKEN
:::
*(Note: This is an example. You can always find your correct personal URL in the Dashboard Studio configuration settings in the Homey app.)*

Save this URL as a bookmark or add it to the Home Screen on your tablet. It will open the dashboard directly every time, without any login prompt.


### 2. The Personal API Key [badge: Homey Pro]

Dashboard Studio can write directly to Homey User Variables, start your Standard and Advanced Flows, and activate zone Moods without needing intermediate flow cards. Because Athom restricts third-party app tokens from modifying variables, starting flows, or setting moods, this functionality requires your owner authorization through a Personal API Key.

#### Why Homey Requires This Key

Athom designed Homey with a strict security boundary between apps and system logic. When an app installs on your Homey, it receives a scoped app token. That token is granted read-only rights for variables and flows, but write actions are blocked by the operating system.

A **Personal API Key** is created by you as the administrator in the Homey Web App. Because it is tied to your account rather than the app, it possesses the required administrative scopes (`homey.logic`, `homey.flow`, and `homey.mood`). When saved in Dashboard Studio, the app uses your key to communicate locally with Homey's internal API over your home network.

#### How It Is Stored and Validated

* **Local verification**: When you enter the key in the **Settings** tab and leave the field, Dashboard Studio verifies it locally against your Homey. Active permission badges display for Variables, Flows, and Moods. If the key is rejected, an **Invalid Key** badge appears and the key is marked as unused.
* **Flows and Moods Integration**: Flows expose both a start capability to run the flow and a read capability to inspect enabled status. Moods appear grouped inside the active zone where they belong, allowing you to trigger scene presets with a single tap.
* **Isolated and private**: Your Personal API Key is saved directly in Homey's private app settings storage. It is never transmitted across the network, never sent to connected dashboard viewer tablets, and never exposed in dashboard save files.
* **Safety cooldowns**: Direct flow executions carry a built-in 10-second cooldown per flow, and moods carry a 3-second cooldown per mood, preventing accidental rapid repeats from overloading Homey.

### 3. Remote Access via Port Forwarding

To reach your dashboard from outside your home network, you need to open a port on your internet router.

1. Log in to your **internet router** (often via `192.168.1.1` or `10.0.0.1`).
2. Find the **Port Forwarding** (or NAT/Gaming) section.
3. Create a new rule with these settings:

**External Port:** `5050` (or any port you prefer, for example `8080` or `8888`)
**Internal IP:** The local IP address of your Homey Pro (for example `192.168.1.50`)
**Internal Port:** `5050` (or the Dashboard Port you configured in Settings)
**Protocol:** TCP

Your external URL will then look like this:

::: code-block
http://[YOUR_PUBLIC_IP]:5050/?token=YOUR_TOKEN
:::

::: alert warning warning-circle
**A note on HTTP security** 

A direct connection to a home IP is unencrypted (HTTP). If you expose a port to the internet, a man-in-the-middle attacker could theoretically read the token from the plain-text URL. In practice, this risk is low for home networks, but if you want absolute security when accessing from outside your home, consider using a **VPN instead of port forwarding**.
:::

### 4. The Recommended Approach

* **Inside your home:** Use the local URL. A Security Token is optional for local access and only necessary if you also wish to reach your dashboard securely from the outside. Bookmark it. Done.
* **Outside your home (practical):** Port forwarding + Security Token is sufficient for most users.
* **Outside your home (maximum security):** Use a **VPN** (e.g., WireGuard, Tailscale, or your router's built-in VPN) to connect back to your home network, then access the dashboard via its local URL with your Security Token. No port forwarding required.

topics.title: Troubleshooting
topics.content:
![header: Troubleshooting](help/images/header_troubleshoot.jpg)

::: lead
If you are experiencing issues with widgets updating, data failing to connect, memory issues, or display problems, consult this guide to resolve the most common configuration errors.
:::

### Page Index

* [My widget isn't updating!](#my-widget-isnt-updating)
* [I opened the dashboard but only see the viewer (Kiosk Mode)](#i-opened-the-dashboard-but-only-see-the-viewer-kiosk-mode)
* [I can't see the Save, Load, or Gallery buttons](#i-cant-see-the-save-load-or-gallery-buttons)
* [It does not work on my iOS 12 iPad relic](#it-does-not-work-on-my-ios-12-ipad-relic)
* [The Homey App is crashing or restarting](#the-homey-app-is-crashing-or-restarting)

---

### My widget isn't updating!

1. Did you **enable the device capability** in the Homey App [badge: Homey Pro] Settings? (See [Step 1](help://Tutorials/homey-complete-guide#help-step-1))
2. Did you copy the **Topic** correctly? Check the **Data Stream Explorer** in **⚙️ Dashboard Settings** to be sure.
3. **Check Case Sensitivity:** Topics are case-sensitive. `myDevice/onoff` is different from `mydevice/onoff`.
4. Right after the driver connects, the dashboard replays the **last known values** it already has so gauges and text widgets can populate immediately. Wait a moment for live updates if the device is quiet.

### I opened the dashboard but only see the viewer (Kiosk Mode)

**Viewer mode only** is on in Homey App [badge: Homey Pro] Settings. The main link opens the lightweight viewer. Design at `/editor.html`, or turn **Viewer mode only** off and refresh. See [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters), [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display), and **Viewer URL** in the [Editor Interface Guide](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#3-viewer-url-dashboard-files).

### I can't see the Save, Load, or Gallery buttons

**Save to Homey**, **Load from Homey**, [Image Gallery](help://Image%20Gallery%20Manager), and [Audio Gallery](help://Audio%20Gallery) rely on Homey storage. They show when **Platform** is **Homey**.

**Solution:** Open **⚙️ Dashboard Settings**, go to the **Platform Connection** section, and set **Platform** to **Homey** [badge: Homey Pro].

### It does not work on my iOS 12 iPad relic

The **Editor** does not support iOS 12. Trying to run the full design suite, drag-and-drop canvas, and modern toolbars on a museum piece running Safari 12 from 2013 will simply make the browser cry and refuse to load. Design your dashboards comfortably on a modern computer, laptop, or contemporary tablet.

The **Viewer** (`/viewer.html`), however, *does* support your steam-driven relic. In the editor, grab your [Viewer URL](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#3-viewer-url-dashboard-files) (or use `/viewer.html?dashboard=yourname`) to give that retired iPad a proud second life as a wall-mounted smart home display. See [Kiosk Display](help://Tips%20%26%20Tricks/kiosk-display) and [Advanced URL Parameters](help://Advanced%20URL%20Parameters) for setup tips.

Be gentle with the vintage hardware though. An ancient A-series processor with 1 GB of shared RAM cannot handle a bloated command center without. If you want a bit of performance on older tablets, avoid these heavy features:

* **Bended and Animated Arrows:** Curved bezier paths with animated flow pulses and glowing outlines melt vintage GPUs. If you need connectors on older screens, keep your [Arrow / Line](help://Widgets/arrow) widgets straight, static, and glow-free.
* **Overloaded Graph Datasets:** A [Graph](help://Widgets/graph) trying to render hundreds of raw historical points and continuous bezier curves will choke old WebKit memory. Keep datasets compact, or show graphs on a separate page.
* **Heavy Shadows, Glows, and Glass Themes:** Multi-layered drop shadows, glowing widget outlines, and translucent blur effects (`backdrop-filter`) take huge computational power. Use flat solid colors and clean borders instead.
* **Rapid-Fire Live Camera Streams:** An [Image](help://Widgets/image) widget polling full-resolution camera snapshots every second will quickly exhaust the browser cache and cause mobile Safari to crash the tab.
* **Chatty High-Frequency MQTT Topics:** Sensors blasting ten updates per second force the browser into endless layout recalculations. Throttle high-speed power meters or update them at sensible intervals.
* **Giant Single-Page Megaboards:** Cramming fifty widgets onto a single screen is asking for trouble. Split controls across multiple dashboard pages using the [Page Navigator](help://Editor%20Interface%20Guide#8-page-navigator-utilities) and simple navigation buttons.

### The Homey App is crashing or restarting

::: lead
If the Dashboard Studio app on Homey crashes, becomes unresponsive, or restarts unexpectedly, excessive memory usage is almost always the cause.
:::

Homey strictly limits the amount of RAM available to any individual application. When Dashboard Studio exceeds its memory threshold, Homey's operating system terminates or restarts the app.

#### Primary Causes:

* **Large or Complex Custom SVGs:** Sending raw SVG vector strings through Flow tokens or MQTT into topics can use enormous amounts of RAM. An unoptimized SVG graphic with thousands of path nodes, embedded base64 images, or heavy filters can easily consume megabytes per payload, quickly choking Homey's memory when cached or broadcast.
* **Massive Markdown Tables & Text Blobs:** Updating large markdown tables or extensive text payloads on short intervals forces the app to repeatedly parse, store, and broadcast heavy strings across all open clients.

#### How to Fix and Keep Payloads Lean:

1. **Optimize SVGs Before Sending:** Strip metadata, run vector graphics through an SVG optimizer (like SVGO), and simplify complex curves or gradients. Keep them as compact and lean as possible in topics.
2. **Use URL Images for Heavy Graphics:** If a graphic is static or very detailed, host or upload it to Homey's **Image Gallery** and reference its URL instead of injecting massive inline SVG strings into live flow topics.
3. **Limit State Caching in Homey App Settings:**
   Open **More → Apps → Dashboard Studio → App Settings** and adjust the **State Caching** setting:
   * **Full (Devices & all events):** Keeps the last known values of all device capabilities and all event topics in memory so dashboards instantly fill upon reload or reconnect.
   * **Optimized (< 16 KB events):** *(Recommended for heavy setups)* Keeps all standard device states and smaller events, but automatically skips caching event strings or payloads larger than 16 KB. This directly protects Homey from running out of memory while still giving you instant dashboard startups for typical devices.
   * **Devices & variables only:** Stores only device capabilities and Homey variables in memory; no custom flow events or MQTT topics are cached.
   * **Disabled (No caching):** Keeps nothing in memory. Dashboards will only populate when fresh live data is broadcast by devices or flows.
